what_it_is: Library of 99 film styles for coding agents, each rendered as a short film made in code.
take: Reading-time rule for on-screen text: hold each line at least max(1.8 s, speech length + 0.6 s).
Style prompts define subtitles as part of the film's world (caption, plate, inscription), not a fixed band.
future_use: Hold times for on-screen text and card reveals in reels.

what_it_is: Starter kit for hand-painted character animation in p5.js, built shot by shot by Claude.
take: Workflow: storyboard first, build shot by shot, render contact sheets to check its own work before writing the MP4.
Keep length and tempo in one config file and shots in one timeline module, so timing changes stay in one place.
future_use: Animated explainer scenes for a non-talking-head format.

what_it_is: Source of a Claude-made music video, with chapter files, a shot-by-shot storyboard and a render script.
take: Storyboard every shot in a STORYBOARD.md before any code; the second generation followed that plan.
Used as the pacing reference for a later film, whose lesson was that a scene must not sit still too long.
future_use: Pacing reference for lyric-driven or music-led pieces.

what_it_is: Painted music video built by Claude with a custom WebGL brush renderer and parallel subagents per chapter.
take: Chapters were painted in parallel by subagents, each briefed from one ANIMATION_GUIDE.md; the lead reviewed each chapter on contact sheets and sent fixes back.
Director's timing note: do not let a scene sit too still for too long; the pacing reference was PDoomVideo.
future_use: Parallel per-scene builds that share one style brief.

what_it_is: HTML-to-video framework whose agent skills define captions, motion doctrine and seam transitions.
take: Caption model: filler (um, uh, stutters, self-corrections) is dropped; ordinary speech shows verbatim as a lower subtitle.
Embed (one big word behind the subject) is the scarce peak: at most one per sentence, never two in a row.
Captions are an overlay on the picture, never a reserved bottom band that the picture shifts around.
Cut at peak velocity and match direction and speed across the cut, using mirrored eases on both sides.
future_use: Caption hierarchy for talking-head reels with punch-word emphasis.

what_it_is: Large agent-run production framework for AI video, with many paid generation tools and per-asset QA.
take: Paid-call discipline: read the live model catalog, then announce tool, exact model, request count and estimated cost before every paid generation.
Route each asset by its role (free catalog, unique generation or licensed source) and record provenance for every file.
future_use: Preflight template for any approved paid B-roll generation.

what_it_is: Agent-driven system that rebuilds a reference video as an editable project from components and providers.
take: Each project keeps its build records and produced files in a result repository, so reruns can reuse existing outputs.
Model, provider endpoint and credential store are separate, so changing a service never touches the video code.
future_use: Editable project layout for multi-format client reels.

what_it_is: Desktop and agent tool that reverse-engineers a reference video into an editable motion project.
take: Its preview browser accepts only a restricted set of pointer, wheel, text and key events, with no arbitrary script or CDP access.
Each architecture change is checked against scope, dependencies and stated limits before it is accepted.
future_use: Reverse-engineering a reference reel into an editable template.

what_it_is: Router skill of best-practice rules for Remotion projects, covering captions, rendering and upgrades.
take: Preserve user changes: if the code changed outside the conversation, do not overwrite it; assume it was intentional or ask.
Captions workflow: decode audio to a 16 kHz mono waveform before transcribing with the Whisper model.
future_use: Only if a Remotion format is ever added to the pipeline.

what_it_is: Skill that drives a narration-video CLI through movie search, voice, script and composition steps.
take: Never submit a paid render without showing the full request body and getting the user's confirmation, since the cost is irreversible.
State the per-minute point cost before rendering, and let the user choose from a catalog of named templates.
future_use: Cost-confirmation step for any paid cloud render.

what_it_is: Toolkit of Claude Code video skills covering music, Blender, ElevenLabs, ffmpeg, image and video models.
take: ElevenLabs by style: natural narration stability 0.75–0.85, similarity 0.9, style 0–0.1; conversational stability 0.5–0.6, style 0.3–0.4.
Pauses: use break tags up to 3 s; if timing is still off, add the silence in post with ffmpeg instead of fighting the TTS engine.
Speed: for ratios above 4x or below 0.25x, or variable-speed ramps, pre-process the clip in ffmpeg rather than in the player.
future_use: Voice settings and pause handling if generated narration is added.

what_it_is: Claude skill that builds browser motion graphics as single HTML files with GSAP, avoiding slide-like cuts.
take: Determinism: no Math.random or Date.now in the render loop; use seeds set once at load and time taken from the timeline.
Slideshow test: if a slow zoom is the only motion, the scene is a slideshow; give it a continuously moving subject.
Sync voice-over to sentence boundaries with silencedetect, or a browser Web Audio pause finder when ffmpeg is missing.
future_use: Motion-graphic cards timed to a voice-over track.

what_it_is: Collection of Claude motion skills: render recipes, Remotion templates, brand launch films and Disney-style rules.
take: Logos are never typeset or redrawn: download the exact official file and keep its aspect ratio and official colours.
Motion hierarchy: product motion first, then camera, type, secondary UI, and decorative accents last; delay secondary layers 2–6 frames.
Decorative particles and glows never lead; they arrive after the main action.
future_use: Logo reveal and end-card motion order.

what_it_is: Index of 56 open motion-graphics skills in 19 packs, plus a shared verify-loop toolkit for renders.
take: Verify loop: screenshot each frozen moment with the seek harness, then tile start, middle and end frames into one contact sheet.
Probe the MP4 with asserts on real resolution, codec, fps and duration before calling a render done.
future_use: Standard QA sequence for every render.

what_it_is: MCP server that drives Google Flow in a browser to make free-tier video, with per-call credit caps.
take: Each generation call takes a max_credits cap, so one job cannot spend past an approved amount.
Keep a quote table per model, resolution and duration (e.g. 360p 4 s = 4 credits) and read it before queueing.
future_use: Credit caps for approved B-roll; browser automation is a terms risk.

what_it_is: Claude skill and TypeScript library for animated ink line-art figures and scenes exported to video.
take: Match a reference clip by measurement: find the loop length from the frame period, then read poses off a measuring grid.
Overlay check: scale the clip into the crop with CSS percentages, set currentTime to t, and compare ink at 65% opacity.
future_use: Matching an animated reference clip exactly, if ever needed.

what_it_is: Agent skill that builds editable videos from reusable templates, with beat-timed changes and automated checks.
take: QA check: no still stretch longer than 3 s; a reading hold may breathe but must still change visibly.
Beat check: report the share of strong visual changes within 66 ms of a beat; its validation files show 73–97%.
Audio check: report mean level in dBFS per file, and flag a short side under 1080 px for delivery review.
Text on screen: one thing to read at a time, held about 5 s or more per page.
future_use: Our QA script: stills, beat alignment, loudness and resolution.

what_it_is: Chinese Claude skill for product, music and explainer videos, with reference research and voice direction.
take: Default to 9:16 (1080×1920) unless told otherwise; never build in 16:9 and then crop or shrink it.
Narration: measure the old baseline before setting a numeric target; sample several takes per segment and keep the best.
Re-time the picture to the spoken start and end of each line, not to fixed seconds.
Facts on screen need sources; generated pictures may illustrate but never serve as evidence of a real event.
future_use: Voice-direction and sourcing rules for explainer reels.

what_it_is: Browserless programmatic video engine for Remotion-style TypeScript, with checks that run before render.
take: Check loop before render: doctor lists every element that would be left out, then lint and type-check, a contact strip, and only then the full render.
Fonts that are not registered can draw as nothing with no warning, so confirm each font by eye on a still first.
future_use: Pre-render doctor-style check for the reel build.

what_it_is: Pipeline that retargets locked-camera video of a person onto a Mixamo character in Blender.
take: QA gate on every retarget: check exploded bones, hip pops and foot skate before accepting a pass.
Never decide a limb from a still frame; the pose estimator loses occluded limbs, so check frames in motion.
future_use: Character animation only, not talking-head reels.

what_it_is: Pure-code, beat-synced showcase video skill: HTML frames, Python-synthesised score, FFmpeg assembly.
take: Under each text card the music drops to about 6% (roughly -24 dB) and returns after; voice-first mixing by dropout.
Beat grid: at 120 BPM one beat is 0.5 s; place cuts on beat multiples and hold text cards for two beats.
Keep text inside an 80–96 px safe margin on a 1920 frame; rescale the margin for our 1080×1920 frame.
future_use: Beat-timed card timing for music-led reels.

what_it_is: Agent skill that directs and renders videos locally, with critic review, loudness checks and fact-checking.
take: Verify before delivery: run QA with loudness and true-peak numbers, fix every FAIL, and leave no open finding.
Researcher pass: fact-check every claim against sources before the final render of any video that states facts.
Quality mode: a separate critic pass reviews each finished video and writes its findings to a file.
future_use: Fact-check and critic passes before a client reel is published.

what_it_is: Remotion and motion-design skill set with pacing numbers, component libraries and explainer scripts.
take: Narration pace: 150 words per minute standard, 120 for technical content, 170 for energetic short-form.
Scene durations: establishing shot 3–5 s, feature demo 5–8 s.
Arc for a 90 s piece: hook 0–5 s, build 5–30 s, peak 30–70 s, resolve 70–90 s.
future_use: Pacing targets for a 30–60 s reel script.

what_it_is: Chinese Agent skills for AI video prompts covering action, emotion, asset sheets and production workflow.
take: Prompt structure: split a 15 s clip into 2–3 s phases, each with a timestamp and one main action.
Describe observable behaviour, not emotion words, and use the fewest signals that make a feeling legible.
future_use: Writing prompts for approved AI B-roll only.

what_it_is: Installable short-video recipes for coding agents: storyboard review, single-shot rework and release QA.
take: Targeted rework: fix one shot, voice line, subtitle or music bed instead of rebuilding the whole reel.
Storyboard first, then one representative shot before the rest; the user approves direction at each gate.
Write lessons back into the recipe only after they pass validation, then reuse them on the next reel.
future_use: Turn each client's approved reel into a reusable recipe.

what_it_is: Nine motion-design skills for coding agents: easing, colour, shot framing, logo reveals and beat-sync editing.
take: Easing tokens: enter ease-out cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); exit ease-in cubic-bezier(0.7,0,0.84,0); reposition ease-in-out cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1).
Reveals run 0.8–2.5 s; never skew or squash a logo, scale and fade only, and always ship a static end frame.
Gradients: interpolate in OKLCH rather than sRGB, and add 3–5% grain to prevent banding.
future_use: Motion tokens for title cards, logo reveals and transitions.

what_it_is: Cloud VideoDB skills for searching, clipping, subtitling and composing video through its API.
take: Transcript first: generate the transcript once, read sentence segments with timestamps, choose the ranges yourself, then cut.
Compose in one render call: tracks of clips with start, duration and asset, with captions timed from the transcript.
future_use: Long-footage search, only if client footage may leave the machine.

what_it_is: Skill that generates short MiniMax H3 image-to-video clips through a Google Colab runner.
take: Reference-to-video takes up to 9 ordered images mapped to Picture 1–9; first-frame mode takes exactly one image; clips run 4–15 s.
Reference prompt structure: subject_definitions, summary, retention_analysis, then one detailed block per shot.
future_use: AI B-roll prompts if credits are approved.

what_it_is: Remotion starter kit with slash commands for image, video and voice generation, plus a caption component.
take: SKIP: a self-described vibe-coded experiment with known bugs and inconsistent docs; its Remotion stack does not fit our HTML pipeline.
Captions are synced from word-level transcript timestamps, the same idea our whisper pipeline already uses.
future_use: Not needed; keep for reference only.

what_it_is: Turkish Claude skill that picks a drawing engine per scene and joins scenes with page-turn transitions.
take: Read each scene's frames before writing its prompt; write only what the frames show and never invent speech or sound.
Pick the engine by what is on screen: text and data to HTML, characters to plain canvas, real 3D to Three.js.
future_use: Per-scene engine choice for mixed-format reels.

what_it_is: Claude skill that adapts real open-source animation cases into new films, keeping their look and motion.
take: No animating before the storyboard is approved; the user approves beats, then the look, then each storyboard panel.
Every factual claim on screen is web-checked and listed with its source in the brief; never claim 'first' without one.
future_use: Storyboard-approval gate and fact-source list for client reels.

what_it_is: Remotion motion-design skill with voice, licensed music, SFX and automatic text-fit and contrast checks.
take: Voice is the clock: one script file produces narration phrase by phrase and sets every scene's timing, with no hand-typed frame numbers.
Text probe reads each text box from the rendered DOM and flags cut-off or overlapping text before render.
Design meter counts generic signals in each frame (near black with one accent, giant condensed face, all caps) and revises them.
future_use: Caption text-fit probe for every reel render.

what_it_is: Skill that makes DeepSeek produce Remotion motion films close to Opus 5.5 output from the same prompt.
take: Priority order: the prompt's own words first, then craft, continuity, rhythm, and bookkeeping last.
Quality gate: five jurors critique the film, and each must score at least 8 before delivery; fix and re-score.
future_use: Juror-style self-review before any client preview.

what_it_is: Skill that researches a topic and renders a promo MP4 drawn entirely in code, with sourced numbers.
take: Fewer process rules made video 23–51% cheaper in their A/B test with no visible drop; keep only the rules that matter.
Every number on screen needs a source; research collects about ten sourced facts before the story is written.
Frames are captured as JPEG with parallel workers at CRF 25: 2–3x faster than PNG and visually the same after H.264.
future_use: Lean prompt rules for cheaper reel-building runs.

what_it_is: AI video studio skill set: onboarding, cast, cinematography and series workflows with budget gates.
take: Budget gate: estimate, show a production book with the cost, and lock the budget only after the user's yes.
Gate 1 is the script; nothing is spent until the script is approved.
Storyboard each scene as one grid image so continuity holds across that scene's shots.
future_use: Approval-gate pattern for any paid generation step.

what_it_is: Agent kit that turns a reference video's style into a Remotion motion video, plus animated logo styles.
take: Describe a style in numbers, not adjectives: 'rises 40px in 0.45 s with easeOutCubic', not 'smooth movement'.
Narration pace is about 2 words per second (120 words a minute); size the script to the reel length before timing shots.
SFX map: small element appears gets tick or pop; key word lands gets hit; fast transition gets whoosh; key beat gets riser then impact, used once or twice.
future_use: Style-from-reference workflow for end-card and title motion.

what_it_is: Remotion starter with copywriting, Remotion best-practice and UI skills for prompt-driven video work.
take: On-screen copy: specific over vague; cut words like 'streamline', 'optimize' and 'innovative' from scripts and cards.
One idea per section; benefits over features; end on one clear call to action.
Honest over sensational: never invent a statistic or testimonial in copy, even for a demo.
future_use: Hook and CTA line checks for client scripts.

what_it_is: Chinese-language knowledge-to-short-video pipeline with narration, scene HTML, audio rules and a feedback loop.
take: Vertical type floors at 1080x1920: headline at least 64 px, body at least 36 px, labels at least 28 px; flag anything smaller.
Set one safe padding for the frame (top 180 px, sides 90 px, bottom 220 px) instead of adding padding per element.
Hook scene (first 3-5 s) is pure hook: shock number, question, strong contrast or suspense; body text starts in scene 2.
Their own sample: 5-second completion at 44%+ went with 36K plays versus 3.1K below 38%; one creator's data, so treat as a hypothesis.
future_use: Type-size and safe-zone QA checks for every vertical reel.

what_it_is: Packages a talking-head MP4 and SRT with side graphics and chapter bars, gated by two human approvals.
take: Gate every job: plan, then storyboard approval, then 8 review stills and a contact sheet, then the full render only after explicit approval.
For 16:9 layouts keep the presenter in x 35-65%, side lanes at x 5-32% and 68-95%, and the bottom 18% for captions; adapt for 9:16.
No single beat longer than six seconds; aim for 1.6-3.2 s per on-screen card where the source allows.
Check stills at about 72% of each beat plus camera entry, peak and return, face clearance and subtitle clearance.
future_use: Approval gates and face-zone rules for any split-layout reel.

what_it_is: Agent skill that drives the VidMuse CLI for images and video: login, price check, generate, download.
take: Estimate before submitting: price = unit price x seconds x quantity; report 'unknown' rather than guess when the unit does not match.
Lock the request in a task record (state planned, authorization not_set) before any spend, so the approved job is the one that runs.
Deliver the file and say what was generated and what was not verified, not a submission receipt.
future_use: Spend-lock and cost-estimate pattern for any paid generator we add.

what_it_is: Agent framework for short dramas, MVs, explainers and ads, with paid jobs priced before submission.
take: Quote every paid generation job first and submit only after the user agrees; show the total before anything is sent.
Run credit jobs in a discounted off-peak window and cap tasks in flight at one by default on small accounts.
Keep a per-series cast and voice so the same face and voice recur across episodes; for us, one per client.
Narration misreads: keep the written word in subtitles and give the voice a respelled string; re-listen after every change.
future_use: Spend approval and off-peak scheduling for paid B-roll.

what_it_is: Claude Code skills that cut real footage and motion films in code with local Python and ffmpeg.
take: Caption law: block centre about 64.5% of frame height; text about 4.2% of frame height (81 px on 1920); two lines at most, broken on meaning.
White text with a thin dark outline (about 0.28% of height, at least 3 px) and no background box; a box reads as an amateur burn-in.
Film test for each choice: would a working editor have made it on purpose? If the tool did it, change it.
Keep a provenance record for every shot (source, licence, in and out points) so each B-roll clip can be traced and cleared.
future_use: Caption placement and per-shot provenance log; still check against the face box.

what_it_is: Agent-run editing stack: understand a video, then cut, add B-roll, captions, cards and motion with review gates.
take: B-roll QA: flag any cutaway shorter than 1.5 s followed by a longer pure-B-roll run as a short flash.
Clip speed only from 0.5x, 1x, 1.5x or 2x; warn above 1.5x and flag high above 3x.
Captions: fill a placement beat for every cue (fixed or meaning-driven) and validate the plan before any preview is made.
Captions over B-roll get a spatial-context check so the text does not land on the subject.
future_use: Shot-level B-roll and caption review gates for talking-head reels.

what_it_is: Chinese-language site and README for HyperFrames, with routes for captions, talking-head overlays and motion graphics.
take: Embedded captions: keep the original footage untouched, then add word-by-word captions and graphics behind the speaker's head.
Talking-head overlay routes (lower third, data callout, quote card, sidebar, picture-in-picture): choose one route per beat.
Narration-free motion graphics stay under about 10 s; design the static frame first, then animate.
future_use: Caption-behind-subject using MediaPipe person masks, so the face is never covered.

what_it_is: Skill that builds standalone HTML animation scenes and renders them deterministically to MP4.
take: Only the last scene fades to black; every earlier cut hands off through a transition (pixel dissolve, iris, wipe, flash).
Over busy backgrounds put text on a scrim, plate or card (scene-scrim, text-plate, text-card) rather than on bare video.
Use a named spring preset per motion class; seven presets run from springGentle to springStiff.
Use the title size classes instead of inline font sizes on headings, so type stays consistent across scenes.
future_use: Scene transitions and text-scrim rules for multi-scene HTML reels.

what_it_is: Claude Code and Codex workbench that makes films as code and checks them with rendered contact sheets.
take: Pick a tier first (quick, standard or studio); it sets how many human stop-points a run has and how much checking happens.
The agent cannot watch its own video; it checks rendered frames as a contact sheet plus transcript timestamps.
Load each reference only at the step that needs it (a stage-filtered command list), instead of reading every guide up front.
future_use: Tiered run plans and frame-based self-check for longer reels.

what_it_is: Five Claude skills for HyperFrames motion styles: 3D toy, kinetic type, hand-drawn, diagrams and data charts.
take: Entries ease out (power2 to power4) and last at most 0.8 s; exits take about 75% of the entry time; a full stagger at most 0.5 s.
Write a reads sheet: the one thing each beat must make the viewer understand; keep each label on screen at least 0.8 s.
Hold 0.3-0.75 s of stillness just before the payoff so the key line lands.
One idea per frame: 1-4 words, at most 3 lines, filling 50-80% of frame width.
future_use: Motion timing and reads-sheet rules for title and end cards.

what_it_is: Agent skill that builds one-HTML-file procedural videos, each frame a pure function of frame number and seed.
take: Verify by looking: render three frames per scene, read them, fix, then move on; never trust the code alone.
Full render only after a contact sheet of the whole video looks right; sound is written last, locked to scene lengths.
9:16 safe areas: platform UI covers the top 15% and bottom 20%; keep labels and faces between them, with lower titles at 70% height.
future_use: 9:16 safe-zone and contact-sheet gate for title and end-card motion.

what_it_is: Multi-engine AI video and motion framework with skills for music, avatars, generation gateways and TTS.
take: Music presets by use: corporate-bg 110 BPM, upbeat-tech 128, ambient 72, lofi 85 for screen recordings, cta 135.
Generative music needs a RunPod key and endpoint, so it is a paid step that needs the same yes as any other spend.
Video generator gateways (fal Kling, MiniMax, VEO; HeyGen) each need a cost check before any call; none is used for talking-head reels now.
future_use: Music bed generation if Mixkit has no fitting track.

what_it_is: Catalog of 13 Claude video skills plus an orchestrator that picks one video engine per request.
take: Never report a video as made until the output file exists and has been probed; list what is still unverified.
Iterate at low resolution and frame rate (for example 480p15), then render full quality once, after the cut is approved.
future_use: Preview-quality render tiers, with one full render at the end.

what_it_is: Desktop editor that generates Roblox R15 and R6 animation clips from AI prompts and previews them on a 3D rig.
take: Skip: Roblox rig animation has no use in talking-head reels; nothing here transfers to our footage, captions or cuts.
The one idea worth keeping is a visual review loop: send a contact sheet of the draft back to the model for one fix pass.
future_use: Contact-sheet self-review pass idea for QA; rig work unrelated.

what_it_is: Skill for code-driven motion videos, slides and landing pages, with rules distilled from 30 high-performing videos.
take: Type floors at 1080x1920: captions at least 40 px, body at least 30 px, meta at least 16 px; keep 220 px clear at top and bottom for platform UI.
One base colour, one foreground, one accent; the accent covers under 10% of the frame.
Every 2-4 s one new event happens; the last frame echoes the first with the same object in a changed state.
Final mix targets -14 LUFS, consistent with our loudness standard.
future_use: Accent-area cap and type-size floors for end cards and title cards.

what_it_is: Three Claude skills for animated charts, infographic reveals and narrated slide-deck videos with exact numbers.
take: Ease the value, not the opacity: count-ups use easeOutCubic; round before formatting and use tabular numerals so digits do not jitter.
Hold each key number about 0.5 s before the next item; title hold 0.8-1.2 s; each item 1.2-2.0 s.
Limit an infographic to 3-5 supporting numbers; more than five competing elements reads as chaos.
future_use: Finance number count-ups and chart reveals, from client-supplied data only.

what_it_is: Open-source HTML-to-MP4 framework for agent-made motion graphics, with named motion bands and easing tokens.
take: Motion bands by mood, per move: energy 0.15-0.3 s, professional 0.3-0.5 s, gravity 0.5-0.8 s, cinematic 0.8-2.0 s.
Set band, ease and stagger once per film in a signature tag so every element shares one tempo; their example stagger is 60 ms.
Name any unchosen dial before rendering (their dev tool lists unset band, ease and stagger), so no default slips in silently.
future_use: Shared motion-band tokens for all client reel graphics.

what_it_is: End-to-end narrated video skill: sources, segmented script, TTS, Manim visuals, QC and archive.
take: Sync scenes to measured voice length: read each generated audio file's duration and set the scene to match, never by hand.
QC from extracted frames: look for cropped text, unreadable charts, broken layouts and severe overlap before delivery.
Log caveats (scope, assumptions, version) beside each figure or claim they qualify.
future_use: Caveat log and frame-QC checklist for any sourced explainer.

what_it_is: Eleven Claude skills for motion films, explainers, product tours, ads and testimonials, each a SKILL.md.
take: Write brief, concept, storyboard and beat sheet before any build; after the build, check every frame and the audio.
Finish with a scored director review of the cut, not just a technical pass.
Testimonial format: use only the client's own recorded words; a drafted quote is never acceptable (our inference from the format).
future_use: Testimonial and how-to formats for client reels, with real quotes only.

what_it_is: Minimal template that turns HTML/CSS cards and a prepared audio file into a 16:9 card video via FFmpeg.
take: Skip: no face, no transcript timing and no speech-linked captions, which our reels need; the pipeline already covers this.
One idea worth keeping: GSAP used sparingly on cards (scene fade, small y move, subtle scale).
future_use: Silent 16:9 card explainers if a client asks for no face.

what_it_is: Hermes skill pack that turns briefs and articles into HyperFrames projects, with brief, storyboard and QA gates.
take: Warm iteration: edit only the affected element by id and its storyboard row; never regenerate the whole HTML file.
Fixed build order: validated brief, then storyboard, then DESIGN.md, then composition, then render report.
Keep brand colours, fonts and CTA in one brand JSON applied to every video; use one per client.
Caption start and end times must match each audio segment within 500 ms; check this in sync QA.
future_use: Surgical-edit rule and per-client brand JSON for multi-client reels.

what_it_is: Remotion skill that builds motion graphics from a brief, with style guides, storyboard templates and render QA.
take: Ask the brief questions once, in one batch, and do not scaffold or render until they are answered.
Render still frames at the opening, before and after each key action, at transition boundaries and on the result hold; read them.
Safe margins: 5-7% on landscape and 7-10% on vertical, then adjust to the platform overlays.
future_use: Still-frame QA at beat boundaries for every client reel.

what_it_is: Skill set for Magic Hour AI video, image and face workflows, with review steps and credit-aware routing.
take: Ad variants: change one variable (opening line, offer line or visual opening) and keep the accepted body unchanged so the test is fair.
Review every generated file: first and last frames, continuity, flicker, abrupt cuts, real dimensions; listen through the full export.
Generate only the missing pieces and record which take each new piece replaces.
future_use: Hook-variant testing on approved talking-head footage.

what_it_is: Claude plugin set for short launch films, captioned clips and charts, each film built as one HTML file.
take: Honest charts: bars start at zero; no truncated, dual or log axes; a donut has at most 5 slices that sum to the whole.
Every number on screen gets a source line; counters land exactly on the sourced figure in fixed-width digit slots.
Captions show the speaker's words unchanged; only punctuation, case and recorded filler removals are allowed; check caption times against the waveform.
Data moves on critically damped springs (no overshoot), so a bar never passes its final value and shows a wrong number on the way.
future_use: Chart and caption-fidelity checks for any sourced number in client reels.

what_it_is: Thirteen Claude skills that turn links, articles and scripts into short videos through the Revid cloud API.
take: Estimate cost before rendering: run the no-spend credit calculation first, then render only after the user agrees.
Polling pattern: check status every 5 s, relaxing to 8 s once progress passes 30%, and stop cleanly on failure.
On insufficient credits, step quality or resolution down before asking for a top-up, and say what each step costs.
future_use: Credit estimate before any paid render or cloud generation.

what_it_is: Hermes skill with an ffmpeg and Whisper toolkit: silence removal, captions, scene detection, reframing and loudness.
take: Silence removal: try Silero VAD first and fall back to ffmpeg silence detection when the model is unavailable.
Platform presets carry maximum lengths (for example 9:16 at 60 s or 90 s); check the length before export.
Smart reframe: a face-tracking crop (OpenCV) for each target aspect ratio.
future_use: Silence-removal fallback chain for talking-head pauses.

what_it_is: Python motion engine with keyframe layers, easing presets and slide and kinetic-type templates; PIL, numpy, OpenCV.
take: Skip for now: our HyperFrames and ghost-editor path already renders motion; this would add a second renderer to maintain.
Idea worth keeping: seeded frame callbacks that give the same output every render, usable without a browser.
future_use: Fallback renderer if the Chrome-based HyperFrames path is unavailable.

what_it_is: Remotion workbench scaffold with hooks that block non-deterministic motion code and a staged production skill.
take: Motion comes from the frame: no CSS or Tailwind animation classes, no Math.random, and every interpolate clamped to its range.
interpolate input ranges must be strictly increasing; a decreasing range crashes the render.
Run a still-frame QA for every new or changed scene before any full render, then a separate semantic review.
Route each learning to one source-of-truth file; propose the diff and wait for approval before writing any rule.
future_use: Determinism lint and still-frame gate for our HTML motion cards.

what_it_is: Claude-driven video workflow using ffmpeg, ElevenLabs music and voice, Scribe transcripts and HyperFrames overlays.
take: Normalise every segment first (one size, frame rate and codec), then concatenate losslessly; mixed sources break a straight concat.
Captions as transparent PNGs overlaid by ffmpeg, so burn-in does not depend on libass fonts.
Mix music with voice ducking, then loudnorm the final mix in one pass.
Sample frames from its own output and check the audio before showing the user.
future_use: Normalise-then-concat step for multi-take reels.

what_it_is: Vendored copy of Remotion's official Claude skills for routing video tasks, captions and rendering.
take: Caption pages: group words into TikTok-style pages and highlight the active word with one colour constant.
Import SRT with @remotion/captions and display it; transcribe audio to 16 kHz WAV first when needed.
Preserve user edits: if code changed outside the chat, do not overwrite it; ask first.
future_use: Caption page and highlight reference for word-timed reels.

what_it_is: Hosted MCP server that drives Google Flow for Veo video and Nano Banana images through the user's own account.
take: Skip: it reaches Google Flow through unofficial access (the README says Google offers no public API), a risk for client work.
Cost reference: video costs 7, 10 or 12 Google credits for 4, 6 or 8 s; images are free up to a per-key limit.
future_use: Cost reference only; any generated B-roll still needs an explicit yes.

what_it_is: Remotion skill for generating Resemble.ai voiceovers with word timestamps for synced captions.
take: Drive captions from TTS word timestamps; the highlight colour switches at each word's start time.
Pad the composition about 30 frames (1 s) past the audio length so the last word is not cut.
Synchronous TTS takes up to 2,000 characters; longer scripts use streaming, generated segment by segment.
future_use: Word-timed captions if a client wants a voiceover reel.

what_it_is: Local MIT editor that agents drive with FFmpeg and whisper.cpp: silence, retakes, transcript cuts, captions, cut checks.
take: Cut check: for each cut, flag words that may be clipped and show a contact sheet of frames on both sides of the cut.
Retake removal: when a phrase is said twice in a row, cut the earlier take and keep the last full take.
Dry-run silence removal first, with a sensitivity setting, so the cut count is visible before anything changes.
Captions do not follow cuts (their open backlog item): re-run captioning after every edit that moves words.
future_use: Cut-check contact sheet for every jump cut in talking-head reels.

what_it_is: Editor's-judgment skill for cutting, pacing, captions, loudness and licensing across video types, with a CC0 audio library.
take: Graphic or text appears at most 0.5 s before the word that names it, each element within 0.6 s of its word, and no card sits empty over 1 s.
Talking-head recipe: open on the strongest line, not a greeting; remove filler and repeated takes, keeping the best fluent take.
Music sits 18 to 25 dB under the voice with ducking; master at -14 LUFS with true peak under -1 dBTP (we keep -1.5 dBTP).
A CC0 sound-effect library with per-file loudness gives a no-attribution SFX source; still check Content ID before any music.
future_use: Timing and SFX-sync checks for explainer and talking-head reels.

what_it_is: Claude Code skill that animates photos into short clips via a self-hosted LTX-2.3 model on Modal GPU.
take: Confirms cost before every run: cold start 90 to 200 s, a few cents, and offers a cheap smoke test first.
Writes the prompt as the photo's description plus one motion phrase, so the motion is authored rather than the subject re-described.
Frame counts follow 8k+1 (97 frames is about 4 s at 24 fps); pick the length before generating.
future_use: Animate a client-approved still into B-roll, only after a cost yes.

what_it_is: Remotion starter kit with three Claude skills and hard rules for deterministic, frame-driven overlay video.
take: Motion is frame-driven only: no CSS animation or transition classes, because each rendered frame is a snapshot and timed CSS drifts.
Every interpolate() gets a clamp and inputRange must strictly increase; randomness comes from a seeded random(seed), never Math.random.
Before an expensive render, a semantic review checks spring remapping, hard-coded colours and dual subtitle paths that hooks cannot catch.
future_use: Determinism rules for any future code-built overlay or chart video.

what_it_is: Agent-driven media studio that renders images, diagrams, 3D and edited video from source files, with bounded JSON recipe packs.
take: Agents extend the system by writing inert, bounded JSON recipe packs against a closed operation registry, never by registering code.
Each pack is content-addressed, so a change is a new render and the previous version stays reproducible.
future_use: Pattern for validated storyboard JSON; not a talking-head editor.

what_it_is: Skill that turns a chat script into a vertical texting-style video with paced bubbles, typing dots and sounds.
take: One message reveals at a time on a rhythm: typing beat, bubble pop, then a pause to read; never dump the thread at frame 0.
Bubbles cap at 74% of width and use 34 px text at 1080 px wide, leaving a gutter at the phone edge.
future_use: Chat-style story format if a client asks for texting reels.

what_it_is: Replicates a reference B-roll clip as editable Remotion code through staged, gated stills, motion measurement and QA.
take: Lock each scene's settled still against the source first; motion work starts only after every scene's still passes.
When QA fails, one owner stage gets the fix (preflight, layout, motion, implementation or QA); after two rounds, record known differences and stop.
Measure each element's first-visible, settled and end frames instead of eyeballing; fit one continuous curve across a move rather than restarting an ease at each sample.
future_use: Matching a client's motion-graphic B-roll to a reference clip.

what_it_is: Portuguese-language studio that builds narrated animated story videos entirely in code, with Fish Audio or cloned voices.
take: SKIP: no talking-head, captioning or compliance pattern to reuse; its episodes are cartoon narratives.
Voice-clone samples are kept out of the repo because they can clone a real person's voice; keep consent evidence separate.
API keys are never pasted into chat; the owner generates them and runs a local configure script.
future_use: Voice-consent handling if a broker's voice were ever cloned, with written consent.

what_it_is: Rust SDK for scripted motion-canvas-style animation with voice, shaders, charts and ffmpeg export.
take: Caches text-to-speech by content hash: the first render writes tts/{hash}.wav and later renders reuse it without calling the voice service.
Falls back to a speech-rate duration estimate when no key is set or the voice call fails, so a render never blocks.
Sound clips are placed at the current frame; a priority flag ducks the soundtrack under voice.
future_use: Scripted chart or diagram videos if we need code-driven data graphics.

what_it_is: Software-engineering monorepo whose bundled Claude skills cover code review, bug diagnosis, domain modelling and design.
take: Diagnose by building a feedback loop first: a failing test, or a diff of output against a known-good snapshot, before any fix.
Raise a flaky bug's reproduction rate by looping the trigger and widening timing windows before debugging.
future_use: Snapshot-diff QA loop for render regressions in the reel pipeline.

what_it_is: Agent skills for the sync. lipsync API: relip a video to new audio, fix spoken words, dub, and batch-run.
take: edit-dialogue changes spoken words in the speaker's voice; under our rule 3 it may only fix words the speaker actually said, with client sign-off.
Paid API: batch runs are quoted and piloted first, and a failed job resumes without paying twice.
future_use: Fix one mis-said word in a take, only with a cost yes and client approval.

what_it_is: Skill that rebuilds a code-made motion video as an editable After Effects project with live text and shape layers.
take: Export the scene from the same data the renderer draws, so the AE project and the video cannot drift apart.
Text stays live text with the real string; handwriting is a per-word mask keyed at narration times, not a pre-rendered image.
future_use: Editable AE handoff of a motion segment to a client's editor.

what_it_is: HyperFrames skill that turns CSV or JSON data into deterministic, editable bar-race and chart videos.
take: Compile data to frozen JSON before any playback, so the animation never fetches or recomputes numbers at render time.
Checks columns, date grain, missing values, series count and units first; asks only when a choice changes the story.
future_use: Client-data chart reveals; unsourced numbers must be labelled illustrative.

what_it_is: Chrome extension plus local MCP server that lets Codex or Claude direct a Google Vids document, with verified export.
take: Speech check: Whisper small, no prompt, matched 103 of 103 normalized words to the script; adopt this word-for-word gate before every final export.
An export counts as succeeded only after the file is copied, hashed, probed and fully decoded; unknown outcomes become needs_reconciliation.
Their review logged a one-frame early caption appearance and said so; report measured limits rather than claiming a clean pass.
future_use: Script-match and export-verification gates for every final reel.

what_it_is: Chinese Claude skill and toolkit that makes narrated, sourced explainer videos, with checks gating render.
take: When true peak hits the limiter first, loudness cannot reach -14 LUFS (one cut landed at -16); add a limiter before normalising.
Assertions such as numbers, years and quotes are checked against a source and logged in a ledger before they enter the script.
Suggested fix in their review: fingerprint each stage's inputs so a stale check or mix cannot pass final; an edited WAV must invalidate its listen check.
An agent that did not build the film reviews script and cut; a human must hear voiceover tone.
future_use: Sourced-claim ledger and limiter-then-normalise steps for narrated client reels.

what_it_is: Skill that builds self-contained HTML canvas animations at 60 fps and exports them to MP4 via Puppeteer and FFmpeg.
take: Entrances use cubic ease-out and transitions use ease-in-out, the two easings the skill calls smoothest.
Phase transitions overlap by 0.5 to 1 s so no frame is empty between beats.
future_use: Motion-token defaults for lower-third and end-card entrances.

what_it_is: Claude skill that builds canvasState JSON with text, shapes and effects, then renders MP4 through a CLI.
take: Every visible element gets animIn and animOut, with a 300 to 500 ms stagger between elements; nothing pops in or out unanimated.
Keep decorative background layers at opacity 0.15 or lower, with 2 to 4 decorative helpers per scene.
Check that maxTime is at least the last element's end, or the final elements get cut off.
future_use: Stagger and decor-density rules for animated caption cards.

what_it_is: Films a web bug and its fix as one before/after MP4 with real clicks, DOM assertions and source hashes.
take: A caption never replaces the check: each side asserts the expected text in the DOM before the film is accepted.
Receipts store source hashes, tying each film to the exact code that produced it.
future_use: Before/after proof films for software clients, not for reels.

what_it_is: Chinese skill set that plans, builds, edits and reviews code-rendered videos from a validated storyboard.json.
take: Each on-screen read lasts at least 0.6 s with no overlaps; text holds for the longer of a minimum or characters divided by reading speed.
Keep picture-in-picture areas in reserved_regions so a layout check guarantees captions never sit under the inset.
A reviewer may not pass a visual check without opening the image; if it cannot view images, the item stays pending, not pass.
future_use: Layout check that keeps captions clear of the talking-head inset.

what_it_is: Chinese video-production hub that routes topics to specialist skills for whiteboard, Q-version history, maps and promos.
take: Character motion runs anticipation, action, overshoot, settle; the wind-up and settle are longer than the action itself.
Accessories such as hats and hair lag one beat behind the body, and expression changes are hard cuts, not fades.
future_use: Character motion timing for a non-face explainer segment.

what_it_is: Claude skill for 10 to 60 s product motion films built as one continuous take with measured moves.
take: Measure pacing before cutting: the reference was 34% dead-still with 7 hard cuts; vary shot lengths at least 4x, from 0.25 s to 2.5 s.
Score continuity per boundary: a film scored 0.40 was rejected and one at 0.75 accepted, so carry is checked, not assumed.
Use the ideas only; the PolyForm licence forbids copying code into client work.
future_use: Pacing and boundary-continuity checks for 30 to 60 s demo reels.

what_it_is: Apache-2.0 motion-direction skill that critiques and builds motion graphics, measuring eases and gating each film.
take: Measured median move is 10 frames (0.33 s); translate and scale take 11 to 12 frames, opacity 6 in and 7 out.
Emphasis is spent, not spread: at most a quarter of beats are 'the point', and endings get smaller.
Hold before what matters and give reading its exact time; stop before the idea is spent and end quieter than you began.
future_use: Motion-timing and emphasis rules for lower-thirds and end cards.

what_it_is: Claude skill for premium short commercials for real businesses, with a builder-versus-critic review loop and audio rules.
take: The business must be clear on mute: a first-time viewer should say what it does and what to do next with sound off.
Never invent testimonials, ratings, savings or confirmed appointments; a concept film is labelled as a concept.
Check generated music loudness per second and reject tracks with a near-silent intro or dips under key scenes.
The builder never judges its own cut: a fresh critic reviews each render against the brief and references.
future_use: Mute-first clarity and fresh-critic review for any client promo.

what_it_is: Chinese skill that makes code-driven software product and release promos with real components, GSAP and original audio.
take: Duck music before a sound effect: about 3 to 3.5 dB for clicks (40 ms ahead, recover in 200 to 240 ms), 5 to 6 dB for confirmations.
Gain SFX from measured peaks, not by ear: built-in effects peak near -20 dBFS, so the same gain vanishes under music.
Every on-screen claim records its source and release status; demo data may be fixed, but feature claims need evidence.
future_use: SFX ducking table for click and confirmation sounds in reels.

what_it_is: Claude Code skill for code-only motion design films: HTML frame engine, Playwright render, ffmpeg audio on measured peaks.
take: Illustrative content is labelled 'Example data' or 'Illustration' on screen, and captions must stay true to what was made.
Render a fast 540p draft before the master, and blend sub-frames on a 180-degree shutter for motion blur.
Place each sound effect on its measured peak and master to -14 LUFS.
future_use: Draft-then-master render loop and labelled-illustration rule for explainers.

what_it_is: 15-skill pack for launch-grade motion graphics in code, with brand intake that writes brand and motion files first.
take: Never round, reformat or add a number: real figures are used as given, and sample data gets an 'Illustrative data' label on every frame.
Measure a seamless loop against frame 0, never the midpoint, because a sine returns to zero there and hides the motion.
In ffmpeg's eq filter, add eval=frame or the expression runs once and nothing moves.
future_use: Number-integrity rule for any on-screen figures in a mortgage reel.

what_it_is: Chinese-first HyperFrames skill that directs cinematic promo films: brief, assets, layout, snapshots and review.
take: Two phases with a stop: propose the brief and design, wait for confirmation, then build assets and composition.
One primary motion idea per scene, then stillness after each important reveal so the text can be read.
Snapshot the hero frame and transition midpoints, and check Chinese text measurement and safe zones before render.
future_use: Brief-first gating and midpoint snapshot review for reel builds.

what_it_is: Claude skill that turns a website URL into a music-first launch film with one continuous shape and measured sound.
take: Voiceover first: render one audio per line, get word timestamps, derive each frame's duration from its line, then build frames.
Cue visuals 0.02 to 0.06 s before the word so they land on it; transcribers often clip the first word of a line.
Motion grammar: nothing ends moving; every frame lands and holds.
future_use: Word-locked caption and motion timing for talking-head reels.

what_it_is: Codex skill that builds a paper-collage advertisement from brief to mastered MP4 with narration and music.
take: Leave room around narration: hold for voice duration plus 0.7 to 1.5 s; extend the picture first and rewrite the line second.
Their mix target is -16 LUFS with a -1.5 dB true-peak ceiling, not our -14; state which target a reel uses before mastering.
Exact logos, UI and Chinese text stay on deterministic overlays; a draft motion model is used only where it adds value.
future_use: Narration hold rule and deterministic overlays for exact logos or text.

what_it_is: Claude skill that proposes three video plans with previews, waits for a choice, then builds the chosen video in code.
take: Propose three distinct plans with a still or short preview each; build only after the user picks one.
Render three stills per shot and check overflow, overlap, subject size and on-screen hold time before the next shot.
For films 30 s or longer, use a 960x540 low-res rough cut to check pacing before any polish.
future_use: Plan-and-preview gate before building any client reel.

what_it_is: Devrel video studio skill: records product walkthroughs with Playwright, composes cards in HyperFrames, masters with FFmpeg.
take: An approved_claims list: only numbers and names in the brief may appear on screen, and they come from the captured page.
Capture scripts use real locators and deliberate pauses; the browser capture repeats but is not frame-identical, so drive timing from the script.
future_use: Approved-claims whitelist for any software client walkthrough.

what_it_is: Runs a studio team of jobs to turn one request into a finished, reviewed short film rendered from code.
take: Before any paid image, video, voice or music call: read the real price, say what it buys, and wait for a yes.
Phone-width text audit: a script measures every drawn word and fails any too small to read at 360 px, before a full export.
Hook check: the whole hook sits on screen inside the first second; stills are checked by a fresh reviewer before the first cut.
future_use: Automated phone-width text check for caption sizes in every reel.

what_it_is: Seven-stage HyperFrames process for software promo films, with theme packs, a transition atlas and a variety audit.
take: Variety audit: read the storyboard ledger column by column; the same transition, ease or entrance twice in a row is flagged.
Stop at each gate for a human decision: brief, components, theme and storyboard each need a yes before build.
Credit every borrowed reference by name in a REFERENCES file next to the storyboard.
future_use: Variety audit for repeated effects across a client's reel series.

what_it_is: Chinese promo-video skill where cheap models fill a validated storyboard form and one command renders the film.
take: Cheap models fill a validated form, never code: the script rejects bad storyboards and checks industry rules before render.
A banned-word list returns a replacement phrase for each blocked claim, so the model rewrites rather than guesses.
Numbers reach the screen only through a counter field the script converts; two numbers split by punctuation are never joined.
Revise by naming the change: only the mentioned shots are rewritten, validated, and previewed as stills first.
future_use: Banned-claim list and counter-only numbers for compliance-heavy reels.

what_it_is: Claude skill for showreel-grade HyperFrames motion graphics with beat-locked timing, sound and generative layers.
take: Lock cuts to a beat grid: at 120 BPM one beat is 0.5 s, so every cut and impact is written as a beat index.
Keep one paused GSAP timeline for choreography plus a pure render(t) for generative layers, so any frame seeks on its own.
Use motion blur only on fast moves of one to three beats; everything else stays crisp.
future_use: Beat-grid cut placement for music-bed client reels.

what_it_is: Agent skill for cinematic product videos from shot recipe cards, real page screenshots, beat-synced cuts and sound design.
take: Fit the music grid by least squares over beat times, not the tempo scalar; accept only if residuals stay within 15 ms, and test half and double tempo.
Let key information settle for at least 1 s before the next cut, and give the brand mark a full second of hold.
The final SFX check runs on the rendered output, not the preview, because preview clamps volume and hides clipping.
future_use: Beat-fit check for music-driven promo cuts.

what_it_is: Beat-synced HyperFrames motion-graphic video skill with voice-over, captions, SFX and music.
take: QA gate: every music cut within ±2 ms of its target beat; music measured 4-6 dB under speech.
Loudness check: EBU R128 about -14 LUFS, true peak at or below -1 dBFS, blackdetect finds nothing outside fades.
Never overwrite a finished edition: each new cut gets its own project folder.
future_use: Music-bed level and loudness checks for product or explainer films.

what_it_is: Chinese-language promo-film skill pack: brief, storyboard, assets, edit, music and delivery as gated stages.
take: Stop for user confirmation after the brief and again after the storyboard, before any paid asset generation.
Asset plan table records each shot's source (generated, searched or client-supplied) and its status.
No shot plan, no image generation: a storyboard must exist before any asset is made.
future_use: Gate paid asset generation behind an approved shot list.

what_it_is: Scenario-driven screen recorder that films and edits web or desktop app demos with zooms and callouts.
take: Run a no-film check first: it plays the scenario fast and reports the failing step before recording.
Review one storyboard image per step before handing over, and fix the scenario rather than the file.
One video shows one idea of 15 to 60 seconds: settle the start, the 3 to 8 actions and the result first.
future_use: Screen-demo inserts for client product-feature explainers.

what_it_is: Ad-video skill turning product links into 15-45 s Remotion or HyperFrames ads with render QA.
take: Hook lands inside the first 2 seconds with the product visible; no scene runs over 2.5 s without a secondary beat.
The CTA gets at least 2.5 s and holds; the final scene has no transition-out.
Render cheap first: low-res stills, then a half-size draft, full size only after approval.
future_use: Short paid-social cut timing: hook, beat cap, CTA hold.

what_it_is: Agent skill that records a click-through web-app demo in a hidden browser with auto-zoom.
take: Phone demos use a 390x844 viewport with vertical output; LinkedIn clips under 3 s fail, so add a closing pause.
On a failed step, read the saved failure frame before changing the steps.
The posting target picks the preset: YouTube, X (up to 140 s), LinkedIn or Discord size caps.
future_use: Click-demo captures for app-feature inserts in other formats.

what_it_is: Showreel-grade motion graphics made from HTML scenes rendered frame by frame, with an original score.
take: The brief lists every on-screen fact with its source; anything not listed is not shown on screen.
Length by film type: 4-8 s logo sting, 10-20 s intro, 30-45 s selling promo with 3-5 proof points; the client's number wins.
Delivery master at -14 LUFS integrated, true peak at or below -1 dBTP, measured on the file.
future_use: Fact-sourcing brief template for compliance-checked client scripts.

what_it_is: Korean motion-graphics showreel skill: concept, script, narration, music, render and critique loop.
take: Script budget: about 220-255 Korean characters per 60 s, with 60-70% of the time spoken.
Measured TTS pace is about 5.5 characters per second on full sentences, 3-4.7 on short lines; trim short-line scripts 15-20%.
Critique with a 1-second contact sheet of the whole film, then 0.033-second frame bands on each key moment.
future_use: Script length budgeting per reel duration.

what_it_is: Remotion product-film skill: cuts placed on the soundtrack beat, built from the product's real screens.
take: Fast render ladder: stills first, then a half-size draft for review, and full size only after the user approves the draft.
Narration-led films place cuts by hand; the brief states that the cuts will not follow the music.
A sound sits on its beat; the picture may trail it by up to 3 frames.
future_use: Draft-before-final render ladder for any client reel.

what_it_is: Shot-language recipes from Apple and Linear launch films, rebuilt as HyperFrames HTML and GSAP.
take: Bundle the client's font file with @font-face; use Inter only when a system font cannot ship.
Adapt two layers only per recipe: the brand layer and the content layer, leaving the timing intact.
Run the recipe check and a draft render before handing a shot over.
future_use: Client font bundling for brand lower-thirds and end cards.

what_it_is: Claude skill turning a brand URL into a 40-second launch video with real site assets and voice-over.
take: One font family in weights 300-600 only; never bold 700 or heavier.
Every asset is checked frame by frame before use; no visual proof means no video.
Pacing is luxury: a 40 s film gives each feature time to breathe instead of rushing it.
future_use: Typography weight rule for client end cards and captions.

what_it_is: Turns before and after UI screenshots into an animated red-ink walkthrough video.
take: Brisk pacing: 2 to 3 seconds per change; first cuts are almost always too slow.
Hold the final state at least 2 seconds after the camera settles.
Never invent data: use user-supplied content, or flag placeholders in the delivery.
future_use: Before-and-after callouts for product-feature inserts.

what_it_is: Turns the user's own voice and real assets into a 20-60 second styled promo or explainer.
take: Hold on-screen reading text at least 0.8 s; hold the end card at least 1.5 s.
Stranger test per frame: would a passer-by stop here? Replace the weakest frame.
Fixed defaults: 9:16 at 720x1280 and 30 fps; keep user assets exactly as supplied.
future_use: Reading-hold and end-card timing for explainer inserts.

what_it_is: Motion-graphics skill pack covering briefs, beat timing, camera, audio mastering and review.
take: No whooshes on plain card slides or fades; reserve whooshes for big zooms and whip transitions.
Silence music and ambient effects for at least 60 ms before the hero hit so it lands clean.
Master about -14 LUFS (±0.5), true peak at or below -1.0 dBTP; voice stem near -16 LUFS; duck music at least 12 dB under speech.
future_use: Sound palette and mix levels for client reel sound effects.

what_it_is: Remotion app-store preview skills that scan a codebase and write bespoke scene files.
take: Phase gates: stop for user confirmation after extraction and again after creative direction, before writing scenes.
Cache extracted project context and ask the user to confirm it before any re-scan, saving tokens on repeat runs.
The first screenshot is the hero: put most of the effort there, since it is often the only one seen.
future_use: Cached client context so repeat reels skip re-scanning brand files.

what_it_is: Brief-to-render motion piece pipeline: several blind design drafts, then a critic-driven refinement loop.
take: Draft N directions that differ at the idea level, one per draw, so the options are genuinely different.
A blind selector picks among previews without knowing which draw is which, because the model could not reliably rank its own ideas.
The refinement loop runs until the critic reports CONVERGED: YES, with the critic keeping memory across rounds.
future_use: Blind comparison of hook variants for client reel openers.

what_it_is: Narrated product-demo pipeline that captures a live web app and renders a voiced video.
take: Two user gates: sign off the scene-by-scene script before capture, and review the first render at scene level.
Redact real data in the page before capture, and sweep final frames for visible secrets.
Report deltas against the approved script; never fake a capture, and renegotiate any beat that cannot be captured.
future_use: Script sign-off and delta reporting for client screen-demo inserts.

what_it_is: Interactive Claude skill for Remotion videos: strategy, expert panel, scene design, build and review.
take: Write a creative brief with duration in seconds and frames plus a scene table, and confirm it before building.
Cross-dissolve transitions run 8 to 12 frames between all scenes.
Lower music under data-heavy scenes and keep the voice clear.
future_use: Scene-table brief format for multi-shot client explainers.

what_it_is: Hyperframes skill that turns a project website into a short, shareable launch video.
take: Each line a viewer must read holds about 0.8 s once settled; a full sentence needs about 0.3 s per word.
Keep pace with motion and cuts, never with flashing text: fast in, then hold.
Keep the video at 15 to 25 seconds; add nothing longer without a reason.
future_use: Reading-time budget for on-screen disclaimers and CTA cards.

what_it_is: Director skill that turns evidence and narration into a product film with deterministic QA and claim checks.
take: Proof cards get a 0.5 s lead-in and a 1.5 s read hold by default.
Preflight runs source, claim and audio checks before any render; a failed check stops the build.
Bind every render to source hashes and integer frame boundaries so the same inputs give the same file.
future_use: Claim preflight for compliance-sensitive product or rate claims.

what_it_is: Two skills: narrated product videos cut from a talking take, and no-voice teasers cut to music.
take: A scene starts 0.3 s before its first word, or on a cut in the pause before it.
Light edit by default: cut restarts and false starts; trim pauses over about 1.1 s down to 0.7 s (0.9 s at a scene change).
Before rendering, check narration is near -16 LUFS, read the transcript, and look at the filmstrip.
future_use: Pause and restart trimming rules for every face-reel take.

what_it_is: Remotion skill for short column-sized web app onboarding loops that isolate one UI piece per beat.
take: Each onboarding beat is 3 to 8 seconds; the whole video rarely exceeds about 20 seconds.
Ask for 2 to 4 screenshots per view so interaction states come from real captures.
Make the last frame crossfade back to the first so the loop does not jar.
future_use: Column-sized feature loops for a client website section.

what_it_is: Claude skill that directs short mixed-media films from brief to storyboard, motion spec and HyperFrames build.
take: Show 2 to 3 options at every design decision; the user picks, so nothing is built on a single take.
Log each pick with its exact values in a decisions file; later sessions read that file, not the chat.
Version every review page and refuse to overwrite a previous version.
future_use: Decision log format for client reel learnings.

what_it_is: Cinematic product-video skill: 152 shot recipe cards, Remotion components and an audio library.
take: Key information must hold at least 1 s before the next cut; budget hold frames in the timeline up front.
With narration, duck background music to a gain of 0.12-0.18 (0.34 without voice) and keep SFX clear of speech.
Write the real TTS duration back into the storyboard and re-budget frames from it.
future_use: Music gain levels under voice-over for product explainers.

what_it_is: Node bridge that drives After Effects over WebSocket from Claude Code, with a headless simulator.
take: SKIP: it is a control bridge for After Effects, a tool this workspace does not use; nothing fits the talking-head pipeline.
Its batch command runs many edits in one round trip, a pattern useful only if an After Effects step is ever added.
future_use: Only if a client needs an After Effects deliverable.

what_it_is: Spanish-language Claude plugin that analyzes references and builds Remotion motion graphics locally.
take: Ask for everything missing in one message (format, duration, tone, brand, music) so the user answers once.
Frames per beat = 30 x 60 / BPM (120 BPM = 15 frames); snap cuts and entries to that grid.
The user approves the storyboard before any animation is built.
future_use: One-message intake and storyboard sign-off for client reels.

what_it_is: Product launch-video skill plus a Gemini TTS skill for voice-overs with style and pause control.
take: Intake covers product, audience, core message, tone, duration, assets, voice-over and where it will be posted, since posting context sets aspect and pacing.
Pause tags: [short pause] is about 0.5 s and [pause] about 1 s; use them to pace narration.
For a consistent multi-segment voice, join segments into one prompt with [3 second pause] markers, then split.
future_use: Intake checklist and voice-over pause tags for explainer inserts.

what_it_is: Workflow skill that turns a company URL into a 60-90 second SaaS demo with captured UI evidence.
take: Structure: hook in the first 3 to 6 s, product surface 6-18 s, primary action 18-34 s, result 34-48 s, CTA last.
Capture product screenshots at 2x device scale or higher and keep a manifest of each.
Show only features the captures prove; the QC list checks product accuracy first.
future_use: Long-form client product walkthroughs of 60-90 seconds.

what_it_is: Remotion skill whose defaults come from frame-level measurements of six Apple recap videos.
take: Typography is an accent: about 0.8 designer-set text events per 10 s; median text hold about 33 frames (1.1 s at 30 fps).
Cap height median 6.7% of frame height (p10 3.3%); most on-screen text is UI inside product shots.
Spring entries calibrated at damping 15.35, stiffness 115, mass 1; animated entries are visibly done in about 8 frames.
future_use: Overlay type sizes and hold times for product-feature inserts.

what_it_is: Three skills for ad creative: batch A/B variants, launch films and animated testimonials.
take: Ad anatomy with holds: hook 0-3 s, context 3-8 s, payoff 8-18 s, proof 18-25 s, CTA held at least 2 s.
Testimonials: quote the customer's exact words, never paraphrase, and attribute name, role and company.
Reveal quote lines in reading order about 6 to 10 frames apart, with one consistent motion.
future_use: Attributed client-quote cards, only with the client's exact words.

what_it_is: Website-to-brand-kit tool plus an Apple-style launch film template with a measured review loop.
take: Review the extracted brand before use: logo on light and dark grounds, accent, fonts and tagline must each be checked.
Use the fonts the page actually loaded; fall back to a named Google font only when the site does not serve them.
Measure each render's cuts, static runs, loudness and beat grid; write a report and a contact sheet.
future_use: Brand-kit review checklist for client intake and sign-off.

what_it_is: Claude-style product promo skill: terracotta or dark terminal demos built from captured real output.
take: Capture first: every number, path and output line in the video must come from a real captured run.
Run the props verifier against the capture before publishing.
Check each beat as a still before declaring the video done.
future_use: Traceable on-screen numbers for product or data claims.

what_it_is: HyperFrames animation skill with atomic rules, blueprints, transitions and runtime adapters.
take: Route by task: an index maps each motion goal to one rule file, so the agent reads only what the job needs.
Compose atomic rules first; load a multi-phase blueprint only when a scene needs one.
House default is power3.out for entrances; back.out is reserved for explicitly playful motion.
future_use: Index-first reference routing to cut reading tokens in builds.

what_it_is: Skill for 60-second landscape product demos with real UI captures, voice-over and beat-locked motion.
take: Voice-over pace about 2.7 words per second, roughly 165-180 words for 60 s, so the voice never goes quiet.
Show only features, names and numbers that appear in the product's own captures; no invented claims.
Mix to -14 LUFS with voice in front of the music; no frozen hold of 0.7 s or more before the last 0.5 s.
future_use: Words-per-second script budget and truth rule for client demos.

what_it_is: Two Claude skills rendering a 20 s iOS-app promo with a 3D phone, mascot and score on a Mac.
take: Check stills in at least two rounds, including mid-jump beats; the mascot must never cover information.
Target -13 to -15 dBFS on the score with 0% clipping, measured in the file.
Take feature facts from the user's repo (real strings and states only) and ask for missing design rather than inventing it.
future_use: 3D phone promo if a client ships a mobile app.

what_it_is: Claude plugin that drives a real app on screen, narrates it and renders a demo MP4 with Remotion.
take: Show the cost estimate and get approval before any paid generation; write the narration before any capture.
Write all narration first, then generate, so word changes do not trigger paid regeneration.
Look at frames during QA; there is no automatic visual check, and failed scenes are reported, not hidden.
future_use: Cost-estimate gate and narrate-first order for paid voice or video.

what_it_is: Remotion promo generator from a website URL, with intake questions and beat-locked music.
take: Intake batch before building: duration, audience, hero moment, goal, which numbers are safe to show, and what must not be claimed.
Beat-lock: detect onsets in the music and land the biggest hit on the payoff scene within 6 frames.
future_use: Intake question list for new client onboarding and claims checklist.

what_it_is: Agent skill turning sites, footage or data into brag, promo or explainer videos with sources.
take: sources.md records where every on-screen line came from; apply the same idea to trace every reel claim back to the transcript.
footage.py check gates: -14 LUFS within 1, true peak at or below -1.5 dBTP, exact frame count, no hold over 0.6 s.
future_use: Source-tracing sheet per reel for compliance review.

what_it_is: Skills for product demo, sale promo and photo slideshow videos from screenshots and images.
take: Ken Burns: zoom 1.0 to 1.12 or back, pan direction seeded per photo, easeInOutSine; past about 1.15 it reads as a crash zoom.
Crossfade 0.4 to 0.6 s with one transition type only; intro card 1.5 to 2 s; a photo held under 2.5 s feels rushed.
future_use: Client event recap or listing slideshow with one locked transition.

what_it_is: HyperFrames motion-design harness with anti-slop motion rules and readability timing.
take: Readability law: short labels settle for at least 0.8 s; body text holds at least 0.3 s per word.
Ban linear easing (ease none) except slow background rotations; no identical spring bounce on every element.
future_use: Hold-time check for on-screen captions and motion cards.

what_it_is: Remotion cinematic product promo skill: 157 shot recipe cards, template, beat-synced cuts.
take: Hold rules: a brand wordmark holds at least 1 s once settled; batch motion ends on a 0.5 s still; opening subject action gets at least 3 s.
Accelerating group motion works best with a physical metaphor (dealing cards) and a hard stop before the next beat.
future_use: Hold-time budget for end-card and stat reveals.

what_it_is: Claude Code plugin making hype videos from an app, site or repo, rendered on macOS.
take: Plan mode writes DIRECTION.md and SCRIPT.md first, every dial with its reason; the user approves before any build.
Every fact on screen carries a source from the product; anything unknown is marked unknown, never invented.
future_use: Approval-first treatment doc before any reel build.

what_it_is: Code-built vertical motion graphics for any brand, with brand kit, timing sheet and synthesized sound.
take: One idea per scene with on-screen text held at least 2 s; long pieces split into 5 to 15 s chapters.
Pre-delivery pass: frame count and fps, -14 LUFS, audio-visual sync, banned words, unreleased numbers, em-dashes.
future_use: Brand kit file pattern plus a text check for client-restricted words.

what_it_is: Remotion launch-film method: study a reference, show the real UI, split the logo into moving parts.
take: Measure the reference first (fps, shot list, zoom scale, hold lengths) and write NOTES.md before touching any scene.
Measured failure: white headline over a bright backdrop read at contrast 1.13 to 1.37:1 in places; check contrast per region.
future_use: Product UI launch film if a client ever has an app to show.

what_it_is: Claude and Codex plugin routing motion templates and paid media generation behind spend and plan gates.
take: Plan gate: open the storyboard and asset review before any paid image or video call; show first-frame anchors before paid video.
Motion-ui: decelerate every move and clear the blur; a key phrase staggers in, then the group slows and holds readable.
future_use: Pre-spend plan gate for any AI B-roll request.

what_it_is: Cinematic product video skill: 157 shot recipe cards, Remotion template, beat sync and sound.
take: 3D-perspective UI: rasterize at native size, then scale down; blurry text means the texture resolution chain needs fixing.
Deterministic render: ban Date.now and Math.random; fix every pseudo-random seed.
future_use: Shot-card vocabulary for motion-card transitions.

what_it_is: Fork of the video-shotcraft library (152 shot cards) with the same production rules.
take: Check each sound effect in the rendered file, not the preview: previews clamp volume to 1.0 and hide clipping or masking.
Any sample over 5 s needs an explicit durationInFrames so the sound does not ring after the action ends.
future_use: Final-render sound check for any future motion piece.

what_it_is: Scripts calling the Muse API for AI images and 10-second talking videos on a user subscription.
take: Check the weekly allowance before any spend: a video costs about 2 to 3% of a free-plan week, an image 0 to 1%.
Chain outputs by assetId instead of re-uploading; run independent jobs in parallel and poll asynchronously.
future_use: Cost estimate and asset chaining for AI B-roll, only after a yes.

what_it_is: Skill for 20 to 25 s match-cut brand films built from 30 to 40 generated stills sharing one arc.
take: Cut lengths follow a curve: about 1 s, then 0.55, 0.4, 0.3 s, then 5 to 6 frames, then a 4 s calm resolve.
No shot under 5 frames at 25 fps; shorter cuts read as flicker rather than cuts.
future_use: Brand montage or intro for a client's end-card reveal.

what_it_is: CLI and skill that records real browser tasks and renders short narrated walkthrough videos.
take: Verify the export: decode every frame, check presentation timestamps, and sample the encoded MP4 rather than the source.
Keep the take, edit decisions and HTML composition local so a text change re-renders without re-recording.
future_use: Re-render a finished reel after a text change, without re-shooting.

what_it_is: Code-generated promo reels (canvas, ffmpeg, numpy audio) for a person, product or catalog.
take: Nothing made up: every price, colour or feature traces to the website or store API; anything unconfirmed is flagged pending.
Preload every font face before render, or early frames fall back to a system font; review a frame sheet before the full render.
Voice-over ducks the music and effects by about 10 dB; loudness target -14 LUFS.
future_use: Batch reels if a client supplies a product list.

what_it_is: Skill building frame-accurate product demos from an approved storyboard, walkthrough or motion design.
take: Camera moves last 1.0 to 1.6 s on cubic-bezier(0.45,0,0.2,1); linger at least 0.5 s before leaving a framing.
Captions: one line of about 9 words or fewer, on screen at least 1 s plus 0.3 s per word; payoff moments stay still.
future_use: Storyboard approval step and caption wording rules for any reel.

what_it_is: Remotion marketing film method: reference measurement, 3D device stage, AI B-roll and sound design.
take: Three audio layers: music bed 0.18 to 0.70 on a volume curve; transition impacts 0.55 to 0.65; tactile UI 0.04 to 0.45, never competing with voice.
Measure a sound's real attack in 100 ms slices with volumedetect; a whoosh that peaks at 0.5 s will bloom late if placed on the cut.
AI B-roll: stills first, a human approval gate, then image-to-video; one story, one cast, one grade.
future_use: Sound-layer levels now; 3D device stage for future product films.

what_it_is: Skill producing a 45 to 60 s scored product demo from a repo, with VO timing and music ducking.
take: Write the voice-over with timecodes first; TTS compresses long pause tags (a 2.6 s tag came back at about 1.4 s), so retime after generation.
Retime each line from silencedetect boundaries, then trim and delay each line to its timecode before mixing.
future_use: Line-by-line VO retiming for a narrated explainer.

what_it_is: Agent skill for planning, building and rendering Remotion marketing and product videos.
take: Loudness targets: voice about -16 LUFS, music under voice -24 to -20 LUFS, true peak below -1 dBTP.
Reading times: short labels at least 1.2 s, headline copy at least 2 s; change scene every 2 to 5 s unless the piece is deliberately slow.
future_use: Loudness and reading-time reference for client reels.

what_it_is: Remotion product film skill with shot tables, jitter checks and 152 shot recipe cards.
take: Delete any slow move under 0.02 px per frame: it reads as jitter, not camera motion; use an entrance animation for life instead.
