Jitter check: render the same static region at four consecutive frames; on a hold the hashes must match.
Give each scene's last beat 0.7 to 1.3 s to settle; do not leave a second idle second.
future_use: Static-hold jitter check for motion cards before final render.

what_it_is: Beat-synced app promo reels with ACE-Step music, HyperFrames render, critique loop and -14 LUFS.
take: Motion classes with fixed eases: micro 0.18 s, panel 0.55 s, headline 0.35 s then 1.0 s hold, icon 0.32 s; entrances 0.3 to 0.6 s.
read_check warns when a caption is on screen for less than max(0.8 s, 0.3 s per word).
Critique: a fresh subagent that did not make the video scores the frames; fix the worst three; at most three rounds.
future_use: Motion-class tokens and reading-time check for every new reel.

what_it_is: Desktop video studio driven by a coding agent: React scenes, timeline and MP4 export.
take: Verify each video: compile check, then capture first, middle and last frames and look at them; a passing check can still be an ugly frame.
Route first: one owner skill per video type; never stitch two owners together.
future_use: Routing rule for choosing a reel format per client request.

what_it_is: Chat-based skill turning static ads into hand-built or lead-up videos through the MaxFusion MCP.
take: Gate 0 always asks which treatment the user wants; recommend one from the image but never assume it.
Realism rule: a real hand with correct anatomy and contact shadows; stepped or stop-motion motion fails review.
future_use: Static social ad to video, only with an approved paid generation.

what_it_is: 30 free HyperFrames motion templates with variable-driven rebranding and rendering.
take: Keep all copy and colours in variables: a rebrand is a JSON values file applied by script, not hand edits to the HTML.
For product shots, generate the photo on a flat #00FF00 screen and key it out.
future_use: Variable-driven templates for end cards and lower thirds.

what_it_is: Claude skill rendering product reels and launch films in Remotion with rebuilt UI, cursor and sound.
take: Motion taste: one thing moves at a time, everything eases, at most one bounce; sound stays soft and sits under the picture.
Audio references: ask the user for sounds they like, store them with licence notes, and match levels with short and long windows.
Ask before downloading any logo; find the official vector and never trace a raster logo without asking.
future_use: Reference-sound brief for a client; check the Remotion licence for an agency.

what_it_is: Single-HTML film skill: render(t) timeline, synthesized score, frame-exact 1080p60 MP4 export.
take: Storyboard table first: scene id, start and end in seconds, the one thing the viewer must understand, and the beat it lands on.
Export frame by frame rather than in real time, so a slow machine still gives exact timing.
future_use: Storyboard table format for any scripted explainer.

what_it_is: Demo and guide video skills: plan first, record app or site, brand tokens, optional narration.
take: Brand tokens from a website: card is the page's light background; ink is the darkest text colour clearing 4.5:1 on that card.
Concept gate: PLAN.md and SCRIPT.md are approved before anything is recorded; every spoken word is listed in playing order.
future_use: Brand-contrast extraction and plan-first gate for client reels.

what_it_is: Records narrated, captioned demo videos of app flows in Playwright or on iOS with Maestro.
take: Ask first what goes in the video: voice-over, step captions, pointer, motion graphics, frame; each choice sets one switch.
Supersample: record at 2560x1440 and downscale for a crisp phone-size MP4.
future_use: Intake checklist of on-screen elements for a client flow demo.

what_it_is: Code-rendered motion reels with beat-synced music and checks; Chinese-language skill.
take: Energy rule: something new every 2 to 4 s, hook in the first 2 s; minimum text 36 px body and 24 px fine print at 1080 short edge.
Critique gate: score eight criteria out of 10, fix the three worst, repeat until each is 8 or more, at most three rounds.
Its ad-law list bans absolute words (best, first, 100%) and promised outcomes; use as a draft checklist, not as law.
future_use: Absolute-claim checklist as a draft pass before compliance review.

what_it_is: Records zoom-composited web app demos with ElevenLabs narration and aligned captions.
take: Hold on screen equals sentence duration plus about 1.2 s; sync narration by padding silences rather than stretching the video.
Spot-check each sentence start on the final render: the screen must already show what the sentence is about.
Keep focus zooms to 2 to 5 per video and return to a wide shot after every submit.
future_use: Sentence-to-screen check for B-roll inserted over a talking head.

what_it_is: Local-first AI film studio with shot plans, characters and asset generation via Codex or Claude Code.
take: The agent, not a script, inspects generated sheets and chooses crop boxes; check every slice before accepting it.
Each set uses a fixed palette and a consistency reference image in every generation request.
future_use: Character and palette consistency for future AI B-roll.

what_it_is: Codex and Claude Code plugin editing Diffusion Studio projects through local MCP tools.
take: SKIP: a thin wrapper over a desktop editor's MCP tools; the only transferable step is checking the connection before editing.
Not for talking-head reels now.
future_use: Only if editing moves into Diffusion Studio.

what_it_is: Validates a brief.json for timing and copy before rendering motion graphics in HyperFrames or Remotion.
take: Validate before render: beat durations sum to the length, copy stays verbatim, and the closing line holds at least 2.0 s to be readable.
Frame 0 must not be empty (it is the social thumbnail); copy that is transparent at its check time fails as copy_not_visible.
future_use: Pre-render brief check for every motion card and end card.

what_it_is: Hosted MCP server for storyboard, character and video generation billed in credits.
take: SKIP: a paid hosted generation service with no reusable local rules; generation needs an explicit yes and a budget first.
Only the cost-limit idea (spend caps on keys) is worth noting.
future_use: AI storyboard and first-frame generation only if approved and budgeted.

what_it_is: Turns a website URL into a 60 s demo video with zooms, cursor, captions and optional voice.
take: Script budget: 550 to 750 characters for a 45 to 57 s video; every number or claim must appear on the site itself.
Pre-roll about 0.4 s before a line and post-roll about 0.35 s after; check the voice is never cut at a scene change.
future_use: Claim-traceable script budget for any screen-led client demo.

what_it_is: Claude Code plugin making brand marketing reels and ads from HTML scenes rendered via headless Chrome.
take: Hook is the first second: open on the outcome, problem or surprise, never on a logo, title card or empty frame.
Ask at most 2-3 questions per message, each with options; show a still of each option before asking follow-ups.
Pitch 2-3 ideas in one line each, recommend one, and check each idea against a reel-quality rules table before building.
future_use: Client intake questions and idea-pitch step before any reel is built.

what_it_is: Claude Code and Codex skill that builds music-synced app launch films as code, with a plan-approval gate.
take: Viewer test: a stranger should have the product name and its one-sentence promise within about 3 seconds, over the working product.
Approve a scenario table (seconds, music, picture, exact copy) before any build; changing a table costs minutes, a film costs hours.
After render, flag any span over about 1 second where the picture barely changes; a long static end card counts as a fix.
future_use: Approval-first plan step and static-span check for any reel with a long hold.

what_it_is: Playwright-driven deterministic 60fps app demo videos with a Pillow compositor and a virtual camera.
take: Zoom in once per shot and hold through the action; do not over-zoom, since tight zoom loses context and blurs.
Let the camera settle for a short hold after each move before the next action starts.
Decouple the camera from the cursor: panning to follow a pointer looks erratic, so move between fixed focus points.
future_use: Punch-in discipline for face reels: one push per shot, hold, no over-zoom.

what_it_is: Claude Code skill that writes product launch videos as code, storyboard first, with a reviewer pass.
take: Nothing fades in: things change shape, slide or wipe; avoid crossfades and blur-ins.
No hold longer than about one second unless the hold is the point; dead time reads as amateur.
One camera move at a time; never zoom in and out back to back. Mix audio to -14 LUFS.
future_use: Motion-graphic beats and cutaways: no fades, short holds, one move at a time.

what_it_is: Agent skill turning one topic into a Vox-style paper-collage explainer using Atlas Cloud image and video APIs.
take: Cut every 4-6 seconds: shots run 3-6 s and never past about 7 s, or AI motion goes dead.
Split each beat into two shots (wide, then detail); the first headline must land as a hook within 3 seconds.
Lock the look in the still-image step and add motion after, so approve keyframes before paying for any video.
future_use: Shot cadence rule for cutaway B-roll; paid video only after a keyframe approval.

what_it_is: Claude skills for planning and coding 3Blue1Brown-style math animations in Manim Community and ManimGL.
take: Pacing: write a formula in 1-2 s then wait 2-3 s; highlight one term for 0.5 s then wait 1 s before moving on.
Write scenes.md (hook, arc, scene list, palette) before any code, then implement scene by scene.
Transform objects instead of replacing them; use ReplacementTransform when chaining so no ghost mobjects remain.
future_use: Math or formula explainers, if a future client needs an educational series.

what_it_is: Free local explainer-video generator: on-device voice, Whisper word timing, Chrome-drawn frames, ffmpeg MP4.
take: Cut recordings: a pause of 0.6 s or more is trimmed to 0.25 s; shorter pauses (0.3 s) and quiet filler sounds can be caught too.
A word keeps trailing sound up to 0.4 s, so word endings are not clipped when pauses are cut.
Review each auto-marked cut by ear before rendering, especially sounds flagged as possibly holding a word end.
future_use: Silence and filler trimming on raw talking-head takes, using word-time cut lists.

what_it_is: Desktop motion-design studio where Claude builds videos stage by stage, with human approval gates.
take: Rules live in code, not the prompt: a submission is refused when a check fails, and only the human can approve a gate.
Final pass: a frame sheet at about one frame per second, three full frames at the busiest moments, loudness -14 LUFS and true peak -1 dBTP.
When a real mistake is pointed out, the session proposes a new automatic check so the same error cannot pass twice.
future_use: Compliance checks written as code in each client's QA gate, not left to the prompt.

what_it_is: Chinese finance-explainer skill with a presenter-on-camera mode: evidence hangs behind the speaker.
take: Talking-head mode: the presenter is the ground. Evidence hangs on the wall behind her; detail shrinks into a circle or vertical window, then grows back to full frame.
Drive every shot from the presenter's own word timestamps; align the transcript word by word and check it against the speaker's words.
Plan each shot with a presenter-position column: room, wall, world swap, vertical window, circle window, or away from camera.
future_use: Shot table with a presenter-position column for every talking-head face reel.

what_it_is: Chinese Claude skill for code-made Remotion videos, with MiniMax and Edge TTS narration scripts.
take: SKIP: generic Remotion basics (interpolate, spring, Sequence) and TTS scripts; no reusable reel rule and no licence stated.
Gotcha worth remembering: a Python script that writes TypeScript through an f-string emitted a literal backslash-n, so generated code needs real newlines.
future_use: Only if we ever build data-driven Remotion videos in batch.

what_it_is: Chinese hand-drawn explainer skill: stroke-by-stroke whiteboard video or programmatic animation with real MP4 checks.
take: Time shots from real audio: use valid timestamps or forced alignment; an even split of time must never be called word-aligned.
Keep exact text (dates, names, figures) as a deterministic text layer added after generation, never drawn by an image model.
Verify one representative clip (faces, pen lifts, subtitles, the final frame) before rendering the whole batch.
future_use: Verify-one-clip-first gate and deterministic text layers for non-face explainer formats.

what_it_is: Claude Design skill: one-screen blueprint animations that explain UX decisions step by step, without cutting.
take: One continuous shot in 3-6 numbered steps; each step explains a single design decision, so the viewer sees why.
A scan line turns the real UI into a blueprint; only the changed parts rebuild, then a second sweep reveals the result.
future_use: UX before-and-after explainers for software clients; ideas only (non-commercial licence).

what_it_is: Chinese math-tutor skill: solves a problem, writes HTML, and makes a narrated Manim video timed to keywords.
take: Anchor animation to narration keywords (2-6 characters) using TTS sync points, not hard-coded seconds.
Order the work: storyboard, then narration audio, then read back the real timestamps, then write animation code.
Leave a 0.2-0.4 s visual pause after each key conclusion; never pad a scene with a wait calculated from its duration.
future_use: Keyword-anchored overlay and caption timing in talking-head reels.

what_it_is: Agent skill for Vox-style collage explainers on the MuAPI platform: topic, talking-head or photo modes, paid APIs.
take: Make each beat a finished collage poster first; animate only approved stills so credits go to approved frames.
Reuse one fixed style block verbatim on every beat; vary only the scene, background colour and headline.
Pick shot size and camera move from a short fixed vocabulary, never free-form, so motion stays consistent.
future_use: Cutaway B-roll style, only with a user-approved generation budget.

what_it_is: Code-built narrated documentary films: one camera move over one designed board, timed to the voice.
take: Time the whole film with a free scratch voice first; the film re-times itself when the final voice lands.
Lint the beat table before building: chronology, line length, and digits in spoken text (spell numbers out for TTS).
Split whole-section takes into one clip per line and flag suspicious cuts automatically.
future_use: Scratch-voice timing and beat-table lint for any narrated film.

what_it_is: Chinese skill turning a 15-60 s narration into a styled HTML animation with subtitles, seven visual styles.
take: Write a change list per shot (entrance, main action, secondary motion, exit), with a visible change every 2-3 seconds.
Use at least three transition kinds, and never let the same kind appear three times in a row.
Approve three static frames before rendering the full video; subtitle highlights use exact word matches only.
future_use: Static-frame approval gate and per-shot change list before rendering any multi-shot reel.

what_it_is: Claude Code skill rendering chalkboard-style explainer videos with pen drawing synced to a local voice.
take: Estimate length before recording: quick explainer is about words / 3 + beats x 0.15 + 1.3 s; tutorial about words / 2.9 + beats x 0.6 + 1.3 s.
To hit a target length, change the words, not the speaking rate; the render prints the real length for checking.
After rendering, read the contact sheet and each beat frame to confirm every highlight lands on the intended spot.
future_use: Script length estimates before a talking-head take, to avoid re-recording.

what_it_is: Chinese voice-to-video Remotion skill: animates a script or recording using a shot-by-shot orchestration plan.
take: Write a short shot table before building: time, meaning, main focus, one main effect, supporting transition, reading window.
Hold a settled on-screen number about 1.6-3.5 s so it can be read; give a line of evidence text about 5-8.5 s.
Make a 15-20 second sample first; expand to the full length only after the user confirms clarity and continuity.
future_use: Reading-window timing for on-screen stats and evidence in face reels.

what_it_is: Pipeline for vertical explainers: TTS, caption alignment, Remotion render, and a hash-bound final release gate.
take: Release gate loudness: integrated -14 +/-1.5 LUFS, loudness range at most 8 LU, true peak at most -1.5 dBTP, near-silence at most 45%.
Require exactly one video stream and one stereo 48 kHz audio stream, with audio covering the video timeline within 0.25 s.
Bind the review receipt to the exact final MP4; any re-export invalidates the receipt and needs a new review.
future_use: Automated final-MP4 gate before any face reel is delivered to a client.

what_it_is: Five Claude skills for explainer videos: scripts, storyboards, diagrams, whiteboard, isometric and recap videos.
take: Script first: the voiceover is the spine and visuals illustrate the line being spoken, never lead it.
Reveal diagrams in order: nodes, then edges, then labels; hold each step 0.5-1.5 s so it lands.
Dim non-active items to about 0.35 opacity while one is highlighted, and lift along Z rather than scaling to fake height.
future_use: Highlight and reveal timing for explainer overlays and diagram beats.

what_it_is: Vox-style animated ad and explainer skill driving video generation through MCP, with script approval gates.
take: Cap the pre-script research pass: snippets only, under 5 tool calls, so the script carries specific facts without bloat.
Chain generated clips by passing the last frame of one clip as the reference for the next, and verify the reference is attached.
Explainer mode sells nothing: no call to action by default, and the video ends on an insight.
future_use: Research budget and no-CTA explainer mode for compliance-heavy mortgage topics.

what_it_is: Codex and Claude skill with 86 visual styles: recommends three, shows reference posters, then builds a 20-second sample first.
take: Three-step gate: user picks one of three styles shown as real reference images, then approves a 20-second sample, then the full film.
A sample must be a real 18-22 s animation with narrative beats; a slideshow of static images does not count as a sample.
Load a style's detailed guide only after that style is chosen, which keeps the working context small.
future_use: Style-choice gate and sample-first flow for non-face motion projects.

what_it_is: Chinese skill turning a process into a narrated, crayon-style state-chart video with a poster per chapter.
take: Lint blank paper: flag a scene where more than about 38% is empty (about 55% for loose themes such as pen or linen).
Generate narration per sentence with a noise gate and an ASR check, cache each line, so editing one sentence redoes only that line.
Review a contact sheet of stills at each step before the full render.
future_use: Per-sentence voice caching and contact-sheet still review for any reel.

what_it_is: Codex and Claude skill for fact-checked, cinematic Blender education videos with strict visual QA.
take: Reject any frame at 100% zoom with flat materials, alpha-dither noise, implausible scale, or floating parts before showing approval.
Tag every claim verified, inferred or conceptual; qualify inferred or conceptual statements in narration or subtitles.
future_use: Fact-status tagging for engineering or product explainers, if a client needs them.

what_it_is: Markdown-to-video skill: a paged markdown script becomes a Remotion explainer built from fixed scene templates.
take: Pick a fixed scene type first (Title, ContentCard, TwoColumn, BeforeAfter, Outro); write custom code only when none fits.
Reserve custom scenes for things templates cannot do, such as simulations or data charts, and keep text cards on templates.
future_use: Scene-template approach for text-card beats in longer explainers.

what_it_is: Hosted service skill that turns text or documents into narrated hand-drawn explainer videos.
take: Narration tempo cap: a pitch-preserving speed-up of up to about 1.08x, and never clip narration to hit a target length.
It uploads content to a remote service, which conflicts with our local-only rule; use only with the user's explicit approval.
future_use: Only if a client approves a hosted service; the tempo cap idea is reusable.

what_it_is: MuAPI-based 3D curiosity-loop explainer shorts: anatomy shots, character sheets, cloned voice and FFmpeg zooms.
take: Curiosity-loop script: every sentence opens a question the viewer wants answered, with the hook landing in the first 3 seconds.
Shots run 2-4 seconds, two per beat (wide establishing, then close detail); never hold one shot longer than 4 seconds.
Impact zoom on key beats, and music ducked by -18 dB under narration.
future_use: Curiosity-loop hooks for face reels; 3D shots only with approved spend.

what_it_is: Claude Code skill turning an arXiv paper into a narrated, fact-checked explainer with a verification report.
take: Tie every number and claim to a verbatim quote or table row, and check each one mechanically against the source text.
The writer and the verifier must be different contexts: the verifier runs in a fresh subagent, and the fix loop stops after three rounds.
Check every on-screen string the renderer actually drew, not only the script, so text added late is verified too.
future_use: Traceability check: every on-screen claim in a face reel traced to the transcript.

what_it_is: Generates 3Blue1Brown-style Manim explainers from topics or slide decks, with audience and domain presets.
take: Pacing: a first-time equation gets 1-2 s to write and 2-3 s to read before anything else happens.
Gotchas: Create() on text traces outlines, so use Write() for text; use ReplacementTransform when chaining transforms.
future_use: Math or science explainers, if a future client needs them.

what_it_is: Agent skill and Remotion engine packaging talking-head clips into finance-style explainers, with a layout library.
take: Subject fills at least 60% of frame width or 55% of height; at least a third of scenes crop the subject at an edge.
Insert one white-paper scene for every two or three dark scenes; on white scenes place a circular picture-in-picture at bottom right.
At most two labels per frame; highlight the item being spoken, dim the rest, and keep the camera at zoom 1.12 or more.
Keep the subtitle band (bottom 905-960 px of 1080) clear of graphics, picture-in-picture and watermarks.
future_use: Layout rules for B-roll cards and overlays around the talking head.

what_it_is: Claude skill for code-driven Remotion motion explainers, with a hero-frame-first build and QC evidence.
take: Build the hero frame first: compose the frame with the most information, check hierarchy and spacing, then split it into actors.
When narration exists, human-verified subtitles are the timing authority; never invent numbers or product behaviour.
Keep the same on-screen objects across shots so the viewer tracks one thing changing state, not a series of new slides.
future_use: Continuity rules for product or concept overlays in face reels.

what_it_is: Installer and skill making 10-second knowledge clips in 16 styles, with a three-second sample picker first.
take: Make a 3-second sample for each candidate style before any full build; the user picks one, then the full clip follows.
Check the finished clip at its beginning, middle and end frames for overlapping text, off-frame elements and a conclusion that does not fill the frame.
User-supplied references are treated as one more candidate, judged alongside the built-in styles in the same picker.
future_use: Sample-picker gate before any full build of a new face-reel style.

what_it_is: Spanish-language Claude skill making 9:16 Vox-style shorts from a topic, using ElevenLabs and Kie APIs.
take: Use 4-6 scenes of about 30-45 seconds in hook, development, payoff-with-CTA order, all in one scene JSON file.
Slide-and-bounce motion with no fades, and cut-out cartoon images on a paper texture.
Store brand colours, channel tag and voice once at onboarding so every video reuses them.
future_use: Cut-out cartoon style for vertical explainers, only if a client asks for it.

what_it_is: Chinese 9:16 code-animated talking explainer skill: dialogue TTS, global Whisper alignment, final MP4 QA.
take: Run one global Whisper pass on the final-speed audio and map the corrected on-screen text onto its timings; Whisper sets time, not wording.
Check transitions at their midpoint: no blank frame, no black flash, and both scenes must cover the full canvas.
Re-extract key frames from the encoded final MP4 (H.264, 1080x1920, 24 fps, AAC 48 kHz), not the browser preview, and check for black frames and silence.
future_use: Final encoded-MP4 QA and subtitle-timing rules for every face reel.

what_it_is: HyperFrames HTML explainer pipeline with narration, music and mixing on NeuralDeep models.
take: Re-time scenes from the real voiceover length before laying out HTML; never plan timing from the script alone.
Transcribe each generated TTS line and diff it against the script: TTS swallows or swaps words, e.g. 'reuse' came out as 'ray use'.
Keep word-level timings in a words file so captions highlight each word as it is spoken.
future_use: Voice QA: transcribe and diff every generated narration line before use.

what_it_is: Chinese 16:9 HyperFrames explainer skill: script to lint, preview and render, with knowledge-card layouts.
take: One main graphic per beat, at most one accent; all text stays inside a 64 px safe margin.
Map each beat's core image to a graphic family and motion: growth to rising bars, chaos to scattered drift.
Keep the kicker fixed in one corner (left 80 px, top 64 px), separate from the centred text block.
future_use: 16:9 explainer graphics; beat-to-graphic mapping for B-roll cards.

what_it_is: Remotion motion-graphics skill with locked style tokens, voice-timed words and loudness-checked audio.
take: Stagger words 4-5 frames apart, never all at once; exit frames must be fewer than enter frames.
Hold each text state at least 0.8 s plus 0.25 s per word before it changes.
Run a style check: ink and accent contrast, at most two text lines, font size hierarchy.
Check overlaps on decoded export frames, not only on debug boxes.
future_use: Text-card hold timing and overlap QA for motion overlays.

what_it_is: GSAP and SVG explainer toolkit with a seven-phase build path, retention pass and overlap auditor.
take: Retention: last content beat at 70-85% of each scene's length, no dead zone over 4 s, first beat within 0.5 s.
The hook must close by name at the peak; a kicker that could caption any scene is a label, not a re-hook.
Run an overlap audit at 0.5 s steps and whitelist only the overlaps that are intended.
future_use: Hook and pacing audit for reel scripts and motion cards.

what_it_is: Six-stage YouTube video workflow: topic, script, TTS, timed storyboard, images and MP4 assembly.
take: Keep an invalidation table: a narration edit re-aligns audio, storyboard and images; one bad image re-reviews only itself and the cut.
Stale to-do items in a handoff are not instructions; check the files on disk before acting on them.
Name storyboard frames by number plus start timestamp, so a re-timed storyboard is a clearly versioned set.
future_use: Scoped re-render plans for revisions of reels.

what_it_is: Vox-style editorial collage skill: layered paper assets, code-drawn text and strict visual evidence checks.
take: Fail any scene where only captions or labels move; motion must come from separate actors in the picture.
Phone-size review: downsample to about 360 px wide and check the subject is not a postage stamp.
Each transition declares an inherited anchor (material, object, rail, colour or motion) or an explicit intentional reset.
future_use: Transition continuity and phone-size checks for collage inserts.

what_it_is: Portuguese Three.js space and science short-video studio with gated scripts and draft-then-final renders.
take: Write an idea-to-device table: one row per spoken idea, each with its own picture that shows the mechanism.
One stage only: new things enter on top of what is already on screen, so the viewer never has to reorient.
Each shot introduces one new thing and lasts 0.9-1.8 s.
Gate script, plan and draft for approval; show the cost before any paid final voice.
future_use: Idea-to-device planning for B-roll cutaways in reels.

what_it_is: Skill for Vox-style animated maps: camera zooms, drawn routes, dropped pins and region highlights.
take: Animate graphic overlays on a 12 fps step inside a 24 or 30 fps edit: STEP = round(fps / 12), base footage stays smooth.
Drop pins on a spring with overshoot; fade labels in only after the pin lands.
Frame geography with fitSize or fitExtent instead of hand-tuned scale and translate values.
future_use: Place or route beats if a reel covers provinces or borders.

what_it_is: Chinese narration-video director workflow: visual planning, a style library and reviewed iterations for HyperFrames or Remotion.
take: Keep a guidance layer only if it beats a plain brief: compare a plain brief (A), a style card (B) and the full workflow (C) on the same input.
Retire guidance once a newer model makes the same judgments without it.
Discover installed skills and tools before building, and match each one to the shot it serves.
future_use: A/B testing which skill instructions earn their tokens.

what_it_is: Claude skill that turns a topic into a hand-drawn whiteboard MP4 with an approved script and chosen voice.
take: Get the script approved before drawing anything: one idea per scene, one sentence per caption line.
Budget by length: about 140 words per minute once pauses count, so 60 s is 130-145 words.
Audition voices cheaply: render one representative sentence in 2-4 candidate voices and pick by ear.
future_use: Cheap voice audition before paid TTS in any format.

what_it_is: Agent-written GSAP HTML page, recorded in headless Chromium and merged with free Edge TTS narration.
take: Cache voiceover MP3s by sha256(voice + text), so re-renders with the same script skip TTS.
Measure each segment's audio duration and pass it to the page, so animation timing follows the narration.
The page sets a done flag and the recorder waits for it, instead of using a fixed timer.
future_use: Hash-cached TTS and duration-driven timing for any reel.

what_it_is: Codex skill: approved image-model hero frames, layers extracted from them, animated in HyperFrames.
take: Three approval gates: narration and storyboard; real stills with cost and maximum attempts; the encoded preview.
Inspect every still at full resolution before extracting layers; animate only the one or two focal layers.
Keep text out of image generation; add typography only after the exact text list is approved.
future_use: Credit-gated image generation for B-roll stills.

what_it_is: Korean whiteboard explainer engine: one storyboard rendered in eight hand-drawn styles, no GPU needed.
take: The storyboard fixes what, where and when; the style fixes how it looks, so one storyboard re-renders in any style.
Limit each scene to 12 elements, text at 28 px or larger, and keep the caption strip clear.
Preview one scene across several styles before rendering the whole video.
future_use: Storyboard-to-style split for multi-format explainers.

what_it_is: Remotion skill turning a web article into a 1080p video with harvested figures and a storyboard.
take: Size narration at 4.3 syllables per second (about 258 Chinese characters per minute).
Do not read on-screen text aloud: keep only titles and numbers on screen, and let the narration add what the picture does not show.
Cap zoom at about 1.25x for moves of 4 s or more and 1.6x for short moves, to keep images sharp.
future_use: Narration length budgeting and the text-versus-voice split.

what_it_is: Chinese HTML and GSAP HyperFrames toolkit for tutorial videos, with a reviewer checklist and shared blocks.
take: Visuals should extend the spoken idea with a metaphor or data, not repeat the caption word for word.
Scenes must not add their own exit animation; the transition belongs to the framework.
Claude-orange body text on cream #F7F2EA fails contrast; choose a darker text colour.
future_use: Composition review checklist for any HyperFrames build.

what_it_is: Chinese book-review video generator: LLM script, storyboard images, TTS, subtitles and ffmpeg assembly.
take: Optional assets fail soft: a missing BGM or transition sound drops out and the video still renders.
Word-level TTS timestamps drive subtitle timing; fall back to duration estimates when the engine gives none.
Crop watermarks off AI-generated images before compositing.
future_use: Graceful degradation and subtitle timing fallbacks for batch video.

what_it_is: Chinese knowledge-video skill: research, script, design, original illustration, narration and review gates.
take: Caption cues: at 42 px, no more than about 26 Chinese characters per cue as a conservative limit, split at phrase boundaries.
Type scale for explanatory graphics: headings 54-76 px, explanatory text 32-40 px, supporting text 26-30 px.
A finished script does not show the video works; review the picture separately.
future_use: Caption cue length and type scale for on-screen text.

what_it_is: Chinese Codex and Remotion tutorial-video skill with six confirmation steps and a talking-head mode.
take: Talking-head mode keeps the original audio and shows the speaker in a small window throughout, with one-line captions.
Report three states separately: generated, technically checked, user-confirmed; never promote a status without evidence.
Reuse a confirmed sample's shots and timing for the full cut instead of rebuilding them.
future_use: Talking-head layout and status tracking for reel QA.

what_it_is: Vertical 1080x1920 paper-collage explainer pipeline: research, narration, cut-out animation, captions and mix.
take: Never open a beat on an empty frame: the primary element is on screen by about 0.1 s.
Depth planes move at different speeds: ground 0.05, mid subjects 0.6-0.8, front confetti 1.0, headline 1.15.
Burn captions as PNG overlays rather than a subtitle filter, for portability.
Never hold a freeze frame to fill time; regenerate the shot instead.
future_use: Hook timing and depth-layer parallax for vertical B-roll.

what_it_is: Codex skill for Vox-style paper-collage videos: ImageGen stills, HyperFrames motion and MiniMax narration.
take: Keep titles, numbers and captions out of image-model output; add typography in post so text stays correct.
Do not use AI image-to-video unless the user explicitly asks; default to deterministic motion on approved stills.
Approve the beat map (Gate 1) and the visual identity (Gate 2) before any asset is generated.
future_use: Credit-safe asset plan for B-roll stills.

what_it_is: Manim animation skill with voiceover, pinned requirements, frame verification and MP4 delivery.
take: Use GIFs only for layout checks; deliver MP4 at high quality, since aggressive re-encoding crushes gradients.
Rate review findings: P0 wrong fact or unreadable core message, P1 layout that confuses the story, P2 polish.
Extract frames from the actual render and review them against the storyboard before delivery.
future_use: Severity triage and frame-review checklist for QA.

what_it_is: Claude skill for narrated infographic films: sourced research, ElevenLabs narration and Remotion cards.
take: Ask before every paid batch: a dry-run prints item count and cost, and the user says yes first.
Text and numbers are drawn in code from a fact base; image prompts forbid text entirely.
Every scene falls back cleanly: no component shows its card, no picture gets a drawn ground, no voice gets estimated timing.
future_use: Dry-run cost gate for any paid generation step.

what_it_is: Codex and Claude skill turning a real software workflow into a narrated, captioned SOP tutorial video.
take: Measure the real voice duration before arranging scenes; never let a caption cue outlive its scene.
One action per beat: where to go, what to click, and what success looks like.
Target about -16 LUFS integrated with true peak at or below -1 dBTP for web output.
future_use: Screen-capture tutorials; not for talking-head reels.

what_it_is: Chinese skill for explainer animations synced to narration: voice first, word timing, then the picture.
take: Land each action 3 frames before its keyword's first character, accepting -6 to +1 frame (at 60 fps); new objects appear at least 12 frames early.
Keyword check: visual change from 0.35 s before to 0.15 s after the keyword must be at least 1.5x the change one second earlier.
Small benchmark (9 keywords): without the workflow Opus landed 1/9 and Sonnet 0/9 on time; with it both landed 9/9.
Finish at -14 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP and 48 kHz.
future_use: Word-timed motion cues for motion cards in any reel.

what_it_is: Claude skill for 3Blue1Brown-style research promo videos in Remotion, with a claims ledger and fact-check.
take: Independent fact-check: a fresh agent re-checks every claim against its source before the cut is final.
Keep a claims ledger (notes/claims.md): each claim, its source, and the exact value shown on screen.
Label illustrations as illustrations; use real data from the paper for every number.
future_use: Claims ledger and fresh-agent fact check for sourced reels.

what_it_is: Chinese HyperFrames explainer workflow with motion-design rules, sourced photos, generated stills and contact-sheet review.
take: Never call a render done until you have viewed the current version's contact sheet; file existence or logs do not count.
Easing tokens: enter bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), exit bezier(0.6,0,0.9,0.35), move bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1); exits run faster than entries.
Masked text reveals start at yPercent 135, not 100, so rotated glyphs do not peek past the mask edge.
Final loudness check: integrated -14 LUFS plus or minus 1, true peak at or below -1 dBFS.
future_use: Easing tokens and contact-sheet QA for motion cards.

what_it_is: Remotion engine for whiteboard, sketch and paper-style motion graphics with pen-following and cross-hatching.
take: Tailwind preflight forces img max-width 100% and height auto; set an explicit container size and override it so images are not stretched.
A pen-tip anchor at (0,0) plus tangent-based rotation keeps the drawn tip on the path.
Stroke wobble is a parameter per shape, so sketches look drawn rather than generated.
future_use: Sketch-style B-roll and diagram strokes for explainers.

what_it_is: Claude skill turning a paper or experiments into a 3Blue1Brown-style video with a claims ledger.
take: Claims ledger (claims.json): each claim has a status (final, development, planned or reported) and a source; the check fails if a narrated number is missing from the ledger.
Every figure comes from real data, and each image is registered with the script, seed and hash that produced it.
Plan scenes beat by beat by what moves, and show the plan before any animation code is written.
future_use: Claims ledger with numeric check for sourced explainers.

what_it_is: Claude Code skill turning a paper or codebase into a narrated animated video, rendered locally with Remotion.
take: Narration is spoken only; on-screen text is authored separately. Budget about 2.5 words per second, so a 14 s scene holds about 35 words.
Calibrate every claim to what the source actually shows; do not overstate the result.
future_use: Narration budgeting and the spoken-versus-on-screen split.

what_it_is: Manim and edge-tts skill for pop-science explainers, with a four-part narrative plan and timed segments.
take: Split long-form time by story role: hook 15-20%, build 30-35%, deepen 30-35%, conclude 15-20%.
Time each narration segment from its real TTS clip and hold the picture for that length, not an estimate from character count.
Run a review checklist on the plan (hook strength, jargon, transitions) before writing any code.
future_use: Story-beat timing split for longer explainers.

what_it_is: Chinese Remotion skill making silent knowledge shorts with BGM-synced cues and sound effects.
take: Subtitle dwell = max(3.5 s, Chinese characters x 0.22 + 1.0 s), stretched up to 30% when the scene has room.
Visual events snap to music beats within one frame; use real CC0 foley for physical objects, synth for non-physical events.
Layer the key moment as impact, sub and hit; the music ducks about 3 dB under it.
Check true peak at or below -1 dBFS and that video length matches the music within one frame.
future_use: Dwell formula and foley layering; bundled BGM is not reusable.

what_it_is: Claude skill turning LaTeX, PDF or text notes into 3Blue1Brown-style Manim videos with TTS and captions.
take: Confirm scope before building: resolution, length, caption format and TTS backend, each with a default.
Run a scene validator before render: text overlaps, out-of-bounds elements and text overflow are caught.
Write soft subtitles as an .srt beside the MP4 with the same slug, so players load it automatically.
future_use: Pre-render overlap and bounds validator for text layouts.

what_it_is: Claude skill driving Google Vids in Chrome to build a 50-second stick-figure explainer with voiceover.
take: Fit clip speed to the voice: speed = floor(5 / (voice length + 1.0) x 20) / 20, so each scene holds its line.
Mute generated clips' own audio before adding voiceover; overlapping voices garble at the cuts.
Set transition dissolves to 0.3 s; the 1.5 s default swallows the joins.
The tool shows no generation counter, so treat a limit message as a stop-and-ask point.
future_use: Voice-fit speed formula and cut-join rules for AI clip edits.

what_it_is: Claude plugin for one-camera history documentaries: layered plates, typed captions and no hard cuts.
take: Each typed line starts on its narrated word (up to 0.5 s late, never early) and stays about 0.5 s plus 0.3 s per word.
Type text at 1.5-3 frames per letter, with exactly one emphasised word per line.
Measure a reference frame by frame before building: count hard cuts and note each hand-off type.
future_use: Caption on-screen timing and reading-time rule for text cards.

what_it_is: Chinese skill producing AI tech review videos: script, Qwen TTS, slides, ffmpeg render and Bilibili upload.
take: After loudnorm, check the audio sample rate with ffprobe; loudnorm output came out at 96 kHz and had to be forced back to 44.1 kHz.
Trim a voice-cloning reference to 30 s or less; longer clips failed in the speaker encoder.
Write JSON and sidecar files as UTF-8 without a BOM, so readers do not fail on a leading byte-order mark.
future_use: Audio and ffmpeg QA gotchas only; skip its cookie-based upload.

what_it_is: Codex and Claude video workflow turning documents into Remotion previews with timecoded player review.
take: Revise one shot first: share the candidate and the changed clip, then rebuild the full video only after that shot is confirmed.
Report the downstream timecode and subtitle changes whenever a shot changes length.
Keep review notes timecoded by scene and version, so feedback can be applied without re-watching the whole film.
future_use: Shot-level revision loop that avoids full re-renders.

what_it_is: Chinese Remotion explainer skill with Doubao TTS, LXGW WenKai font and paper-color palettes.
take: Evidence images enter from the right with ease-out-back over 0.4 s and exit with ease-in-out over 0.3 s; keep the overshoot small.
Outline weights at 1080p: main shapes 8 px, connectors 6 px, detail 4 px; check after local and camera zoom, not only in source.
Pause cues of 150-350 ms between sentences only for emphasis or section changes; let TTS punctuation handle ordinary breaths.
future_use: Motion timing and stroke-width rules for explainer builds.

what_it_is: Canvas-to-MP4 film renderer with stills review, text-timing check and hardware H.264 encoding.
take: Gate every full render behind a stills check: look at frames at 2, 10 and 20 s and fix what is wrong first.
Run a text-timing check before rendering so each on-screen line stays up long enough to read.
Render size and fps are flags, so one page can output 1080x1920 vertical at 30 fps.
future_use: Stills-then-timing-check-then-render gate for any canvas-drawn explainer.

what_it_is: Turns a document or article into a narrated Remotion explainer via storyboard JSON and TTS.
take: Scenes run 5-20 s and carry one or two sentences each, with one core point per scene.
Copy budget: target seconds times about 4 Mandarin characters per second.
future_use: Article-to-video explainers from written sources.

what_it_is: Chinese paper-cut explainer skill: layered character scenes, speech-edit padding, caption timing and QC.
take: Speech edit: keep about 80 ms before a retained word and 120-180 ms after phrases; split only on pauses longer than about 0.75 s.
Keep 800-1000 ms after the last sentence; caption chunks typically last 0.7-4.5 s.
QC: video and audio durations within 0.10 s, and a 7-frame contact sheet covering opening, concept, flow, and outro.
future_use: Speech-edit padding and caption-duration rules for talking-head cuts.

what_it_is: Narrated explainer pipeline: Kokoro voice, Whisper word timings, shot planning and Chrome motion graphics.
take: Human test before planning: a thing gets a clear photo, a number a counter, a comparison both items side by side at one scale.
Kinetic text on about 5% of runtime, only on thesis lines; short editorial shots run 2-4 s.
Recorded retakes: a later repeated paragraph replaces the earlier one; log which source intervals were kept.
future_use: Shot-type rules for B-roll and cutaway choice.

what_it_is: Korean Claude Code pipeline: source text to narrated Remotion explainer with local TTS and approval gates.
take: Run a wording gate (lint plus semantic review) on the script before any TTS or render, so rework stays cheap.
Each stage writes a JSON contract, so one stage can restart without redoing the whole chain.
Keep a transliteration map for foreign terms and extend it whenever a new term appears.
future_use: Script-review gate and JSON stage contracts for client scripts.

what_it_is: Narrated learning-video engine in soft 3D clay; a separate agent checks facts and formulas before voice.
take: Before any voice or picture, a separate checker re-derives every fact and formula and lists Must and Should fixes with exact replacement sentences.
Every formula term must sit on the thing it names, and the script says what happens when that term changes.
Keep a faults table: each real mistake gets a row naming the automated check that now stops it.
future_use: Independent fact-check pass for any explainer script.

what_it_is: Chinese HyperFrames explainer workflow: beat-timed motion design, photo evidence, AI video layer and review loop.
take: Easing tokens: enter bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), exit bezier(0.6,0,0.9,0.35), move bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1); use ease-out for every arrival.
Spring table: default back.out(1.2) at 0.6 s, heavy panels power3.out at 0.8-1.0 s, one elastic.out(1,0.4) at 0.9 s per video.
Review loop: snapshot each beat 0.15 s before its clause ends, read the whole contact sheet, fix, and repeat before calling it done.
Stagger timing: derive each item's start from the inverse of the counter's easing, or bars and numbers drift apart.
future_use: Easing and spring tokens for every HTML/GSAP motion card.

what_it_is: Public sanitized script-to-video skill: voiceover, transcription, storyboard and HyperFrames composition.
take: Talking-cut mode: start from a talking-head video and alternate face-cam footage with graphic cutaways while the original audio stays in sync.
Only the README was read; it gives no numeric timing rules, so verify timings before reusing the mode.
future_use: Talking-head cutaway mode for graphic inserts.

what_it_is: Vertical 1080x1920 talking-head explainer kit alternating concept scenes with app-style workbench shots.
take: Loudness: measure the final AAC MP4, not the mix WAV; target -14.5 LUFS within -15 to -14, true peak at or below -1 dBTP.
AAC re-encode can drop 0.5-1 dB: measure the encoded file, correct gain by the difference, then measure again.
Minimum on-screen text 32 px; spoken words stay at least 32 px after camera zoom; caption text 32/500, body 40/500.
Do not repeat a spoken sentence on screen; big text carries only 2-4 core characters or a number.
future_use: Final-MP4 loudness check and minimum text size for reels.

what_it_is: Claude Code plugin making narrated codebase videos, with fresh agents checking every claim against the code.
take: Every statement carries a file and line reference; a second fresh agent opens every reference before any script is written.
That check caught 9 document corrections and 2 script sentences that would mislead a listener, before any voice was made.
A fresh agent audits each drawn scene against the script; a traceable claim beats a plausible one.
future_use: Claim-to-source audit before reel scripts go to voice.

what_it_is: Narrated architecture-tour generator: Graphviz diagram, narration script, then voiced MP4 with approval gates.
take: Three approval gates (scope, diagram, narration) come before the 15-minute render, so cheap checks run before expensive work.
Per-sentence content-addressed voice cache: a narration tweak re-renders in about 5 minutes instead of a full pass.
Iterate on a low-DPI preview render, then run the full-quality render once the preview is approved.
future_use: Per-sentence voice cache and preview renders for reel re-edits.

what_it_is: Gate-driven motion-video producer: brief, script, storyboard, credit estimate, keyframe review, then build.
take: Show a credit-estimate table before any heavy build: text 2-4k tokens, diagram 5-9k, character or 3D 15-30k, hero explainer 40-80k.
Stop for approval at script, storyboard, estimate and keyframes; rebuild only scenes whose inputs changed after approval.
Keyframe stills and one contact sheet form the review point before the full render.
future_use: Approval gates and credit estimates before any generation spend.

what_it_is: Code-made 30-60 s motion explainer: Remotion picture and numpy synth sound driven by one timeline.json.
take: One timeline.json drives picture and sound, so cuts, numbers and hits share one set of event times.
Put cuts on a 120 BPM grid (0.5 s steps); hook title in the first 2 s; one idea per 4-6 s scene.
Normalise audio to -14 LUFS in the render script, then check a contact sheet for overlaps and empty frames before the full render.
future_use: Timeline-driven sound and picture sync for any animated explainer.

what_it_is: Skill where a canvas HTML file draws every frame and score; a harness verifies seeking and renders MP4.
take: Verify the seek(t) contract: seek forward, backward and cold, then compare frame hashes; pass only when they match.
Test audio determinism by rendering the score twice; a difference of more than 1 LSB fails.
After rendering, run blackdetect, freezedetect and ebur128, and review stills at 4 or more samples per second.
future_use: Seek-determinism and freeze/black checks for our HTML builds.

what_it_is: Turkish 1080p whiteboard explainer engine with character poses, lesson-learned rules and numpy SFX mixer.
take: Never switch character pose on audio amplitude thresholds; word pauses cause 3-5 Hz flicker, so hold a steady pose through speech.
On-screen headings at least 44 px in a heavy weight; thin 34 px handwriting reads weak on a phone.
The subtitle file is the source of truth for timing, and the cursor must sit on the button being mentioned.
future_use: Steady-pose and minimum heading-size rules for talking-head overlays.

what_it_is: Halftone paper-collage stop-motion skill: Gemini-made cut-outs and a deterministic Pillow compositor.
take: Animate on twos (12 new poses per second) with seeded per-pose jitter of about 1.5 px and 0.4 degrees for a handmade feel.
Snap elements in with easeOutBack, overshooting by about 8% before they settle.
future_use: Handmade jitter for stop-motion or paper-collage graphic inserts.

what_it_is: Claude skill making beat-timed motion explainers in HTML/GSAP, voiced, rendered, with a critique loop.
take: Critique snapshots: capture each beat 0.35 s after it starts and 0.45 s before it ends; read the contact sheet for empty frames and entrance bugs.
Phone legibility: labels at least 1cqw (about 19 px at 1080p), body text at least 1.3cqw.
Shorts safe zone: keep content between 9% and 62% of frame height; nothing in the bottom 22% or the right 12%.
Every on-screen number traces to a row in brief.md, rounded only in the direction that does not overstate.
future_use: Snapshot critique and vertical safe-zone rules for every reel QA.

what_it_is: Local agent editor that splits shots, captions each clip with a vision model, filters clips and adds subtitles and TTS.
take: Default flow: search_media, load_media, split_shots, understand_clips (one caption per clip), then filter_clips against the request.
Captioning clips before selection lets an agent pick B-roll by content instead of by file name.
Install rule: check each prerequisite before changing anything, and validate imports before claiming success.
future_use: Clip captioning then content-filtered B-roll selection.

what_it_is: Chinese spoken-video cut workflow: term fixes, five single-issue scans, retake table and Studio review.
take: Fix transcription terms before any cut decision, using a per-speaker dictionary (for example Grok heard as Clock or Glock); change spelling only, never times or word count.
Scan for mistakes in five passes, each finding one error type, so filler, false starts and repeats are never mixed in one pass.
Repeated sentences: keep the best take; risk is low when takes agree and high when wording differs, so listen before accepting.
Every change is read back and checked against the expected revision before the next step; conflicts stop and never overwrite.
future_use: Per-client term dictionary and retake table before reel cuts.

what_it_is: Open-source MCP-driven video editor with transcript editing, draft-review edit sessions and export.
take: Edit sessions: begin a session, make changes as a draft, review the draft, and report success only after that review.
Manual approval mode is the default; unattended runs only when the user explicitly asks.
Variant batches: fix the variation matrix and minimum separation per pair before cutting any output.
future_use: Draft-then-review edit sessions for client-revision loops.

what_it_is: Electron desktop video editor for agents; its skill here covers desktop app release automation.
take: Nothing reusable for talking-head reels: the skill reviewed covers desktop app tag releases and code signing.
Only pattern worth keeping: publish only verified artifacts and compare hashes after a fresh download.
future_use: Release checks if we ever ship a desktop tool.

what_it_is: Embeddable web video editor component with canvas, timeline, transcript and AI chat; host supplies services.
take: Model, transcription and persistence are injected as provider interfaces, so the editor can run without a hosted backend.
The README gives no caption or loudness rules; it is a component to embed, not a method.
future_use: Embedded client-review editor, if we build one.

what_it_is: Free Claude skills for motion B-roll, explainers, sound effects and person cut-outs with SAM 2.
take: Motion B-roll: leave at least about 2 s of face between cutaways, and cut away for the length of one idea, 3-10 s.
B-roll as one element that morphs and never hard-cuts, driven by a spring; content swaps under a short blur.
Person separation: pick the SAM 2 size by GPU memory (large at 12 GB+, base-plus on Apple Silicon, tiny on CPU); process 60-frame chunks.
future_use: Cutaway spacing rule and person matte for talking-head B-roll.

what_it_is: 51 Python-rendered talking-head effects for Reels: punch-ins, checklists, stamps and grades.
take: Effect windows of 1.5-4 s look best; check one still at each effect's midpoint before rendering the full file.
lean-in is a quick punch-in on one word, a useful pattern for emphasis that keeps the speaker on screen.
Skip effects that draw fake app UI (comment box, Follow button, iMessage); they break our no-invented-UI rule.
future_use: Punch-in and stamp timing patterns for emphasis beats.

what_it_is: MCP bridge letting agents operate a local Adobe Premiere Pro project through a CEP panel.
take: Verify the connection before any edit, then re-read the sequence after each change; never report a change as done without that read-back.
Preview an edit plan, then apply only the unchanged plan with an exact confirmation token.
future_use: Handoff to client Premiere editors, with read-back checks.

what_it_is: Electron video editor exposing its live timeline over MCP, with a transcript-driven cut skill.
take: Never cut inside a word: snap every edge to a word boundary from the transcript, keeping about 100 ms of padding each side.
Trim pauses instead of removing them; speech with every gap removed sounds rushed.
Let a move finish before a cut; a punch-in still travelling at the cut looks broken.
Check a contact sheet at every cut before saying the edit is done.
future_use: Word-boundary snapping and cut padding for talking-head cuts.

what_it_is: Chinese video-recap pipeline: deterministic gates for flicker, cut sentences, narration overlap and loudness.
take: Reject any shot of 0.20 s or less (flicker) and any cut that splits a sentence; these gates run before voiceover.
Narration must not overlap original speech and time windows must not overload; a script checks both before render.
Keep true peak at -1.0 dBTP, verified through the encoder's own true-peak measurement, not on the mix.
When studying a reference film: measure cut density per 10 s sliding window and short-term loudness per second.
future_use: Deterministic pre-voiceover gates for flicker and sentence cuts.

what_it_is: Large MCP server for Adobe Premiere Pro with preview-then-apply edit plans and host verification.
take: Preview the edit plan, then apply it only with the unchanged plan and an exact confirmation token; preview again after any change.
Never claim an export exists until a live tool result confirms it.
future_use: Preview-then-apply gate for client-side Premiere handoffs.

what_it_is: Chinese talking-head motion-cut skill: real screenshots as evidence, an AI video judge and pairwise accept rules.
take: Judge revisions pairwise, not by absolute score: accept a new version only if it wins in both A/B orders; a tie or invalid comparison is not a win.
Cap revision loops at 3 versions, and require a visible improvement in each round.
Check every screenshot for sensitive text before use, and log the legible text in a fingerprint manifest.
future_use: Pairwise A/B acceptance for reel revisions.

what_it_is: Claude Code skill: raw talking-head recordings in, vertical reels out, with captions, SFX and QA checks.
take: Keep about 0.6-1 s of air after a take's last word so a sound effect or meme lands cleanly; aim for 45-75 s total.
After render, check loudness, true peak, each SFX against the voice, and where each caption landed.
One fresh helper per reel: planning and judging on the strongest model, mechanical steps handled by scripts.
future_use: Take selection, air and post-render QA for every reel.

what_it_is: Claude-scored longform-to-shorts pipeline: 5-dimension segment rubric, word-snapped cuts, animated captions.
take: Score candidate segments on hook 0.30, standalone sense 0.25, emotion 0.20, value density 0.15 and payoff 0.10.
Bold caption preset: Montserrat 800 at 72 px, 2-3 words per page, active word yellow #FFD700, 3 px black outline, spring damping 12.
Snap cut edges to word boundaries and nearby silences so no word is clipped.
future_use: Caption preset and hook-scoring rubric for short-form cuts.

what_it_is: Claude Code pipeline from raw talking-head recording to cut, Remotion visuals, cleaned voice and SFX.
take: Diagnose noise before choosing a cleaner: steady hiss goes to local RNNoise, dynamic outdoor noise needs the cloud isolator; A/B a short sample first.
Give the transcriber a keyterms list of this video's names and products before transcribing, so proper nouns stay correct.
Text contrast gates: body ink on paper at least 7:1, secondary text 4.5:1, large accent text 3:1.
future_use: Keyterm list and text contrast gates for caption design.

what_it_is: Discontinued SRT-to-B-roll system: independent director, chapter creators, visual review, draft and final media.
take: Keep draft and final media separate and labelled; a draft must never pass as final media.
Fix review problems by patching the original creator's file locally, not by remaking the whole film.
Measured cost on the same input: one creator used about 307k input tokens; director plus two producers used about 1.67M.
future_use: Token-cost benchmark for multi-agent B-roll; project discontinued.

what_it_is: MCP bridge letting Claude Code and others edit video in the Cassette cloud service.
take: Cloud service: local files named in a call are uploaded to Cassette, so client footage would leave the machine; this conflicts with client confidentiality.
Long-wait rule: poll status and never re-issue a call that may already have run; wait retry_after_seconds on rate limits.
future_use: Cloud editing bridge only if client footage rules allow it.

what_it_is: Chinese travel-vlog auto-edit workflow for Claude Code: inventory, whisper, ffmpeg render.
take: Render joins with ffmpeg concat rather than an xfade chain; the skill warns xfade chains drop frames.
Never add shortest=1 to a PNG overlay; a single-frame PNG truncates the whole video.
Whisper invents text over ambient-only audio; gate segments by volume before trusting their words.
Pacing guide: about 3-4 s per shot, under 2 s for montage, over 8 s for narrative holds.
future_use: Ffmpeg render pitfalls checklist for any multi-clip build.

what_it_is: Multi-take ad editing agent with audio cleanup, B-roll capture and branded motion-card skills.
take: Mute censored words before reverb convolution so the swear never enters the room tail.
A 13 kHz lowpass plus an FFT brick-wall (13.0 to 13.5 kHz) kills the AI generator's 13-16 kHz whine; a Butterworth alone does not.
Pad each whisper word span -0.10 s at start and +0.06 s at end; whisper starts run 100-200 ms late on this footage.
Verify each censored span by re-transcribing a plus or minus 0.7 s slice; accept only if the passes agree within about 50 ms.
future_use: Room-matched audio cleanup if a client's voice or location audio is poor.

what_it_is: Open-source macOS desktop editor rebuilt from CapCut research, with local MLX speech.
take: SKIP: a manual multitrack desktop editor; the README has no talking-head rules or numbers to reuse.
Keyframe easing set (linear, ease-in, ease-out, smooth) applies to motion, opacity and volume curves.
future_use: Manual GUI fallback for fine timeline work, if ever needed.

what_it_is: MCP server giving agents verified, reversible Adobe Premiere Pro edits and exports.
take: Duplicate the sequence and edit only the copy; require exactly one new ID and verified:true before touching it.
Caption checks: at most two lines, no single-word orphan lines, reject overlaps or non-positive durations, counts must match the SRT.
Dialogue cuts keep 80-150 ms before speech and 120-250 ms after, and intersect silence with each used source range first.
Treat a queued export as pending until an external file check sees a stable, non-empty output.
future_use: Premiere handoff and caption QA if a client asks for NLE output.

what_it_is: Codex talking-head pipeline with rough-cut, captions, motion preview and export approval gates.
take: Source is immutable and main audio is the clock; never retime audio unless the user approves a rough-cut strategy.
Build a preview and wait for approval before final; final must use the original source, never an upscaled preview.
Merge caption groups shorter than about 0.5 s unless the speech is genuinely that short.
Learn style only from explicit feedback; no permanent rules from silence or one unconfirmed draft.
future_use: Feedback-learning and preview-gate rules for client revisions.

what_it_is: Aggressive talking-head tightener driven by Montreal Forced Aligner word boundaries.
take: Target about one cut every 1.3-1.5 s (median cut near 1.1 s) for a 40-60% runtime reduction.
Check audio amplitude before cutting any silence; audible windows are laughs or content and stay.
Re-transcribe each kept region alone to check its boundary; global alignment can drift by seconds on retakes.
Render with ffmpeg trim plus concat, not select, which misaligns audio.
future_use: Retake-detection check for longer interview-style client footage.

what_it_is: Mac video editor and canvas where Claude Code or Codex drive timeline edits through editorctl.
take: Ask before merging multi-clip footage; the skill requires a yes before concatenating clips to keep audio continuous.
Every generated output gets a unique filename; a previous render is never overwritten.
Canvas mode splits vector drawing (Paper.js), physics (Matter.js) and raw HTML for animated graphics.
future_use: Physics-style card motion if a reel ever needs canvas-driven graphics.

what_it_is: Terminal video agent with a HyperFrames explainer director and a visual-repair loop.
take: Blind-decode sampled rendered frames without showing the intended answer, then grade the decode against the claim list.
Accept a visual repair only if it is monotonic: fewer hard failures and no quality or coverage regression.
Reject any on-screen visual that has no evidence in the transcript before HTML is generated.
Run ablation and temporal-scramble counterfactuals before promoting a visual's quality.
future_use: Blind frame-check QA for captions and cards before preview approval.

what_it_is: MCP bridge letting agents read, build and verify After Effects compositions in the live app.
take: Verify a composition by exporting PNG frames, sampling a grid, and comparing A/B pixel differences.
Checkpoint the saved project before risky operations so a failed script can be inspected and restored.
Run rendering outside any Undo group; mismatched Undo groups break checkpoint recovery.
future_use: Frame-diff QA for motion graphics if we add an After Effects stage.

what_it_is: MCP server for editing CapCut and OpenCut project files, with dry-run as the default.
take: SKIP: it edits proprietary draft JSON and the README gives no talking-head rules; only the dry-run default is reusable.
Dry-run is the default; a save needs an explicit dryRun=false, which is a useful write gate.
future_use: CapCut draft handoff if a client needs an editable timeline.

what_it_is: Claude Code skill set for talking-head graphics: panels behind the speaker and explainer layouts.
take: Explainer layout: speaker sits low in a rounded panel with the head breaking the top edge; keep visuals between y 330 and 760 px.
Keep text out of the top 220 px and bottom 420 px, and 100 px at each side, for platform UI.
Keep captions 80 px clear of the bottom zone and off the mouth; move them before rebuilding.
Behind-the-person: cut the speaker out, put the panel behind the head, and land big words on the chest one per beat.
future_use: Explainer and behind-speaker layouts for stat and list reels.

what_it_is: Creator reel workflow: idea sourcing, hook scripting, footage-matched layouts and event-matched sound.
take: Layout ladder at 1080x1920: full camera; half split with content above y=960; third split with camera from y=1120; full proof for close UI.
Type sizes on a 1080-wide export: captions about 54 px, panel headings 52-76 px, source labels 24-30 px.
Glass fades over the face: 12% opaque at 65 px, 55% at 160 px, solid at 270 px, with a 75 px side feather.
Most moves 0.3-0.5 s ease-out; shared-shape transitions 0.45-0.8 s.
future_use: Layout and type-size spec for split-screen proof reels.

what_it_is: Bilingual talking-head motion style with a morphing presenter window and 23 selectable templates.
take: The presenter stays on screen inside a window that changes shape while solid colour cards and numbers cut in around it.
Long videos render in 10-second chunks with continuous audio and captions instead of one pass.
Each style is a numbered template (T01-T24) the user picks per section, so one reel can switch looks by ID.
future_use: Chunked long-video rendering and template-ID style selection.

what_it_is: Chinese narrated vlog pipeline: TTS or aligned narration, asset index, rough cut and subtitles.
take: Subtitle safe area: title-safe padding of 18% (safe-ratio 0.82), with font size shrunk until every page fits.
Cheap iteration: edit the subtitle pages file and rebuild the ASS file; re-burn only once at the end.
Checkpoint after the plan and after the render; the user approves the picks before any render runs.
future_use: Edit caption text without re-encoding video.

what_it_is: Chinese narration recap pipeline: analyse, script, cut, voice, duck original audio and assemble.
take: Duck the original audio under narration (fixed, sidechain or zone modes), then loudness-normalise the final mix.
Snap clip boundaries to natural pauses and nudge them clear of a hard shot change, so no sliver of the next shot shows.
Narration segments carry pause_after_ms, default 250 ms, to keep a tight rhythm.
future_use: Ducking modes for voice-over over client b-roll.

what_it_is: Chinese knowledge talking-head cutter with frame.md style presets driving HyperFrames overlays and covers.
take: Style as a spec file: frame.md holds the visual rules; template.html and cover.html are its executable forms, and a style is incomplete without both.
Cover recipe: 100% feathered mirror mask for centre focus, title of 6-8 characters over 3 lines.
Templates may not introduce any colour or motion that the frame.md does not declare.
future_use: Per-client style spec file for overlay and cover looks.

what_it_is: Codex skill cutting local videos into 30-60 s vertical shorts with silence removal and Whisper captions.
take: Its normal cut style keeps 0.5 s of silence on each side of a cut so speech feels less abrupt.
Preset ladder light, normal, aggressive chosen per request, with a 45 s default target.
future_use: Light, normal, aggressive cut-style presets for reel length targets.

what_it_is: Local-first desktop editor where humans and agents share one timeline through MCP.
take: Edit by transcript: delete clips by word with an impact preview and one-step synced undo.
Agent edits arrive as proposals; a human reviews rendered frame evidence before a patch applies.
Frame-window render caching so re-renders only redo changed segments.
future_use: Transcript-delete preview and proposal review for client notes.

what_it_is: Spanish Remotion reel editor with versioned edits, learned creator style, SFX and stickers.
take: Corrections never touch the previous version: copy to vN+1, change only the requested fields, then diff against the request.
General preferences go into the active style file, so later edits inherit them without re-asking.
Earlier versions stay read-only; the highest version number is the working one.
future_use: Versioned revision workflow for client change requests.

what_it_is: Russian-language Claude Code harness: take finding, beat lists, mastering, cover and Buffer publishing.
take: Find duplicate takes and false starts before any cutting pass.
Keep key text out of the bottom 15% and top 8% of the frame.
Measure loudness with ebur128 after mastering and check it against the configured target.
Cover: matte the portrait with birefnet-portrait before compositing the sticker.
future_use: Take-finding order and cover-matte step for new reels.

what_it_is: Agent skill turning travel footage into a story plan and bounded scene-by-scene edit revisions.
take: Work one named scene or revision at a time, keeping an editable timeline and a record of each change.
Separate what the agent can see or hear from what the tool actually inspected; report the reviewed intervals.
future_use: Multi-scene story planning for longer client documentaries.

what_it_is: Turkish Remotion workspace that builds a channel brand kit and edits talking-head videos.
take: Motion tokens: calm enter 0.38 s expo-out, exit 0.22 s; energetic enter 0.22-0.28 s with a larger slide.
Audio levels set per channel: SFX around -13 dB, music bed level from the user's answer.
Render design stills at chosen timestamps before the full render, to check each look cheaply.
future_use: Motion token table for brand easing and durations.

what_it_is: Hermes-agent toolchain routing screen capture, HyperFrames motion and headless post-processing.
take: Decide the stage route before touching any tool: capture, design or post, chosen from the input type.
Engines exchange only MP4, SRT and PNG frames, so each stage can be swapped or rerun alone.
future_use: Stage routing table for screen-demo reels.

what_it_is: Mac-local Claude plugin editor: transcript cuts, brand storyboard, notes loop and HyperFrames animations.
take: Notes loop: read the storyboard, look at the frame, make the change, then wait for the next note.
For an animation, state one idea in one line, build it, render a check shot, then show the user.
Cut pauses longer than the gap setting; add stat callouts only on numbers worth seeing.
future_use: Notes-driven revision loop for client review.

what_it_is: Chinese Remotion skills for talking-head motion graphics: assembly, design system, B-roll and SFX.
take: Plan table: every segment cites the rule number it follows; a plan with no rule numbers means the rules were not read.
Do not back-derive rules from one existing scene file; it only shows the rules that scene happened to use.
Motion vocabulary to reuse: counting numbers, verdict slam, growing bars, defined exit rules, clean-screen beats.
future_use: Rule-cited plan table for every reel beat sheet.

what_it_is: Music-driven edit: beat analysis, scene tagging, EDL planning and ffmpeg render for montages.
take: White flash: 0.07 s fade-in from white on the beat; punch-in scale 1.15 held about two frames.
Cut density is a stride: 1 means a cut on every beat, 2 or more keeps every Nth beat.
Take only the look the user asks for from a reference, never the whole clone.
future_use: Music-cut intros and montage B-roll, not talking-head reels.

what_it_is: Original-voice talking-head pipeline: word-level script review, clean cut, then optional motion packaging.
take: Every word gets a keep or delete decision with a stated reason, reviewed in chat before any render.
Subtitles may only cover words the audio actually kept; captions are never rewritten to hide an audio edit.
Two approval gates: transcript first, then the clean cut; motion packaging is a separate third gate.
future_use: Word-level keep/delete log for client script approval.

what_it_is: Portuguese Claude Code reel editor: pause cuts, word captions, anchored effects and re-hear QA.
take: Cut only in real pauses, measured on volume and sibilance, so a final 's' is never eaten.
Anchor each on-screen element to the exact spoken word, not a guessed second.
After rendering, re-hear the file: speech below 97% recognition or a missing word near an edit is a fail.
Keep the call-to-action; cut the middle, never the ending.
future_use: Re-hear ASR QA gate on every final render.

what_it_is: Chinese Claude skill kit: transcript-based cutting, subtitles, burn-in, keyword highlight and self-update.
take: Self-update: corrections are logged and turned into updated rules, so mistakes are not repeated.
Subtitle font size scales with resolution: about 50 pt at 1080p, 24 pt at 720p.
future_use: Correction-to-rule logging for client feedback.

what_it_is: Portuguese Reels editor agent with per-step instruction files, subagent inserts and Drive/Notion publishing.
take: Read only the one step file you are on; load the rest later to save context.
Publishing shows a file-to-folder plan and runs only after an explicit yes; check that a target does not exist before copying.
Export spec for scheduling: 4K H.264 at -14 LUFS, with HEVC masters kept separately.
future_use: Per-step file loading to save context on long reel builds.

what_it_is: Vision-first multi-clip cutter: looks at footage, picks usable seconds, grades, and adds animated titles.
take: Title animation vocabulary: fade-up as the safe default, zoom-in for energy, blur-in for calm, typewriter for short lines.
Title at y 0.42 of frame height, slightly above centre, for visual weight; outline and shadow keep it readable on bright backgrounds.
Pick a look per footage type: warm for people and food, cool for city, clean as the safe default.
future_use: Title animation presets for chapter cards.

what_it_is: Claude edits talking-head takes from text files: cuts, captions, wall cards and verification.
take: Run voice activity detection before transcribing and transcribe per speech span; long silence makes the transcriber hallucinate.
Detect faces on a square crop; full-frame detection on 16:9 or 9:16 frames misses faces.
Never cut from a restarted take; the take-cutlist tool proposes the last attempt as keeper but never cuts.
Measure the subject's edge and headroom per cut instead of typing a constant; a typed constant was 286 px off.
future_use: Pipeline hygiene: VAD before transcribe, square-crop face detection, measured headroom.

what_it_is: Claude skill cutting talking-head footage tight, cleaning voice, framing, captioning and adding code-driven motion graphics.
take: Collapse every pause to about 0.09 s; out points wait for the word's real end, and the longest remaining silence should be under 0.2 s.
Voice: DeepFilterNet capped at 24 dB attenuation, then -14 LUFS; re-run at 18 dB if it sounds processed.
Framing: full shots at 110% with the face centred; optional punch-ins at 130% on long holds.
Motion graphics over about 40-60% of runtime, keeping the face for hooks; springs under 2% overshoot.
future_use: Pause-collapse and framing numbers for every talking-head reel.

what_it_is: Plan-first cinematic edit skill: blueprint and approval first, then render with versioned outputs.
take: Blueprint first: no final render until an explicit approval phrase, and the reply states that nothing is rendered yet.
Never overwrite prior renders; use versioned names such as promo_cut_v2.mp4.
Missing intake details get stated defaults written to an intake summary, not a stream of questions.
future_use: Blueprint-then-render gate and versioned outputs for each client reel.

what_it_is: Desktop editor where Claude writes motion graphics as code and checks its own frames.
take: Agent verifies its own output: render frames and contact sheets, read errors, fix, and repeat before showing the user.
Renders are frame-exact and deterministic, so a fix can be proven against the same input.
future_use: Frame and contact-sheet self-check loop before each preview.

what_it_is: Remotion motion graphics on measured footage: ffmpeg measures silences and cuts, Remotion draws, frame counts verified.
take: Round frame counts half-up like JavaScript Math.round; Python round() is banker's rounding and gave 94 where the composition drew 95 at 3.15 s x 30 fps.
