Measure first (silences, scene cuts, speech ranges), draw only speech ranges, and re-time captions to the new cut from the same measurements.
Refuse variable-frame-rate or HDR sources; conform to a constant-frame-rate SDR copy and leave the original untouched.
future_use: Frame-exact render checks for any Remotion or motion step.

what_it_is: Claude skill turning a talking-to-camera video into a captioned reel, with script and storyboard approval gates.
take: Two gates before render: print the whole numbered script for approval, then render one storyboard frame from the middle of every scene.
Captions show 1-2 words per screen (capWords=2) or 3-4 words (capWords=4), placed just under the jaw using face-frame detection.
Ask once about audio clean-up and lighting before editing; skip any question the saved profile already answers.
future_use: Approval gates and jaw-anchored captions for face reels.

what_it_is: Chinese long-video clipper that picks complete viewpoints from a reviewed transcript, not keywords.
take: Select highlights by complete semantic viewpoint after reading the whole transcript; never by keyword score or fixed duration.
Review speech-recognition mistakes into a plan before subtitles render, so wrong words never reach the caption.
Keep an auditable edit-plan file (cuts, reasons, corrections) so each render can be re-checked against it.
future_use: Semantic clip selection for long recordings such as webinars.

what_it_is: Staged HyperFrames workflow for talking-head videos: fixed-frame-rate preprocess, SRT and storyboard approvals, then render.
take: Re-encode the source to stable 30 fps H.264 with fixed keyframes before transcribing, so timing and renders stay consistent.
Portrait rule: the speaker stays on screen at all times; charts and footage appear only as overlays, never replacing the face.
Gate each stage (SRT, structure, storyboard, design) with the user before generating the HyperFrames project.
future_use: Overlay layouts for portrait talking-head reels.

what_it_is: French skill packs for SEO audits and short-video editing; scripts measure first and Claude judges after.
take: Measure before explaining: a metric change counts only if it beats a noise threshold of 1.96 x sqrt(before + after), widened for small sites.
Small-volume rule: under 30 clicks, say the comparison is unreadable rather than draw a trend from it.
Audit scripts print a priority-ordered report (indexing, internal links, basics, tags); Claude then writes the fixes from it.
future_use: Client website SEO audits and reel performance tracking.

what_it_is: Claude Code and Codex skill that edits raw talking-head clips locally: best takes, dead-air cuts, captions, punch-ins.
take: Punch-in 1.15-1.2x, instant, on a key word; slow push-in 1.0-1.1x across long sentences; never above 1.25x on 1080p footage.
Change the visual every 3-5 seconds and place a caption roughly every 3-6 seconds; the hook lands in the first 3 seconds.
Keep captions and large words out of the face band, and check the rendered frame before handing the edit back.
future_use: Punch-in and caption timing for every face reel.

what_it_is: Turkish Claude Code skills for talking-head edits: silence cutting, card-style Reels, and measured animation.
take: Safe zones measured in pixels every 5 frames: on 1080x1920, keep text and cards above about 520 px from the bottom and off the right side past x 900.
Audio: final -14 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP; effect tracks sit about 15 dB under the speech.
Whisper timestamps drift about 0.5 s early: cut at the quietest audio point near the word, not at the timestamp, and transcribe in chunks of 10 s or less.
future_use: Silence cuts and safe-zone checks on every reel.

what_it_is: Chinese motion-template packs (.motion files) where an AI assistant fits the user's script and assets into fixed animation.
take: Scene choreography is fixed per template; the assistant re-times it to new narration and logs the source pack and scene ID per shot.
Never guess word times inside a sentence from a sentence-level SRT; align words first, or label them by hand.
Use only the layout a template declares (portrait or landscape); never assume the other variant exists.
future_use: Full animated explainer packs for non-face formats.

what_it_is: Claude Code skills drawing reel animations in code: line graphs, map routes, exploded phone views, stick figures.
take: Graph: the highest value touches the top gridline, the counter lands exactly on the final value, and labels thin out above 12 points.
Never invent data: with only a start and an end value, ask for the points in between or label the curve as illustrative.
Keep callouts and marketing words off the graphic; the number and the line carry the message.
future_use: Finance number reveals and rate or growth charts.

what_it_is: Local storyboard workbench for Codex and Claude Code: a shot table with voice, images and video filled per shot.
take: Before generating any B-roll, read every local template and record the roots checked, including an empty result.
Long jobs send a heartbeat every 10 minutes; tasks expire after 30 minutes without one, so late output never attaches to a new task.
Write the whole shot list in one call, not shot by shot, so the agent makes fewer round trips.
future_use: Shot-list tracking for B-roll generation jobs.

what_it_is: Faceless YouTube Shorts factory in Claude Code: code-animated, AI-video and collage shorts with voice-synced captions.
take: State the cost before any paid generation, and state the re-roll cost too; the user approves the spend first.
Caption safe zone: nothing critical in the bottom 340 px or the right 160 px of a 1080x1920 frame.
Frame 0 is already composed with the payoff visible, no fade from black; end on the payoff, not a 'like and subscribe' outro.
future_use: Cost gates for any paid video or image generation.

what_it_is: Vietnamese Remotion skill set for 50-60 s vertical explainers from a topic, a GitHub repo, an article or a comparison.
take: Every on-screen fact must trace to source data; an author's own numbers are labelled 'according to the author'.
Script length: about 200-225 words for 50-60 s, 30-40 words per scene; re-measure after voice generation and rewrite if under 50 s.
Comparisons: one fixed colour per side, never red against green (that implies one side is wrong); each sentence matches one fact line.
future_use: Source-traceable explainers and comparison reels.

what_it_is: Nine-skill pipeline for paper-cut vertical explainers: strategy, hook, script, storyboard, voice, build and QA.
take: Hook in three layers: the spoken line opens a gap within about 10 words, the title shows on frame 0 for 2-3 s, and the frame is already mid-action.
Banner track: 10-18 all-caps fact banners of 3-7 words, changing every 1.8-3 s, never repeating the voiceover.
Captions: one tag per word, pages of 1-3 words in the 68-80% height band, never over a face.
future_use: Hook scoring and fact-banner overlays on talking-head reels.

what_it_is: Claude Code skill drawing faceless 9:16 cut-paper explainers in code, timed to a local voice and word timings.
take: Voice is the clock: each spoken line is one scene, with a hard cut just before the line starts.
Cue props from word start times (VW(line, word).t0), so a stamp slams on the word that names it.
Script budget: 6-8 lines, 18-25 s at about 3.5 words per second, arc: hook, how, catch, kicker, CTA.
future_use: Faceless explainer or B-roll reels in paper style.

what_it_is: Chinese map-animation skills: route, flight, region and photo-spot videos from real map data, rendered in Chromium.
take: Check every geocoded place by reading the resolved name and level; same-name places resolve wrong, so use a more specific name or coordinates.
Built-in auto-QA reports off-screen items, overlapping text and black blocks; open the stills only when it fails or taste is in question.
Mark placeholder values as placeholders at delivery (for example unreadable EXIF) and say which figures are illustrative.
future_use: Location and travel B-roll for client stories.

what_it_is: Claude skill for creative reel and long-form edits built on HyperFrames, with pixel-measured safe zones and loudness checks.
take: Safe zones at 1080x1920: no text, face or logo in the top 270 px, only atmosphere below y 1570, and nothing critical in the right 120 px between y 1000-1700.
Captions at least 60 px cap height on a phone; active word in black on #ffd84d or white on saturated dark, never dark text on a mid-tone pill.
Check the top margin by pixel scan (first bright row), not by eye, and measure loudness and true peak before delivery.
future_use: Safe-zone pixel checks and caption contrast for all reels.

what_it_is: Codex skill for auditable Chinese book-review videos: evidence packs, approved scripts, rights gates, local renders.
take: Lock narration timing before generating any footage; never stretch narration to fit clips after the fact.
Normalize each approved clip to silent 720x1280 H.264, then to a constant 30 fps timeline with no speed change.
Picture-lock before the final audio mix, and check each clip alone before the full render. Freesound music candidates are non-commercial research only.
future_use: Timing-locked narration and clip QA gates.

what_it_is: Chinese one-person MCN workbench for Claude Code: topic radar, research, scripts, video and per-account publishing.
take: Hook test: after the first sentence the viewer should be able to restate the topic; scenery or props alone do not pass.
Explainers: re-read the full script as someone who knows nothing about the field; cut or explain any step they could not follow.
Muted check: judge the first frame and on-screen title with sound off before reviewing the rest.
future_use: Hook and clarity checks for explainer scripts.

what_it_is: Open-source Python tool making faceless YouTube Shorts from a topic, article or podcast, with voice and captions.
take: Retention edit: cut every 2-4 s even inside one long scene; a scene is not one shot however long it lasts.
Use word-accurate caption timing when the voice provides it; fall back to script-token alignment otherwise.
Its own audit calls its loudness normalisation approximate; measure integrated LUFS instead of trusting the filter.
future_use: Shot-length rule for long talking-head segments.

what_it_is: Claude Code skill for Remotion Reels, website explainers and carousels with an ElevenLabs voice and word captions.
take: Reels safe area at 1080x1920: keep 285 px at the top and 400 px at the bottom clear; caption zone about y 1300-1520.
ElevenLabs presets (stability / similarity / style): narrator 0.5 / 0.75 / 0.4, calm 0.7 / 0.8 / 0.2, dramatic 0.3 / 0.8 / 0.7.
After regenerating one scene, re-run timing; the info file carries the real durations the composition must use.
future_use: Voice presets and safe-zone numbers for ElevenLabs reels.

what_it_is: Chinese skill making 9:16 hand-drawn story videos from text-to-video clips, with TTS narration and Remotion captions.
take: Render narration first: frame count follows the audio at 24 fps, rounded to 8n+1 and clamped to 41-441 frames.
Keep captions deterministic in Remotion; the video prompt carries a negative instruction so the generator never paints text.
Skip clips already rendered; re-render only a clip that is unwatchable (black, blank or wrong).
future_use: Generated-motion B-roll scenes once budget is approved.

what_it_is: Chinese HyperFrames skill for halftone paper-collage info animations from a voiceover script, rendered locally, no image models.
take: Information sits only in the upper two-thirds (y at or below 1280); the bottom 640 px is the caption zone, with torn paper edges only.
Motion snaps to a 10 fps grid with steps(n) easing; hold at least 0.8 s after each landing so every pause reads as a poster.
One accent colour per frame under 10% of the area; check the end frame matches the approved still.
future_use: Stop-motion info graphics for number and step reveals.

what_it_is: Claude skill kit of 18 HyperFrames styles (fonts, palette, motion, SFX) for 9:16 AI-eval, tutorial and explainer videos.
take: Sound pass after render: fix each FAIL by changing cues or sounds, at most two rounds, then check the waveform image.
Re-subset fonts after all text is final; a stale font build renders missing glyphs as blank boxes.
Pick one main style plus at most one accent style, and treat the brief's 'not:' lines as hard rules.
future_use: Sound-pass checks and font subsetting for any HyperFrames build.

what_it_is: Claude Code skill: a director-producer playbook for code-drawn motion graphics and edits, with preflight and approval gates.
take: Resume from PROGRESS.md: read it and the log tail, then continue from 'Next step' instead of re-deriving context.
Run preflight as a table (tool, status, version, action) and ask about each missing item one at a time.
Never render a full video before the user approves a preview; keep API keys in a local .env with empty slots.
future_use: Resumable project logs for long multi-session reel work.

what_it_is: Vietnamese Claude Code and Codex skill that auto-edits talking-head or voice-only video, picking keyword effects per sentence.
take: Cues must match words the speech model actually heard; a hook gets only a sticker and punch-in, and a CTA gets one circle callout.
Effect text and numbers come only from the spoken line; no invented figures, and a per-effect character limit keeps copy short.
Person masks and thumbnails are prepared before rendering, and cards avoid the face position automatically.
future_use: Keyword-triggered effects on specific spoken words.

what_it_is: Remotion skill for VS Code-style typing animations with keyboard sounds, narration sync and themes.
take: Sync B-roll to narration with delayFrames set from the word's start time; the docs flag an audio startFrame offset gotcha.
Pick a typing speed to set pace: deliberate for key words, a thinking pause before a twist, burst for filler.
Strike-correct a word (type it wrong, pause, delete, retype) to show a change of mind instead of a hard cut.
future_use: Typed-text B-roll inserts for explainer segments.

what_it_is: Claude Code skill directing films built in JavaScript: sound first, a treatment, then a frame-exact MP4 render.
take: Let the voice set every cut: word times come from the recorded voice, and cuts land 0.05-0.15 s before each phrase.
Two clocks: stop-motion objects step at 15 poses per second while pushes and drawn lines move every frame.
Delivery: flat colour and steady motion survive a Reels re-encode; grain and fine particles eat bitrate and go soft.
future_use: Cut timing rule and delivery checks for any reel.

what_it_is: Spanish-language skill for animated vertical shorts: Three.js and Remotion cartoons, or realistic Blender 3D.
take: Mix: voice forward, music and effects 5-10 dB below it, final -14 LUFS.
Story formula: a shocking fact in one line, then place and date, three or four escalating beats, then a dry 'but' turn.
Blender renders are slow, so test a short cut before committing machine time to a long render.
future_use: Caricature-style explainers for non-face segments.

what_it_is: Chinese skill set for AI-knowledge talking-head videos: topic picks, script polish, branded render, covers and titles.
take: Delivery check: verify_output.py must pass audio track, duration match, cover sizes and titles; any FAIL means nothing is delivered.
Prose gate: a banned-phrase checker must come back clean and the user must approve the script before any voice or render step.
Scene rule: every scene has an entrance and a transition; only the final scene may exit.
future_use: Automated delivery checks and prose gate for scripts.

what_it_is: Agent skill turning a voice note, talking-head or green-screen take into an animated, brand-styled video timed to words.
take: Cut on the word: a new shot every 1-4 s, starting on the word where the idea lands; a shot held over 3 s keeps moving.
Recording: start 2 s before speaking and hold still 2 s after the last word, so cuts have clean room tone to land on.
Determinism: every frame is a function of time and every sound comes from a cue; the mix pads to full duration.
future_use: Word-synced shot list and room-tone recording guide.

what_it_is: Claude Code skill adding motion-graphic effects behind or in front of a talking-head clip, using Remotion, GSAP and Three.js.
take: Punch-in on a key word: 1 to 1.06-1.08 over 5 frames, back to 1 over about 24 frames; never let an effect run into the last 0.8 s.
Land decelerates and leave accelerates; arrivals come from about 1.45x scale over roughly 6 frames, with one spring per film at most.
Land each effect about 2 frames before its spoken word; render stills at 30% and 60% of every effect before the full render.
future_use: Punch-in timings and effect-landing rules for face reels.

what_it_is: Claude Code plugin drawing narrated films in code from PDFs, essays or topics; the voice sets the clock.
take: Voice first: generate narration before building scenes, because a line change re-renders every later shot.
Reuse finished spans: re-render only changed shots and reuse the rest, so one edited line never re-renders the whole film.
Watch your own output: render frames, check a contact sheet, fix and repeat instead of self-certifying.
future_use: Shot-level render caching for long narrated edits.

what_it_is: Russian-language Claude Code skill making 9:16 explainer cartoons in the user's own style, with a hero character.
take: Gate: no production until onboarding steps are marked done in a state file; a status command shows the next unfinished step.
Do not send a person's photo to an external AI image service without their explicit consent; offer a built-in character instead.
Each sound and label is tied to a spoken word through a cue file, so changing one word changes only one cue.
future_use: Client onboarding state and avatar consent for future formats.

what_it_is: Claude skills for short-form video: hooks and retention, word-timed captions, countdowns and lower thirds.
take: Captions: pages of 1-4 words, heavy outline, about 72 px on a 1920 px frame; word timing comes from a transcript, never interpolated.
Lower third: stagger the bar, then the name, then the role 3-6 frames apart; hold 3-5 s; exit in about two-thirds of the entry time.
Countdown numbers come from the frame index, not setInterval, so timers never drift.
future_use: Lower-third name tags and caption pages for talking heads.

what_it_is: Claude skill making 9:16 faceless kinetic-type reels: word-by-word captions, one hero object per phrase, HyperFrames.
take: Storyboard gate: no HTML until the user approves the frame-by-frame plan; then verify with snapshots, not more questions.
Edit-speed presets: calm about 2 s per frame, standard 1.4 s, rapid 0.9 s with hard cuts.
Without speech-to-text, estimate word times from the voice's loudness envelope, and pin hand corrections.
future_use: Faceless kinetic-type reels for non-face topics.

what_it_is: Codex skill producing fact-checked Chinese book-intro vertical videos with voice, captions, music and HyperFrames/Remotion render.
take: Keep background music 12-20 dB below narration; start by auditioning at the low end of that range.
Take caption timing from the final narration audio, never from manual guesses.
Gate the render on factual, audio, caption, layout and output-spec checks passing first; use a separate publish cover.
future_use: Music-bed level and caption-from-final-audio timing for explainer reels.

what_it_is: Grok-based AI generator for TikTok/Instagram/X videos and carousels with posting queue and xAI cost caps.
take: Nothing talking-head specific: it generates AI clips from prompts, which our rule 4 blocks without a credit yes.
Template-first habit: check for an existing template and save the research artifact before generating, which saves repeated research tokens.
Per-clip prompt contract with explicit length targets and continuity rules, if AI B-roll is ever approved.
future_use: Template-first prompt contract if AI B-roll is ever approved.

what_it_is: Remotion skill turning a topic into a 1080x1920 kinetic-text short, with reading-speed timing and safe-zone checks.
take: Use strictest platform safe zones on 1080x1920: top 288px, bottom 672px, left 96px, right 192px; keep captions and cards inside.
Time each on-screen text scene to reading speed and review a stills sheet of every scene and the frames around each cut before rendering.
Lint the script: hook payoff in about 10 words or fewer, one idea per scene, every number carries a source footer; warn past 59 s.
future_use: Safe-zone numbers and reading-speed timing for QA of any vertical reel.

what_it_is: Free local Claude Code plugin suite for talking-head edits, podcast clipping, voiced cartoons and Remotion videos.
take: edit-footage stops after picking takes and shows a keep/drop script; render only after the user OKs it. Copy that gate.
Before any download or setup, list sizes (for example about 6 GB total) in a table and wait for a yes.
snipshorts asks how many clips to make first, then picks exactly that many moments.
future_use: Keep/drop script review gate before rendering a face reel.

what_it_is: Director skill that chains cut, storyboard, build, sound and QA stages across installed video engines, with one approval gate.
take: Motion pacing: a new beat every 3-6 s, never more than two layers at once, entrances 0.25-0.4 s ease-out.
Safe zones: top 220 px, bottom 450 px, 35 px sides, right 100 px from two-thirds down; stricter than the Remotion figures in some edges, so use the strictest set.
Audio: sound effects on each visual beat under the voice, mixed to -14 LUFS and true peak under -1 dBTP.
future_use: Beat-rate and entrance-timing rules for reel motion graphics.

what_it_is: Chinese Claude Code skill turning a voice-over into a code-rendered motion video, beat-synced with 16:9 and 9:16 outputs.
take: Transcribe only the clean dry voice track; mixed audio transcribes badly, so mix after word timing.
Mix music that auto-ducks under speech, loudnorm to -14 LUFS with a short fade-out tail; set total length to voice plus 0.5-1 s for the end card.
Snap cut points and keyword moments to a beat grid (120 BPM = 0.5 s beats) when a generated music bed is used.
future_use: Dry-voice ASR, duck-and-normalise mix and beat-snapped cuts for reels.

what_it_is: Claude Code reel kit: topic radar, hook-tested script factory, browser editor, 11 styles and a taste-rule learning loop.
take: Facts rule: every number in a script needs two independent sources in a sources table; if unconfirmed, cut it or write around it.
Hook check: 8 spoken words or fewer, 3 s or less, line 1 must not answer its own question, one spike word.
Learn from feedback: a reaction becomes a checkable rule only after the user confirms it; retire the old text by deleting it.
future_use: Sourced-claim table and confirm-before-saving rules for client learnings.

what_it_is: Claude skill that turns an approved script and talking-head footage into a 9:16 HyperFrames short with creator-grade pacing.
take: Open with an engineered hook in the first 1-3 s (pattern interrupt or split panel that grows to full frame); never open on a static talking head.
Vary cut lengths down to about 0.2 s and pace them to the script's energy; avoid uniform 1 s cuts.
Camera pushes: animate a wrapper and promote layers to the GPU (force3D) so motion is smooth in the render, not only in preview.
future_use: Hook-first openings and non-metronomic cut rhythm for face reels.

what_it_is: Free pixel-art animation engine where Claude writes deterministic per-frame JS scenes with synthesised sound.
take: Make draw(t) a pure function of time with seeded randomness and precomputed physics, so any frame can be rendered out of order (same idea as our seek(t) build).
Use palette indices, not hex, so one palette swap recolours a whole scene.
Step animation at 12 fps for a hand-animated feel.
future_use: Retro pixel-art explainer scenes if a client ever asks for that look.

what_it_is: Claude Code plugin that clones a YouTube channel's format into an original channel with scripted, voiced, scheduled episodes.
take: Fact table before the script: every claim gets a status (confirmed, alleged, reported, estimate) and a source; the script may only say what is in that table.
Rule from its production notes: when unsure, cut the claim; a shorter accurate video beats a takedown.
Shots: a new beat every 4-8 s and never a static shot longer than about 10 s; split it or add a reveal.
future_use: Claim-status fact table to back every on-screen claim for compliance.

what_it_is: Spanish-language Remotion explainer-video toolkit: script formulas, pacing table, motion-design guidance and ffmpeg recipes.
take: Pacing: narration about 150 words per minute standard, 120 complex, 170 short-form; 30 s spotlight = 3 s hook, 15 s feature, 7 s result, 5 s CTA.
Scene lengths: establishing shot 3-5 s, feature demo 5-8 s; a 30 s social video has one idea per scene.
Fit demos to voiceover with ffmpeg speed changes pre-computed; use ffmpeg rather than the renderer for speeds above 4x or below 0.25x.
future_use: Words-per-minute pacing table and 30 s feature-spotlight timing for explainer reels.

what_it_is: Codex plugin running a research-to-reel pipeline: sourced evidence, scripts, word-timed intake, HyperFrames edit and delivery.
take: Opening rhythm: an unchanged intro image lasts at most 0.5 s (1 s absolute), useful views change every 0.7-0.8 s; strongest action in first 3-5 s.
Completion gates: a stage counts as done only with a verified artifact or live URL, not a file upload or plan; user approval must be recorded.
Script check counts spoken words and beats before filming; the real timing comes from the recorded take.
future_use: Opening pacing limits and artifact-verified stage gates for reel jobs.

what_it_is: Skill that breaks a viral short into hook, beats and CTA, then rebuilds it around your subject (paid renders).
take: Teardown first: keep the reference's line count, per-line timing budget and shot count, and replace only the content.
Show the teardown, shot list and rebuild plan together and get approval before any paid call.
Before the first paid call, price the whole batch from live prices; the first insufficient-balance error stops the whole batch.
future_use: Structure-only teardown of studied reels, plus batch price-before-spend rule.

what_it_is: Local MIT tool (ShortsFlow) that clips long talks into face-tracked 9:16 shorts with word captions and a quality benchmark.
take: Tighten: remove silences and pauses between words but never a spoken word; keep laughter and applause.
Measure clip quality with a benchmark: starts and ends on sentence boundaries, face found rate, crop jitter (about 0.02 on their talking-head tests), silence share.
Two-person framing: combine a face detector with voice-pitch clustering; mouth motion alone was weak on real footage.
future_use: Benchmark metrics for crop jitter and sentence-boundary cuts in QA.

what_it_is: Russian-language Claude/Codex montage engine: speaker video to captioned, graphic-rich reels with motion layers and QA.
take: Audio recipe for voice-over: music at about -16 dB, ducked -40 dB under speech with ratio 4; final target -14 LUFS, true peak at or below -1.5 dBTP.
Before rendering a preview, a critic pass scores each scene on five axes and returns a JSON list of fixes; then re-render.
Preview QA: no black gaps between scenes, one 48 kHz track, frame size and fps checked, and a contact sheet of the current preview.
future_use: Ducking recipe and critic-pass QA step for reel previews.

what_it_is: Spanish-language Claude skills making animated voxel-character dialogue shorts for TikTok and YouTube with per-character ElevenLabs voices.
take: Voice plan before spend: a dry-run command lists voices and characters without calling the voice API, then the paid render runs.
Pacing by platform: TikTok 40-60 s in 6-8 scenes; YouTube 60-90 s in 7-10 scenes; no more than two two-person scenes in a row.
Each speaker gets its own voice ID stored in a profile file, not in code.
future_use: Dry-run-before-paid-voice step for any animated or narrated format.

what_it_is: Chinese-language end-to-end video pipeline from topic and sources to HyperFrames MP4, covers and publish pack.
take: Caption contract: formal captions come from acoustic alignment of the real narration audio, stored as JSON with display rules; never estimated by hand.
Covers: generate a text-free key visual first, then set the title with HyperFrames typography, and check full size and phone thumbnail.
Keep a source record for every factual item and package the evidence with the final files.
future_use: Aligned-caption JSON contract and source record for every claim.

what_it_is: Claude Code skill adding 36 Remotion-rendered overlay effects to face-camera clips, with local person cutout for text behind the head.
take: Put text behind the head by layering a local person matte over the graphic, so the cutout does the occlusion.
Cutout frame rate is a quality knob: 30 fps is smoother on fast motion but takes about twice as long than 15 fps.
Show a render checklist (face found, cutout, text behind head, grade, export) while the render runs so the user sees each step pass.
future_use: Behind-the-head text via person matte for spotlight-style overlays.

what_it_is: Claude skill making 9:16 cartoon shorts from SVG scenes keyed to voice lines, with synthesized music and a contact-sheet QA.
take: Key every animation to voice-line IDs (line start, mid-line, line end), so re-voicing a line moves its visuals with it.
Keep text out of y 1340-1560, bottom 300 px and right 120 px; check one contact sheet for readable frame 0, a change every 2-3 s, no empty frames.
Master encode: PNG frames then x264 CRF 10, AAC at 320 kb/s, mixed to -14 LUFS.
future_use: Line-ID keyed motion and contact-sheet safe-area check.

what_it_is: Korean-language skill that analyses a reference Short, adapts it 30%+, then drives storyboard, image and video generation.
take: Adaptation rule: keep the emotional beat structure but change setting, character, key prop and payoff by at least 30%, shown in a checkbox change table.
Cost per clip is listed by engine ($1.20, $0.45, $0.05, $0) and mapped to emotion; run a dry-run cost check and get a yes before generating.
Forensic score of a reference: hook, narrative arc, open loops, payoff, and a viral score out of 10 from the same checklist each time.
future_use: Reference-adaptation change table and dry-run cost gate for studied reels.

what_it_is: Hosted paid skill that swaps the person, outfit or product in a short, or adapts a viral template.
take: Nothing reusable for face reels: it swaps a digital person or outfit into the shots, which breaks our no-invented-on-screen-content rule and the paid-generation rule.
Spend gate pattern: restate the exact plan and get a yes before any credit-spending call; poll render status no faster than every 30 s.
Renders take about 3-8 minutes; tell the user the job is running and keep checking at a fixed interval.
future_use: Only the spend-approval gate pattern is worth keeping.

what_it_is: Vietnamese-language content and Facebook ads kit: ideas, scripts, 9:16 video, ad policy linting, fatigue watch and reports.
take: Ad-copy linter with BLOCK and REVIEW levels: flags personal attributes, before/after claims, body-outcome claims and unprovable superlatives; output says it is not legal advice.
Only call a result when the sample is big enough: at least 3 days and 2,000 impressions per ad; below that write 'not enough data'.
Fatigue rule: compare each ad against its own first 3 days; two or more signals (frequency at least 3, CTR down 25%, CPM up 30%) means refresh.
future_use: Compliance pre-flight linter for client ad and reel copy.

what_it_is: Portuguese skill and Python CLI turning a topic or link into a validated JSON edit plan for approval.
take: Plan first: emit a renderer-agnostic JSON edit plan, run a validator where any error blocks render, then write a human summary for approval.
Hook in the first 3 s: pattern interrupt and an open loop; the plan's hook beat must state its caption timing in seconds.
Preset profiles set cut length, transitions, music and caption style together (for example viral uses about 1.1 s cuts at energy 0.95).
future_use: Validate-then-approve plan file as the beat-sheet gate.

what_it_is: Mac-local skill that cuts raw talks into tight full edits and 9:16 clips with virtual-camera reframing and word captions.
take: Captions: one sans family in two weights, mixed case, warm off-white with soft shadow not thick stroke, one accent colour on at most one word per video.
Cross-check transcripts from two speech models and flag doubtful words for a human look before captions are burned in.
Clips: 3-6 standalone clips cut on word boundaries and reframed by a virtual camera that follows the speaker.
future_use: Caption typography rules and two-model transcript cross-check.

what_it_is: Code-first video pipeline: expressive cloned narration with word timings, React scenes cued on words, GPU render and export check.
take: Cue on words, cut on lines: every reveal fires on a word start time from captions.json, never a guessed frame number.
9:16 safe areas: keep captions out of the bottom ~20% and right ~12%; at most about 8 words per phrase; show the promise by about 2 s.
Mix to -14 LUFS with a -1.5 dBTP ceiling, and look at stills of the busiest frames before any full render.
future_use: Word-cued reveals from caption timings and 9:16 safe-area numbers.

what_it_is: Noncommercial Claude skill for motion-graphic promos and reels built on the onetake engine, with curated rules and motion library.
take: Word-to-action table: every spoken word maps to one visible action per beat; nothing appears without a word cue.
Check early, middle and final construction frames of each beat as stills, and trial one 5-9 s beat before the full render.
Motion as numbers: letter drops use damping ratio 0.5 and a 0.055 s stagger; typed text runs about 38 characters per second.
future_use: Word-to-action table and beat-trial workflow for motion cards.

what_it_is: Chinese skill turning a WeChat article into a 9:16 Remotion video that keeps every source image uncropped.
take: Never crop source images: use object-fit contain on every picture; any cover-style crop fails review.
Image belongs to the paragraph just before it; if a paragraph has no image, use a text scene rather than forcing one.
Hold single-image scenes at most 6 s; carousel slides 1.5-3 s; at most 5 text elements per screen plus one non-text visual.
future_use: Uncropped-asset rule and per-scene hold limits for explainer cuts.

what_it_is: Claude skills that turn a context into a narrated Remotion video with TTS voice, generated artwork and measured scene timing.
take: Audio drives length: measure each voice file and set scene durations from it, not from a guessed reading time.
Show the narration and get a yes before paid voice or image generation; re-runs skip any voice or image that already exists.
Safe area at 1080 wide: 80 px sides, 100 px top and bottom; keep headlines 84 px or larger; spell numbers as words in narration.
future_use: Measure-voice-then-set-duration rule and cache-skip on re-render.

what_it_is: Tutorial documenting a YouTube Short diagnosis, FFmpeg measurement and HyperFrames rebuild into 16:9 and 9:16 versions.
take: Measure the original before re-cutting: hard-cut count, mean and median shot length, and number of shots under 1 s, using FFmpeg scene detection.
Keep a sources file: every number in the script must appear there with its origin, or it does not go in.
Test the 9:16 crop on a contact sheet with the crop box drawn; a centre crop cut titles and subtitles in their test.
future_use: FFmpeg shot-length measurement and source-logged numbers for analysis of reference reels.

what_it_is: Polish local dashboard app that writes Claude scripts and renders ElevenLabs-voiced 9:16 reels with Remotion.
take: Narration budget at 170 words per minute: about 72 words for 30 s, 108 for 45 s, 145 for 60 s, 217 for 90 s.
Each scene is only two fields, what the voice says and what is on screen; edit one and rebuild only that scene.
Keep API keys in a local data folder excluded from the repo, entered once in the dashboard.
future_use: Words-per-second script budget for face-reel length planning.

what_it_is: Claude Code skill building flat 2D stick-figure story shorts in Remotion with synthesized audio and A/B choice format.
take: Audio target: about -17 LUFS integrated with the voice always loudest and a bed underneath; our standard is -14 LUFS, so keep the level step explicit.
Cut rhythm: hard cuts every 2-6 s (about 20 per 75-80 s part); review stills at the hook, every card and each cut before rendering.
Caption keywords get one highlight colour; sound effects and music beds are synthesized in code, so no licensed samples.
future_use: Cut-interval guide and synthesized-SFX approach for sound-light reels.

what_it_is: Hosted-service CLI and skills that make AI influencer UGC videos for mobile apps, billed in credits.
take: Nothing reusable for face reels: it invents synthetic people and testimonial-style posts, which breaks our rules against invented testimonials and unapproved paid generation.
Cost gate: generate the cheap still first (2 credits), show the user, then spend on video (7 for 5 s, 13 for 10 s), never in the same turn.
Pre-spend credit table in each plan so the user sees the total before approval.
future_use: Approval-gate pattern for any future paid generation step.

what_it_is: Chinese skill building 9:16 and 16:9 podcast videos with waveform, burned subtitles and ffprobe-checked outputs.
take: Subtitle hygiene: a banned-fragment list drops ASR hallucinations from music, silence and outros; a correction table fixes names and terms.
Waveform amplitude uses a square-root scale, not linear; linear makes speech look flat.
Render a 10-30 s sample per orientation first, then check resolution, fps, duration and codecs with ffprobe before the full render.
future_use: ASR hallucination filter and sample-first render check.

what_it_is: MIT skill adding 47 ffmpeg/OpenCV effects (glitch, zooms, intros, phone and chat mockups) to 9:16 clips.
take: Preview on the first few seconds before a full render, and always write a new output file so the original is never overwritten.
Short intro effects with fixed lengths work as hook openers: a 0.8 s zoom from 80% to 100%, or a 2.5-3 s photo-card open.
Keep a third-party notices file that lists each bundled model and its licence (OFL font, Apache person matte, MIT face detector).
future_use: Preview-first render habit and notices file for bundled models.

what_it_is: Claude Code skill and HyperFrames template for 1080x1920 paper-collage reels with cut-out people and typed paper labels.
take: Beat table per 6 s scene: label 0.3 s, document 0.48 s, punch word 1.0 s, person sticker 1.35 s, second word 3.3 s, exit 0.9 s before end.
Cut-out people are die-cut stickers 600-900 px wide with a 14 px white border; use CC0 photos only and log each source in a credits file.
Typing rhythm: letters 40 ms apart (45 ms for caps), each landing from 1.8x scale to 1x.
future_use: Scene beat table with fixed timestamps for motion cards.

what_it_is: Claude-driven short-video studio that draws explainers with code and renders them locally.
take: Platform UI covers the bottom 200 px and right 120 px on Douyin; verify the equivalent zones for each target platform on 1080x1920.
Compute every number in Python before it goes into the copy; never type a figure by hand.
Agree the style on a few keyframe stills before the full render, since full renders are slow.
future_use: Safe-zone and number-check rules for any explainer overlay.

what_it_is: Agent skill that turns a topic or script into a verified explainer video, with a presenter or styled scenes.
take: Lock the narration audio first and use its recorded durations as the master clock for cuts, captions and graphics.
Run ASR on the final audio and check for omissions, additions and wrong names before any visuals are timed.
Record each user decision in a job file so a resumed job keeps the agreed route.
future_use: Audio-first timing and ASR verification for every voice track.

what_it_is: HeyGen agent skills for creating paid AI avatar presenter videos, translations and avatars.
take: Paid avatar generation sits outside our free-first rule; use only after a cost check and an explicit yes.
Script budget for presenter videos: about 75 words per 30 seconds, about 150 per 60 seconds.
Check the source image's aspect ratio and correct framing before submitting it to the video API.
future_use: Only if a client approves a paid AI presenter route.

what_it_is: Claude skill that builds a 16:9 or 9:16 avatar video from a URL or script, with animated backgrounds and captions.
take: Avatar layout sizes: corner inset about 28% of width in 16:9; centred bottom about 58% in 9:16; side panel about 42% full height.
Never show the same avatar look in two scenes in a row; change the pattern in each video.
Use the slide-in entrance (0.6 s ease-out) once or twice per video, after a full-screen scene.
Write the script the way people speak it; flat read-aloud text sounds synthetic.
future_use: Layout sizes and slide-in rule for picture-in-picture reels.

what_it_is: Skill that turns a long article into a presenter video project with planned visuals and a release quality gate.
take: Keep the presenter out of key text and caption safe areas; never leave a large presenter static over 12 s without a layout or camera change.
Preview a new avatar or voice with a 10-15 s clip first and review lip sync, teeth and face-edge jitter.
Final export must pass a written quality gate; a failed result blocks delivery.
future_use: Preview-first and static-presenter timing rules for talking-head cuts.

what_it_is: Claude Code skill wrapping the HeyGen API for avatar videos, with batch runs, cost estimates and downloads.
take: SKIP: HeyGen API tooling; our simulate_cost rule already covers the cost-first idea.
Cost formula is seconds times rate; HeyGen Video Agent is about $0.0333 per second, Photo Avatar IV $0.05 per second.
Re-fetch generated video links before they expire so paid output is not lost.
future_use: Pricing reference only if a paid avatar route is approved.

what_it_is: Codex skill that makes a 9:16 Chinese football-prediction talking-head video with captions, logos and sound.
take: Keep graphics in phone-safe geometry: nothing at x 0-56 or y 0-110, and critical content 48 px from the left and right edges.
Measure the rendered caption box, not the CSS: one line, left edge at or beyond 48 px, right edge at or before 1032 px on 1080 wide.
Before timing captions, align ASR text to the approved script and block the run if similarity is under 0.80.
Keep the clean source frame rate (25 fps stays 25 fps) and do not convert it unless required.
future_use: Phone-safe zone numbers and caption-box measurement for every reel.

what_it_is: Skill wrapping the LightX2V cloud API for image, video, speech and voice-clone generation.
take: Task pattern: submit, poll task status until SUCCEED or FAILED, then fetch the result URL by output name.
List the available model cards by task type before submitting, so model names are never guessed.
Needs a cloud token and spends cloud credits; keep it behind the same paid-generation approval as other providers.
future_use: Alternative provider for talking-head or image-to-video shots if approved.

what_it_is: Cloud-based Claude skills that build avatar talking-head reels with B-roll, cloned voices and spatial sound.
take: Frame picker: keep frames with exactly one face (BlazeFace), score sharpness on the face box only, reject zero or two-plus faces.
Ambient bed cleanup before mixing: highpass 35 Hz, lowpass 12 kHz, light noise reduction; narration must stay dominant.
Check panning with per-channel RMS over a window, so left and right levels match what is on screen.
Default bed target is -16 LUFS; use -28 for quiet indoor beds so near-silent beds do not lift hiss.
future_use: Face-aware frame selection and bed cleanup for reel audio.

what_it_is: Claude Code skill that turns one portrait and a script into a paid talking-avatar video via the Beatra platform.
take: Planning, auditioning or comparing does not count as approval; only a clear instruction to render that exact item does.
Before paid synthesis, check the portrait's real MIME type, size and alpha, and recheck audio duration against the model card.
Price a whole batch first; the first insufficient-balance error stops the batch until the user says to resume.
future_use: Approval wording and batch-stop rule for any paid generation.

what_it_is: Skill for coded motion-art explainers: 36 art styles, 9 explainer grammars, a shot-table lint and render checks.
take: Storyboard lint before building: every shot row names object, action and camera; with --script, on-screen numbers must match the spoken script.
Vary camera moves by paragraph: no three push-ins in a row; follow a push with a pull-out, pan or hard cut; fast moves only for reveals and key numbers.
Real footage or screenshots fill the frame; code adds annotation and camera moves only, and any chart without client data is marked ILLUSTRATION.
future_use: Shot-table lint and number-matching check for every explainer.

what_it_is: Skill that turns a Chinese story or ordered images into silent hand-drawn 3:4 Remotion videos with generated lettering.
take: Caption breaks follow Chinese word boundaries and punctuation, never leaving a 2-3 character tail; landscape captions normally run 8-18 characters.
Storyboard density: ordinary still 4-8 s; split any still over 12 s; a still over 16 s is a missing-visual defect.
Use a fixed BGM volume with no per-line ducking; check the encoded MP4 for black frames, silence and loudness, keeping 3 dB true-peak headroom.
future_use: Caption tail audit and still-length rule for talking-head B-roll.

what_it_is: Claude skills that draw cartoon, anime and crayon films frame by frame in code, with captions and overlays.
take: Animate characters on twos for poses and faces; keep camera moves on ones so motion stays smooth.
For big actions use anticipation, then snap, then overshoot (spring); a hit gets a 2-3 frame impact frame.
Every frame is a pure function of time: no Math.random and no state between frames, so re-renders match.
future_use: Motion timing for any cartoon or B-roll the agency later makes.

what_it_is: Chinese-language AI animation workflow kit with stage roles, skills, standards and local render tools.
take: Before any new generation, state whether to reuse, fill gaps or start over, with the cost in time, tokens and paid calls; reuse valid outputs.
Resume from the real current stage and reuse finished results instead of restarting a long job.
Write new outputs to a fresh project folder; never edit shared examples or templates.
future_use: Reuse-first rule for client B-roll and reel assets.

what_it_is: Two Claude skills for code-made videos: painted watercolour cartoons and kinetic-type motion reels.
take: Facts are sacred: a figure appears only if it comes from the supplied source, with its scope stated; schematic content is labelled SCHEMATIC.
Every shot gets a list of reads: what the viewer must understand, in order, with times; one read at a time.
No noise whooshes on transitions; about half of cuts get no sound, and the next shot's own entrance sound carries the cut.
future_use: Facts-with-scope and labelling rules for any on-screen number.

what_it_is: Guided Codex/WorkBuddy skill that walks a user through an image-story video, stage by stage with gates.
take: Each turn states five things: current stage, what I will do, the one to three inputs needed, the deliverable, and the next step after approval.
Image count comes from narration length: 10-12 s per image gives 50-60 images per 10 minutes; 6-8 s gives 75-100.
Never dump the full workflow on the user; reveal only the current gate.
future_use: Gate-by-gate intake format for new client reels.

what_it_is: Claude Code skill that makes a 15-25 second stick-figure What-If episode with ElevenLabs voice, drawn as SVG in Remotion.
take: Cut on the word: land each cut 2 frames before its word; the genre runs about 27 cuts per minute in its opening.
Align each sound by its attack, not the file start, and place a hit that illustrates a word in the pause after it.
Master the episode to -14 LUFS and report the ElevenLabs credits spent per run.
future_use: Cut-on-word timing and attack-aligned SFX for explainer shorts.

what_it_is: Procedural risograph films and prints in Canvas 2D, each self-contained HTML, with Claude skills for film, score and still.
take: Audio gate: integrated loudness within 1 LU of target, true peak under -1 dBTP, and any WARN resolved or recorded.
Sync gate for hits: onset within about 40 ms after the visible mark, never more than 20 ms before it.
Score length equals picture length exactly, so the muxed MP4 never drifts.
future_use: Loudness and sync gates for any finished reel audio.

what_it_is: Chinese-language skill that directs xianxia camera moves, storyboards and per-shot image-to-video prompts.
take: Shot count by duration: 10-15 s uses 3 shots; 16-24 s uses 4-5; 25-35 s uses 6; 36-45 s uses 7-8; 46-60 s uses 9-11.
Each shot has one motion purpose and one dominant move; tag its speed as still, slow, mid, fast or stop, and vary it by beat.
Normal narrative shots run 4-6 s; a chase or impact may use 1.5-3 s shots followed by a readable settle.
future_use: Shot-count-by-duration table for any B-roll sequence.

what_it_is: Chinese comic-storyboard narration video skill: one character IP, synced Edge TTS narration, dense stills and encoded QA.
take: Storyboard density: 4-8 s per still; allow 8-12 s only for a deliberate hold; split anything over 12 s.
Rotate shot types: wide, medium action, two-shot, over-shoulder, hand or object close-up, environmental insert.
Check the encoded MP4 itself for black frames, silence, loudness and keyframes; a browser preview is not the deliverable.
future_use: Still-length and shot-rotation rules for talking-head B-roll.

what_it_is: Coding-agent skill that makes a short self-introduction film starring a creator as a 3D vinyl toy, rendered in Blender.
take: Story first: write down the person's own personal moment and what they are known for before choosing visuals, even if unused.
Sound by ear: play several sound options under the animatic and let the user pick before the final score.
Author's length note: about 22 s for two points, 30 s or more for three.
future_use: Story-first intake for any creator or personal-brand film.

what_it_is: Claude skill that makes hand-drawn 2D animations entirely in JavaScript, with a detail library, rigs and synthesized sound.
take: Snap, then hold: a pop changes in 1-2 frames (0.04-0.07 s) then holds; put the ease on the settle, not on the change.
Overshoot on pop-ins: back-ease with s about 1.8-2.2 over 0.3-0.4 s.
Sound cue time is the contact frame minus about 0.03 s, so hits land just before the picture, not after it.
future_use: Snap-and-hold motion timing for any animated title or graphic.

what_it_is: Korean-language skill for 15-90 second motion-graphics and character videos, with gated stages and numeric checks.
take: For AI-generated clips, check the start frame, then look at strips at 0, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0 and 3.0 s; clothes and faces drift after 1-2 s.
SSIM-type numbers do not catch identity drift; use them only for the start-frame match and check the rest by eye.
Set cut lengths on beat multiples and round each start frame once, from the cumulative time.
future_use: Clip-drift check for any approved AI-generated B-roll.

what_it_is: Claude skills that drive Blender for short 3D films: storyboard, set building, physics motion and overnight render.
take: Storyboard first: every shot gets its camera move, timing and sound before anything is built.
Make two sound versions (calm and full) and choose by ear; the calm one won because the hero stayed the star.
Copy the .blend before replaying scripts that edit materials, since several passes are not safe to re-run.
future_use: 3D product or car films, if the agency takes on that format.

what_it_is: Claude skills that draw every frame of a short animation in JavaScript, with a beat-locked synthesized soundtrack.
take: Cut on the beat with a chord change, not a volume accent; a loud accent on a cut reads as a jump scare.
Keep jumps at scene cuts under about +6 dB; bring layers in one or two per bar, since a simultaneous entry measured +11 dB.
Let the music break into silence for a bar before the payoff; a silent break is the strongest beat in a short.
future_use: Music-bed level and cut-jump checks for every reel.

what_it_is: Claude Code skill that builds animated YouTube Shorts in Blender from one idea, with gated story, build and critic steps.
take: Never self-score: a fresh critic agent grades the render; the builder's own score ran about 2 points high.
QA is pass or fail per line, with at most two fix rounds; then show the user what still fails.
Passing the numbers is not passing: a gate passed 37/37 while a night insert was a magenta wash, so look at every still.
future_use: Independent critic pass before any client reel is previewed.

what_it_is: Chinese-language Claude skill making hand-drawn diary-comic videos: text, line art and colour revealed per sentence in Remotion.
take: Override estimated scene timing with the real TTS audio durations before rendering, so visuals never drift from the voice.
Derive the black line-art layer from the finished colour still locally with ffmpeg, so both layers share one composition.
Reveal each sentence in three passes (text, line art, colour) with the same left-to-right wipe direction.
future_use: Duration-from-audio sync for any illustrated narration.

what_it_is: Chinese Remotion starter for paper-cut poetry films: reusable paper-layer components and a step-by-step skill.
take: Paper layer component: spring-in entrance, slow breathing float and drop shadow; the user fills only a spec.
Render Chinese text in code rather than on an image, so the characters are exact.
Give foreground and background layers different depth roles, or the whole frame drifts together with no depth.
future_use: Layer entrance and float presets for a non-talking-head explainer format.

what_it_is: Claude skill that makes 20-60 second stick-figure story films drawn in code with Remotion and ElevenLabs word-timed voice.
take: Animation carries each idea so it reads with sound off; keep always-on text to one plain subtitle line.
Never use fact cards, title cards or chips; show the fact by acting it out with props and camera.
Check the mix by measurement (levels and loudness per stem), not by ear alone.
future_use: Show-don't-tell rule for explainer shorts.

what_it_is: Three.js walkable scroll of a classical Chinese essay, with original text beside each scene and a fixed procedural world.
take: Fixed random seed for every procedural element, so the world is identical on each open and each render.
Connected walkable geometry: no floating islands or sandbox bases; far terrain continues naturally into the distance.
Offer a reduced-motion option that keeps story camera moves but stops ambient particles and transitions.
future_use: Seeded procedural backgrounds for any generated set.

what_it_is: Agent-operated canvas for short AI videos: storyboard, scene stills, and Grok 6-or-10-second video generation.
take: Narrow the agent's tools to the single generation tool; a broad run cost about $0.50 for no output, while the narrow run cost $0.054.
Each 6 or 10 s clip is built from three locked stills (first, mid, last); longer stories are several scenes.
The human reviews prompts and generates; the agent never triggers paid generation on its own.
future_use: Narrow tool permissions for any approved AI-clip generation.

what_it_is: Desktop panel that drives the cinecode skill to script, score and render films from an idea or script.
take: Each scene shows whether its words fit its seconds, so the user fixes pacing before any render.
Script approval gate: title, logline, look and a timed scene list are reviewed before anything renders.
Sound-only fixes rebuild only the sound, not the picture; notes come back as a new final.
future_use: Words-fit-seconds check and script gate before any reel render.

what_it_is: Claude skill that makes narrated 2D storybook films: story, ElevenLabs voice, word-timed SVG animation drawn in Remotion.
take: Start each visual change 2-6 frames before its spoken word so it reads as the word causing it.
Keep music and effects 12-18 dB under the voice; check the final mix at about -14 LUFS.
One camera move per beat, eased; a long beat gets a slow push, never several moves at once.
future_use: Lead-the-word cue timing and level rules for talking-head B-roll.

what_it_is: Chinese-language skill and engine that recreates pixel-character dialogue videos: typed text, blips and 8-bit music from one JSON.
take: Reading time for on-screen rule cards: 0.032 s per Chinese character, minimum 1 s, so each line can be read.
Typing blip: triangle wave around 520 Hz at volume 0.05; cap English at about 20 blips per second.
Put stamps over numbers, not over labels, so the label stays readable.
future_use: Per-character reading time for any text-heavy reel card.

what_it_is: Claude skill for vertical 3D cartoon story Shorts in three.js with a RicksClips-style script formula and voice timing.
take: State an odd act as a fact in line 1 and show its consequence within the first 3 seconds.
Target 35-45 s at about 4 words per second; end the last line mid-sentence so it loops back to line 1.
Reference stems measured separately: voice near -15 LUFS, music about 10 dB lower, sound effects lower still.
future_use: Hook formula and stem-level loudness checks for talking-head shorts.

what_it_is: Chinese SRT-to-storyboard pipeline: splits subtitles into 2-6 s shots, writes illustration prompts, generates images and a silent stitched video.
take: An LLM returns only cue numbers for shot boundaries; deterministic code copies text and timestamps from the source SRT, avoiding transcription errors and saving tokens.
Validate the plan in code: each cue appears exactly once, segments are contiguous (next start = previous end + 1), first starts at 1, last ends at total.
Target 2-6 s per shot; a single cue longer than 6 s stays whole and is flagged rather than split.
future_use: Script-to-shot planning for faceless explainer or B-roll sequences.

what_it_is: Claude Code plugin synthesizing music and drawing every frame in code for short animated films, with storyboard approval.
take: Plan in bars: at 120 BPM one beat is 0.5 s and one bar is 2 s; put cuts on bar lines.
Use the silence-then-drop shape only when the story has a real suspense moment; it is a tool, not a default.
Measure loudness and true peak on the finished render, then verify before delivery.
future_use: Music-led explainer films for non-talking-head formats.

what_it_is: Chinese Claude skill orchestrating Seedance, Kling and music/TTS generation plus FFmpeg cuts from a storyboard with consistency checks.
take: Real-person photos are routed to Kling-Omni; the skill bans Seedance for real-human footage.
Storyboard lighting must match the time state (daytime shots never get sunset or moonlight wording); key objects get locked style descriptions.
A storyboard validation step must pass before any paid generation call.
future_use: AI B-roll for fictional scenes; read its real-person rules first.

what_it_is: Claude skill that writes, voices and assembles 3-5 minute faceless vertical story videos from AI illustrations with word-timed captions.
take: Aim for a new visual every 3-5 seconds, and a cold open inside the first 3 seconds before the title card.
Captions use per-word voice timestamps where the voice provider supplies them (ElevenLabs), so subtitles match the audio exactly.
Character, location and prop reference sheets from several angles are the references for every scene, which keeps faces consistent.
future_use: Narrated story formats and reference-sheet consistency for recurring characters.

what_it_is: Skill for authoring Lottie JSON animations verified in a Skia Skottie player, with lower-third, data and logo recipes.
take: Serious or data content uses calm ease-out with no bounce; playful content may overshoot.
Hard-cut on action at a seam: the focal element is still moving when the cut lands, so the eye hides the content jump.
State easing terms, fps and duration up front, and verify in the real player rather than from isolated JSON.
future_use: Lower thirds and data callouts for finance graphics.

what_it_is: Claude/Codex skill that vectorizes a raster logo into minimal smooth SVG, then choreographs logo motion from brand personality words.
take: Low-energy serious brands use 400-800 ms part timing, 50-100 ms anticipation and 0-15% exaggeration.
Anticipation is 20-30% of the main action's duration; a 750 ms assembly gets a 150-220 ms wind-up.
Do not squash or stretch a precise, trustworthy or premium mark; use plain scale transforms instead.
future_use: End-card logo reveal timing for mortgage brand marks.

what_it_is: Codex skill making a 5-second halftone paper-collage B-roll clip from one voiceover line via Gemini Omni, behind three approval gates.
take: Three gates: approve the metaphor only, then one colour still, then spend on video; nothing paid runs before the still is approved.
Check the first frame is an empty colour field and the end frame matches the still before accepting an assemble-from-empty clip.
Delivery spec is 720x1280, 24 fps, 5 s, silent; the audio track is stripped on purpose.
future_use: Abstract-concept B-roll, only with paid generation approved.

what_it_is: Apache-2.0 code-drawn illustration and film engine with 32 styles, deterministic frame output, narration and score synthesis.
take: Every frame is a pure function of time, so the same source redraws identical pixels at any size and length.
Ask the user before any score work and never download sound libraries without asking.
Separate the content from the look layer, so one explainer can be restyled without rewriting the scene.
future_use: Illustrated explainer stills for non-talking-head client formats.

what_it_is: Chinese Codex skill making sticker packs, lenticular cards, posters, signatures, title cards and storybook animations from images and text.
take: Check the exported file itself, not the preview: sample frames from the delivered GIF or MP4 before calling it done.
Keep the user's approved style and assets; fill only what is missing rather than redoing the project.
Storybook motion: fixed composition, real 6 fps, one action per page of about 3 s, hold 0.5-1 s after each action.
future_use: Animated title cards and signature intros for client brand moments.

what_it_is: Codex skill producing hand-drawn black-canvas architecture diagrams as editable Excalidraw, PNG and animated GIF with flow highlights.
take: Flow loop spec: 1210x1138 canvas, 20 fps, 41 frames (2.05 s), with flow highlights moving along the connectors.
Each GIF ships with an editable .excalidraw source and a PNG preview, so the diagram can be changed without rebuilding it from scratch.
Spec is JSON with fixed copy-length guidance, so text fit is decided before rendering.
future_use: Process or system diagrams for explainer segments.

what_it_is: Repository could not be cloned (not found), so no content was reviewed.
take: Repository deleted or private (HTTP 404 on clone); nothing could be read.
future_use: Unknown; re-check if the repo reappears.

what_it_is: Claude/Codex skill for hand-drawn architecture, workflow and swimlane diagrams with editable Excalidraw, PNG/SVG, GIF/MP4 and interactive HTML.
take: Pick the layout by content: panorama for systems (2-6 inputs, 2-4 core cards), swimlane for category bands, graph for custom loops.
Minimum frame counts: draw 72, relay 88, trace 88, chapter 96, failure-recovery 96 frames at 20 fps.
Bundled OFL fonts (Excalifont and a Noto Sans SC subset) make the output look the same on any machine.
future_use: Architecture or process diagrams for explainer segments.

what_it_is: Agent workflow making Risograph two-ink 1080x1920 info-animation B-roll from transcript lines, with approval gates and automated QA.
take: On-screen words must come verbatim from the transcript: delete or line-break only, never reword; leave blank any category the speaker did not name.
Without a real screenshot, show a replace-me placeholder, never a drawn UI.
QA errors block delivery: text must stay in y 168-1330, and text under 100 px uses only the dark ink for contrast.
Output has no audio track; voice, music and captions are added in the editor.
future_use: Stat and comparison B-roll for talking-head explainers.

what_it_is: Claude skill turning a 5-second voiceover line into a halftone paper-collage explainer clip via MaxFusion image and video generation.
take: Colour meanings are fixed as part of the visual system, so a series reads consistently.
Optional voiceover is trimmed to silence, fitted into a 4-5 s window and muxed without touching the video stream.
Same three-gate flow as gbro-collage-broll; this copy adds the voiceover step.
future_use: Abstract-metaphor B-roll for non-talking-head segments.

what_it_is: Claude skill generating full-code motion-graphic films from one sentence, with music synthesized in code and print-style looks.
take: Loudness target depends on the look: dark-tech about -9.4 LUFS, warm or slow about -13 LUFS, true peak below -0.5 dBTP.
AAC encoding can push true peaks 0.3-1.0 dB above sample peaks; set the sample-peak ceiling at 0.82-0.86 or use 384k AAC.
Choose bars so duration = bars x 240 / BPM is exact, e.g. 24 s = 12 bars at 120 BPM (2.0 s per bar).
Never apply a second sRGB encode on output; it lifts all shadows about 2.5x.
future_use: Music-grid timing and loudness checks for motion-heavy films.

what_it_is: Four agent skills for Remotion motion graphics: mandatory format intake, editorial highlights, cinematic camera moves and terminal inserts.
take: interpolate extends by default; clamp both sides, or a count-up overshoots (a target of 12,400 once reached 30,793).
Proportional digits jitter while counting; use tabular figures for count-up numbers.
Stagger entrances 3-5 frames apart at 30 fps; reserve the exit inside the duration (a 0.5 s exit in a 5 s clip starts at 4.5 s).
Editorial inserts ban neon, glow and gradient wash; a first-pass rejection gate checks for them.
future_use: Count-up stat reveals and editorial inserts for finance explainers.

what_it_is: Codex skill producing WeChat-ready animated Chinese meme sticker packs of 240x240 GIFs, gated on whether people would actually send them.
take: Sendability gate: each item needs a real chat trigger, a readable gag at 240x240 and a concrete send scenario.
Dense-frames mode asks the image model for 8 genuinely different frames in one 2x4 sheet, the smoothest source for animation.
Strict QC rejects fake checkerboards, edge touch, bounding-box drift and loop-closure failures before a pack is built.
future_use: Sticker packs for client social channels, not reels.

what_it_is: Local Canvas animation tool and skill: scene modules drawn as pure functions of time, with checks and export.
take: Caption hold rule: on-screen time is about characters / 4.5 + 0.5 s, so copy stays readable for the whole hold.
One beat table is the single source of shot times and review times; the outgoing element overlaps the next entrance by 0.2-0.5 s.
Keep one camera across shots with monotone cubic keys, so framing never resets at a cut.
future_use: Caption timing and camera continuity for multi-shot reels.

what_it_is: Claude/Codex skill turning a character image into a keyframe-animated chat sticker pack exported to WeChat, Telegram, LINE and others.
take: The agent cannot watch a GIF, so review the generated contact sheet of frames yourself before delivery.
Per-platform specs differ: WeChat 240x240 GIF under 500 KB; LINE APNG 320x270, 5-20 frames, total play under 4 s.
Each caption is paired with a pose, motion and icon so a 16-pack covers reply, emotion and social categories.
future_use: Client sticker packs for WeChat or LINE, not reels.

what_it_is: Portuguese Claude Code skill making studio-look motion graphics from a style gallery, five questions and frame-checked MP4 output.
take: Sample frames about 0.6 s after each scene change, when things have settled, and score each 1-10; iterate until all are 8 or higher.
Pick one style before building and keep it; anchor it to a real reference rather than an adjective.
Write the brief in numbers first: size, duration, fps, hex colours and exact words.
future_use: Brief template and frame-scoring loop for every motion card.

what_it_is: Claude skill and seek-safe GSAP helper library that replaces default fades with per-property curves, distance-based durations and uneven reactions.
take: Duration from distance and weight, dur(px, weight), not a fixed 0.3-0.6 s; exits run about 0.65x the entrance time and accelerate out.
Stagger reactions at uneven offsets (0, 4, 9, 15, 22, 30 frames) behind one leader, not an even 0.08 s chain.
Written text types on character by character; supporting labels cut on instead of fading up.
future_use: Motion-card choreography in our HTML build (seek-safe GSAP).

what_it_is: Codex/Claude skill keyframing stylized Roblox R6 and R15 character animations in Blender through MCP, with GIF previews.
take: Rig-specific 3D character animation; it does not apply to talking-head reels.
Reusable rule only: no linear interpolation for main movement; use Bezier curves with slow-in and slow-out.
future_use: Only if a client asks for an animated mascot character.

what_it_is: Claude Code skill suite making, converting, editing and optimizing GIFs, including a Veo 3.1 AI route that confirms cost first.
take: Before any paid AI video call, state the model, duration and approximate cost (e.g. Veo 3.0 Fast 4 s about $0.60) and ask Proceed?
Optimise in order: lossless first, then lossy, colours, size, frame rate; budgets are Discord 256 KB, Slack 500 KB, web 2 MB.
Presets: discord 320 px, 10 fps, 128 colours; web 480 px, 15 fps, 256 colours.
future_use: Cost-confirm pattern for any paid generation; GIF size budgets for social.

what_it_is: Claude/Codex skill turning JSON specs into 1080x1920 30 fps motion-graphic MP4s, with a mandatory preview-sheet review before render.
take: Entrance 0.4-0.6 s, 70 ms per-item stagger, at least 1.2 s hold after settle, then a 0.3 s exit and a hard cut.
Render only after viewing a fresh preview sheet; passing validation only proves the shape is legal, not that the content is right.
Use only numbers the user gave or a cited source contains; run one render at a time, since parallel renders hang the engine.
future_use: Timing spec for numeric stat and steps scenes.

what_it_is: Agent skill for kinetic type: line, word and character staggers, mask and blur reveals, with CSS, GSAP and Remotion code.
take: Enter with cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); per-fragment 400-600 ms; stagger lines 60-100 ms, words 40-70 ms, characters 20-40 ms.
Mask reveal (overflow hidden, translateY 100% to 0) is the robust default; use blur-in only for short focus pulls with modest blur.
Cap total reveal near 800 ms; for long strings switch from characters to words or lines.
future_use: On-screen keyword and caption reveals in talking-head reels.

what_it_is: Codex skill for original personal-brand intro films from text, illustrations and optional images, timed to music or a beat grid.
take: Use an uploaded image only when the user supplies it or explicitly approves generation; keep source files unchanged.
Designed beat grid by character: calm 82-100 BPM, educational 100-118 BPM, energetic 118-136 BPM; hold the final lockup 0.8-1.2 s.
Keep essential text inside a 5% safe area; reserve the first 0.5-1.0 s for the hook.
future_use: Opening and lockup timing for a client brand intro.

what_it_is: Chinese handbook skill of 16 motion-graphic style cards plus a Canvas scaffold that exports MP4 with music for motion shorts.
take: A checker script runs before export: font size, contrast, platform-UI overlap, text overlap, stillness and loudness; fix findings first.
Text contrast at least 4.5:1, and sound effects land 10-20 ms before the visual they mark.
Use the first frame as the cover, and run a slide-style risk gate before rendering.
future_use: Pre-export QA script checks for every finished reel.

what_it_is: Claude/Codex skill for Manim Community Edition explanatory animations: scene code, low-quality previews, frame inspection and final verification.
take: Render a low-quality video first, inspect opening, middle and final frames, then render the requested quality.
Verify deliverables before reporting: the file exists, decodes, and has the intended dimensions, duration and format.
Check essential labels at the intended display width, not only when enlarged.
future_use: Math or algorithm explainers for non-face segments.

what_it_is: Claude skill for Remotion motion graphics: title cards, lower thirds, stat reveals, with transparent overlay export for editors.
take: Diagnose before decorating: look for real bugs, such as an unclamped interpolate, before adding effects.
A backgroundColor on the Remotion root kills the alpha channel; export overlays as ProRes or PNG sequence for editors.
Keep text inside 5-10% title-safe margins and add a scrim or backing shape over busy footage.
future_use: Transparent lower-third overlays for our reels.

what_it_is: Claude skill for motion graphics inside one seekable scene: grids, bars, cards and lines animate in order with camera pushes.
take: One scene tells one story: about 1-2 s to build, 1-2 s for the change, and at least 0.3 s held still.
Only the protagonist gets the accent colour; background information blurs 2-5 px during the action.
Appearance comes in waves, not all at once and not one by one.
future_use: Scene pacing rules for explainer segments in reels.

what_it_is: Claude/agent skill for Arabic RTL motion-graphics reels: word-by-word text, style packs, pacing numbers and platform safe zones.
take: 9:16 safe zones: top 250 px and bottom 350 px sit under platform UI; keep about 120 px clear on the right for like and comment buttons.
Word-by-word text runs 120-200 ms per word with 60-120 ms stagger; pill labels enter in 300-450 ms.
Flat explainer end cards hold 3-7.5 s: logo, then tagline, then handle rows, all staggered.
future_use: Safe-zone and end-card timing numbers for vertical reels.

what_it_is: Agent skill building frame-exact motion graphics as one HTML file on a paused timeline, with measurement checks and MP4 export.
take: Export with -pix_fmt yuv420p and +faststart; without yuv420p many platforms and QuickTime will not decode the file.
Change the canvas for each aspect ratio instead of padding; flat-colour padding leaves a visible seam where vignettes meet the edge.
Measure before animating: scenes sat 28-41 px below centre in a 1080 frame until corrected; check with getBoundingClientRect.
Two animations on one property collide: with fill both, the later one wins from time zero.
future_use: Export flags and centering checks for every HTML motion-card build.

what_it_is: Go CLI driving the Cavalry motion-graphics app: scenes, contact sheets, checks and MP4 renders, plus a PR skill.
take: When a run, check or render times out, inspect its operation ID and resume it instead of relaunching the whole job.
Start with a quick JSON diagnostic (cav check --quick --json) before a full render.
Review a 12-frame contact sheet after each change, and use onion-skin inspection to check a single move.
future_use: Resumable render jobs for long motion exports.

what_it_is: Chinese Codex skill generating short Remotion chapter transitions and motion clips from text, with a plan-and-confirm step before rendering.
take: Propose the plan first: number of clips, source text range per clip and expected files; render only after explicit confirmation.
Show sample styles in a playground and let the user pick before batch generation; do not guess the style.
Run a dry-run validation on each config before rendering the real MP4.
future_use: Confirm-then-render gate for batch chapter cards in reels.

what_it_is: Local-first 2D animation editor with an MCP server so Claude Code or Codex can build editable scenes and keyframes.
take: Agent-built scenes stay editable: layers, keyframes and easing can be tweaked by hand in the browser, then saved as a project.
MCP edits read fresh scene state before mutating, which avoids overwriting newer changes.
Setup and scene work are split into two skills, each with its own readiness checks.
future_use: Editable motion-card projects for revisions without re-rendering.

what_it_is: WebGL logo intro from an SVG logo: lens-warp close-up, wordmark pull-out, lock-in beat.
take: Logo sting shape: the mark arrives from an extreme close-up, the wordmark pulls out of it, then one lock-in beat sends a ring out.
Brand config is one JSON in logo viewBox units: background, ink and bloom palette, exitAt and skippable options.
Bloom opacity defaults to 0.88; drop it on dark grounds so the bloom does not wash out the logo.
future_use: Animated logo lock-in for a brand end card in other formats.

what_it_is: Agent skill that turns an approved og:image into a looping MP4 whose frame 0 is the still.
take: Approve the still first; video frame 0 must match it, with mean pixel difference at most 2 levels.
Seam check: last-to-first frame jump at most 1.5 ordinary frame steps, or the loop visibly breaks.
Give each element a role: a window moves whole, a button gets a pointer press and ripple, text types in.
future_use: Motion versions of approved still cards and looping end-card plates.

what_it_is: Remotion project with 39 code-drawn animation styles, one fixed five-second story redrawn in each.
take: Plan the story on six beats in a short table before any code; keep shape coordinates in the story's own space.
Render frames and look at all six before delivering; a render nobody has looked at is not verified.
future_use: Non-talking-head explainer B-roll in a chosen art style.

what_it_is: JSON spec of hand-drawn morphing line shapes, exported as animated SVG, Lottie or HTML.
take: Shapes sharing an id morph between keyframes; use 2-5 bold shapes per pose on a 1200px canvas with about 120px margin.
Stagger element delays at 0, 0.15 and 0.3 s, and give every keyframe an explicit ease curve.
future_use: Animated icons or stat callouts placed beside the speaker.

what_it_is: Claude skills for waveform audiogram videos and 3-5 second YouTube intro and outro stings.
take: Keep a logo sting to 3-5 s with the logo readable within 1-2 s; align the sound's loudest hit to the impact frame.
Shorts do not support end-screen elements; use a 2-3 s end card and a spoken call to action instead.
Trim audiograms to a soundbite under 90 s; a tight clip beats a full episode.
future_use: Logo sting timing for brand openers and Shorts end cards.

what_it_is: Directing skill for ASCII-art films on MiniMax H3: transformation chains, continuation, paid-generation gate.
