take: Pass a 7-question gate before any paid generation: one chain, clear source state, physical cause per transition, real contrast, usable exit state.
Preview the beat offline and look at it first; the paid call should be the last step, never the first test.
If the gate fails, change the mechanism or density curve rather than adding decoration.
future_use: Cost-gated preview habit before any paid AI clip.

what_it_is: Local GIF-story workshop for Codex and Claude Code: shot planning, continuity checks, MP4 assembly.
take: Inspect the first and last frames of adjacent shots with endpoint tools before accepting any join.
Paid calls run under a user-authorised cap with retries set to 0; claim success only after inspecting the returned clip.
When assembling, state aspect and fps explicitly; check for frozen starts and duplicate frames.
future_use: Bounded-call and continuity-check habits for AI B-roll.

what_it_is: Agent skill for Remotion motion graphics with hard motion rules: easing, stagger, exits, verified renders.
take: Never use linear easing; every interpolate gets a curve, and idle elements get slow sine micro-motion after about 2 s.
Entrances move 2-3 properties together (opacity, translateY, scale) over about 20 frames; exits take about 10 frames.
Stagger word and card reveals by 3-6 frames, and add a new visual element at least every 90 frames.
future_use: Motion tokens for HTML overlay cards and lower-third callouts.

what_it_is: Screenwriting and dramaturgy skills distilled from classic plays, films and series, mostly in Chinese.
take: Chekhov's rule 'start strong, end soft': open on the hardest line and let the close trail off quietly.
Ozu's method: keep the big event off-screen and write only the scene before and after it, so the reaction carries the beat.
Make the speaker choose something visible under pressure; the choice reveals who they are better than description does.
future_use: Scene turns and endings for talking-head scripts.

what_it_is: Claude and Codex video skills: shot breakdown with pixel-checked camera claims, sync panel, metadata stripping.
take: Strip source metadata with an allowlist: map one video and one audio stream only (-map_metadata -1 -map 0:v:0 -map 0:a:0?).
Metadata also hides in the H.264 SEI and the avc1 compressorname, which ffprobe does not show; grep output bytes for source strings.
Cut times come from code, the model only labels shot size and move, and any claimed camera move is checked against measured frame change.
future_use: Breakdown of reference reels, and privacy stripping before delivery.

what_it_is: Reverse-engineers a reference video into MiniMax H3 prompts, after restating its story and getting confirmation.
take: Two stages: restate what the reference shows and why its shots connect, get confirmation, and only then write prompts.
Track each object through the clip (contact, possession, occlusion, final state); never fill unknown details from common sense.
Keep the true end state of the clip, aftermath included, instead of a tidy finish.
future_use: Confirmed shot briefs from reference reels before AI clips.

what_it_is: Creative-adaptation skill: turns a reference video into a new script, shot list and segmented prompts.
take: Break a generation segment before a location change, a time jump, a costume change of the same person, or a new input asset.
Each segment restates its own start and end state; do not assume the model sees the previous clip's last frame.
Keep a segment only as long as its content needs; never stretch a short action to fill the limit.
future_use: Segment plan for AI-generated B-roll and prompt length control.

what_it_is: YouTube marketing MCP: SEO, analytics, scripts and thumbnails for long-form channels, with live data.
take: Its benchmarks (CTR 3-8%, watch time 35%+) rest on secondary sources listed in whitepapers.md; treat them as unverified.
Built for long-form tutorial channels; the algorithm rules it quotes do not map cleanly onto 9:16 face reels.
future_use: Long-form metadata pack for a client channel, if one is ever in scope.

what_it_is: Cuts a video into shots with ffmpeg, grabs thumbnails and writes shot rows to a Feishu Base.
take: ffmpeg scene detection with threshold 0.32 and minimum gap 0.45 s; if no cut is found, sample one frame every 2 s.
Make thumbnails 720 px wide; re-run at 480 px if an attachment exceeds the 20 MB limit.
Record shot size, camera move, transition and sound per row, so reel structures can be compared side by side.
future_use: Logging reference-reel shot structure for comparison.

what_it_is: Evidence-based video breakdown: transcript, keyframes, audio and BGM, each claim graded confirmed, inferred or unknown.
take: Label every claim confirmed, reasonable inference, or cannot judge; never fill a missing field from its neighbour.
Review frames in order: overview sheet, opening 10 s, transitions, body, ending; do not judge visuals from the transcript alone.
Pick the speech backend by hardware and cache the detected tools in a project file for reuse.
future_use: Structured reference-reel reports with graded evidence.

what_it_is: Chinese self-media method: positioning, topic selection, 40-second openers and five-dimension script diagnosis.
take: Open within 40 seconds with one hook type that fits the topic, and state the payoff early.
Pre-publish check: heard elsewhere? usable tomorrow? leaves the viewer hopeful? gives them something to reply to?
Merge repeats: a point said in two paragraphs is said once, and self-summary lines at paragraph ends get cut.
future_use: Hook and script review for talking-head reels.

what_it_is: Turns a Chinese voiceover into a renderer-bound storyboard spec for HyperFrames or Remotion, with hard gates.
take: Estimate runtime as Chinese characters divided by 4, then add 10-15% for pauses.
Split the piece into opening, middle and closing at roughly 15-20%, 60-70% and 10-15% of runtime.
Neighbouring shots must not share a density level; keep one emptiest and one fullest shot at least two steps apart.
future_use: Timing and density rules for any code-rendered explainer spec.

what_it_is: Breaks viral short videos into shot tables, mechanisms and machine-readable production briefs.
take: For slow continuous footage sample a frame every 3-5 seconds; a 20-60 s video should yield about 10-25 shots.
Analyse method, rhythm and structure only; do not copy exact scripts, shot sequences or creator identity.
Each shot row records time code, size, camera move, transition and emotional function.
future_use: Pre-production brief for a new reel built from a reference.

what_it_is: Skill for Vocaloid-style lyric MVs: beat analysis, concept, deterministic Canvas engine, MP4 render.
take: Every lyric line must sit within plus or minus 0.15 s of its vocal onset; check against the timeline before rendering.
Measure the beat grid first and label song sections; timing comes from the audio, not from a feel.
Make every frame a pure function of time so previews and final renders match exactly.
future_use: Caption and lyric timing checks for voiced or sung captions.

what_it_is: Pipeline for AI historical rap-battle shorts: sourced lyric notes, lip-sync prompts, captions and cover.
take: Caption legibility: bold pure-white text with a soft white glow over a dark bottom gradient; accent colour only on key words.
Each annotation card is a footnote tied to a source line on screen, so every on-screen claim traces back to its source.
future_use: Source-note cards and caption legibility for explainer shorts.

what_it_is: p5.js and p5.brush skill that paints watercolour cartoon videos frame by frame, with boiling ink lines.
take: Every frame is a pure function of time t; ink lines boil on a 12 fps grid to keep the hand-drawn feel.
Write a per-shot 'reads' list: what the viewer must understand, with a timestamp for each read.
future_use: Hand-painted intro or animated B-roll in a non-talking-head format.

what_it_is: Code-drawn music video skill: lyric timing, beat analysis, storyboard, frame rendering and self-check scripts.
take: A rhythm script measures frame difference over time to find slideshow-like still stretches and hard cuts.
Re-mux the original audio after rendering; renderers often drop loudness by 2 dB or more.
One shot per lyric line: if a line has no clear visual, rewrite that shot before rendering.
future_use: Pacing and loudness checks for any rendered reel.

what_it_is: Four skills that turn a song and lyrics into a watercolour MV: storyboard, chapter painting, render and checks.
take: Before encoding, check total frames equal ceil(duration x fps); ffmpeg silently stops at the first missing frame.
Render a contact sheet at each chapter boundary (plus or minus 0.1 s) and at each wipe before any full render.
Make frame renders resumable: skip existing non-empty frames and write to a temp name, then rename.
future_use: Frame-count and resumable-render guard for any frame-based render.

what_it_is: Skill that animates glowing balls hopping along sheet-music note heads, synced to audio.
take: Sheet-music animation; nothing here transfers to talking-head reels.
General QA habit worth keeping: every event must match a source note by ID, with no silent deletes to pass validation.
future_use: Score-synced motion if a music-led piece is ever commissioned.

what_it_is: Two music videos made in code with Claude Opus 5.5: a Blender tabletop piece and a League montage.
take: Every frame is a pure function of song time, so parallel and resumed renders match previews exactly.
Treatment and plan are written before any code, then agents build one file per scene.
future_use: Planning-first workflow for multi-scene code-built films.

what_it_is: Turns a character still into a green-screen dance video cut to a generated beat, rendered to MP4.
take: Do not time-stretch or reverse AI dance to hit beats; it jerks. Keep native speed and put the beats on lights and camera.
Seam check: compare each join's frame change with a normal frame change, and flag joins far above normal as visible jumps.
Trim the last frames where the model pushes into a face close-up; detect that per frame and cut it.
future_use: Seam-ratio check for any generated B-roll joins.

what_it_is: Plugin that makes full music videos from a song: beat-grid analysis, performer clips, compositing and render.
take: Keep a history file of past videos and rejected directions; read it before choosing a look so later videos do not repeat.
Check archive footage rights before use and record the source for each clip.
Build the look from motifs in the brief, prototype each on a still sheet at its key moment, and drop what does not read.
future_use: Per-client history file to stop repeated looks across reels.

what_it_is: Chinese music-MV production workflow: first-frame gate, per-shot generation and pixel-level QA.
take: Gate each generated frame with numbers from a vision model: people count, share of frame, facing direction; not by eye.
Never let image or video models draw UI or write text; draw type and interface in code.
If the same failure returns after two fixes, change the design (fewer or smaller subjects) instead of re-rolling.
future_use: Numeric QA gate for AI B-roll before it enters a reel.

what_it_is: Music video with a riso-print look: halftone plates, misregistration on the downbeat, rendered in headless Chrome.
take: Riso look: four ink layers with halftone screens and a small misregistration pulse on the downbeat.
One still plate per lyric beat, then short image-to-video clips trimmed per clip, instead of generating whole scenes.
future_use: Print-texture style package for a graphic explainer.

what_it_is: Skill that remakes a music video as a synced Windows XP desktop recording, with cut-out people and code-drawn UI.
take: Fit beats to kick onsets on a half-beat grid; the project's test found librosa's raw tracker drifted about 50 ms.
Letterbox bars are often dark grey (about RGB 19), not black; use cropdetect with a limit near 44 and take the per-frame median.
Art-director subagents score each chapter in a fresh context; ship at average 8 with no item below 6, at most 3 rounds.
future_use: Beat-fit and crop-detect routines for reference-video remakes.

what_it_is: Research-song music video, plus explainer skills covering TTS narration, Manim scenes and QA.
take: Transcribe-back QA: run each voice clip through speech-to-text, word-diff against the script, and confirm with a second transcriber.
Preview at 480p with a contact sheet of frames at each beat's middle and end before any final render.
Keep a fact ledger: every number on screen must come from a model that was actually run, with provenance noted.
future_use: Voice-clip transcribe-back QA for narrated explainers.

what_it_is: Claude Code plugin that directs music videos and films in code, with objective render gates and frame scoring.
take: Hard gate: fail any render with no visible change for over 1.0 s, or with two luminance spikes less than 0.17 s apart (flicker).
Self-scores run about 10 points high; have a fresh subagent that never saw the code score stills on a 100-point rubric.
Route each scene to the lightest engine that holds the look, and print the cost before anything paid runs.
future_use: Freeze and flicker gates for every final render.

what_it_is: Claude Code workflow for films in code: sound-first clock, storyboard, look development, parallel build, reviews.
take: Let every shot conclude: hold at least 0.75 s after an action's payoff, 1 s after a punchline, and cut on completed actions.
Name the clock first: in a music video the song sets timing; in a narrative short, cut to the action and then score it.
Video-generation models stay off by default; use one only when the user approves that specific spend.
future_use: Hold-time rules for captions and end cards in any format.

what_it_is: Curated gallery of Claude Opus 5.5 videos, with links to original posts and prompts.
take: Gallery of finished pieces and links; the digest holds no reusable rule or number.
Useful only as a pointer to an original post when a specific style needs a reference.
future_use: Style reference links when a new look is needed for a non-face format.

what_it_is: Catalogue of Claude Opus 5.5 prompts in many languages, generated from a content system.
take: Prompt catalogue; the digest holds only translated index pages, with no tested prompt structure or numbers.
Nothing here changes FACE REELS practice; keep it only as a prompt-idea index.
